general_details.Description:
-Objective: To provides the basic knowledge about the berverage industry as well as the knowledge of the world beverage culture in operating the Restaurant - Bar.

-Description: This course is the continued part of RES213. This course focus on the beverage service of the Hospitality Industry including spirits, wines, beers and mixology beverages. Topics include purchasing, resource control, beverage storage and issuing, bar stocks and sales control, bar customer care, safety and security, managing bar wastage, the law and sale of liquor.

-Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, roleplay, project based learning, group work

- Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on  the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Manage and  correctly arrange sanitation standards and routines for the bar setup.
Present basic knowledge about tea and coffee beverages
Outline the history of Mixology.
Explain the Stirring, Shaking, Blending, and Building methods of drink mixing.
Identify and outline the types of jobs in the beverage industry.
Identify the functions and relations of the purchase order, the invoice, and the credit memo.
Identify the needs of targeting a clientele.
Create and use a workable business plan for a bar.
Develop a sense of good discipline, a sense of responsibility, and a sense of serious work in the assigned work as well as with colleagues.
Develop ability to work quietly; with cooperation; patience, carefulness, cleanliness and aesthetic values.

sessions.Student Materials:
Group assignment implementation 

Including: Presentation + Report + a practical video (optional)

Presentation:

For the 30-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates and lecturer with slides, a practical video and reports about your group project.   

Report:

To accomplish this group, you need to:

• Conduct a particular Mixology beverage (the Stirring, Shaking, Blending, and Building methods of drink mixing)

• Prepare and discuss information of the chosen alcoholic beverage: the brief history of Mixology, the physical layout of a bar and beverage operation regarding efficiency, cleanliness, and effective design, new drink recipes and create standardized recipe sheets for them, basic procedures of inventory management, purchasing, receiving, and storage of the beverage, how to serve the beverage…

• Have a group proposal (This is the mission done at group assignment)

• Writing a final report

• Reporting the whole group project at the end of semester

Include the following sections in your report:

PARTS OF FORMAL REPORTS 

1. Preliminary Section 

Title Page 

Table of Contents 

2. Body 

Introduction

Analysis 

Conclusions & Recommendations 

3. Supplementary Section 

Appendix (If any)

Reference List 

Based on chapter 10,11,13 of The Bar & Beverage Book textbook

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students'  preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Question Type:
Four or five students per group.

Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.
assessments.No Question: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Grading Guide: Group presentation in class room
assessments.Note:
All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 13-point font, and must be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission

Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (reccommded 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Grading Guide: Bar study room
assessments.Note:
Competency in this unit may be assessed through: Demonstration of skills on mixing different (in quantity) international alcoholic beverages in a prescribed timeframe; utilizing systematic liquor pouring and proper bar measurement; mixing of alcoholic concoction showmanship skill techniques.

The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Question Type: Each student must be assessed through practical demonstration in a simulated workplace environment where beverage ingredients and equipment are provided. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Grading Guide: Bar study room
assessments.Note:
Competency in this unit may be assessed through: 

- Observation shall be done on the proper classification of alcoholic beverages and glasses; proper mixing procedures on several cocktails and the uses and maintenance of different bar tools and equipment.

- Direct observation of student providing advice to customers or colleagues on cocktail and its proper serving procedures.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Grading Guide: Class room
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice .  Other types of questions may be included.

general_details.Description:
-This course introduces students to a professional studio experience where their goal is to create a 3D animated short film from scratch using Autodesk Maya. 



-Students will be responsible for all aspects of production, from developing their own original story, creating storyboards and concept art to finalizing textures, animation, character models, and lighting in a complete short film.

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Autodeks Maya, Film Editing Software (After Effects or Adobe Premiere)

clos.LO Details: Coming up with an idea that is suitable to create a short 3D animated.
Be able to organize and implement Digital art & design projects effectively.
Writing the script. Students will discover a lot when they translate the idea into written words.
Creating storyboard to pre-visualize the shorts.

Shoot live-action reference. It’s good practice to record 
yourself on video doing what your 3D character acts in your film.
Apply 3D skills such as Modeling, Texturing, Rigging to prepare ready characters for animation.
Apply animating workflow to animate the entire film.
Shading, lighting and rendering to establish the looks and feels of the film.
Adding sounds and editing sequences to create final film.
Students have a proficient in  presentation, teamworks and evaluation products. Having a positive attitude and a professional working style

general_details.Syllabus Name: Principles of Accounting_Nguyên lý kế toán
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Main objectives: 

Upon completion of this course, students should: 

1. Have clear understanding of  ideas, principles, and techniques of accounting 

2. Have the knowledge and tools to better understand business performance issues, and the decisions and problems faced by managers;

3. Understand the important role of accounting and finance in all organizations, in all jobs, and its link with the development of increasingly sophisticated IT systems.

Specific objectives : 

1. Recognize and organize accounting transactions

2. Classify and calculate correctly  in terms of revenue, cost, profit or loss in an account

3. Be able to prepare comprehensive and accurate financial statements 

4. Learn how to prepare comprehensive and realistic budget plans.

5. Have the ability to appraise the efficiency of the project 



Description:

The main content is structured into twelve chapters covering Financial Accounting, Management Accounting and Business Finance.

Topics include: business transaction, financial statement format and analysis,  inventory and account receivable, type of assets and liability, costing classification, master budget and capital budgeting

A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to answer constructivist questions while maintaining their critical thinking and originality.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Financial Statement Analysis_Phân tích báo cáo tài chính
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
The course provides a framework for interpretation, analysis and evaluation of financial statements from viewpoints of creditors, owners, investment firms and others. Thereby, the users of accounting information understand business strengths or weakness, the impact of general business and specific industry situations, behavior of financial markets, credit or lending criteria, and equity investment standards on present and future company financial conditions.

After completing the course, the student shall be able to:

- Be familiar with the organization and disclosure of reported information 

- Quantitatively and qualitatively evaluate core accounting issues that are particularly relevant in the context of financial statement analysis.

- Have a framework for forecasting future earnings and financial performance.

- Evaluate the business financial performance by applying quantitative and qualitative techniques.

- Use financial statement information in a modeling environment to identify and recommend solutions to a variety of financial challenges, and to recommend investment decisions.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class

- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material on the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Description:
-Main objective: The aim of this subject is to integrate knowledge with front office, housekeeping and others relevant departments in accommodation and apply them to problem solving in the areas of room division management. The course provides learners the necessary knowledge and skills to become a room division manager. 

-Description: During the course, students are practiced to design a room division department, apply the plan in real operation. Learners will be trained in management skills in  several key aspects of  room division management including operational administration, human resource management and departmental revenue optimization.

-Teaching method: Lecture, Desmontration, Role Play, Project based learning, Cooperative Learning

general_details.Time Allocation:

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description:

This course introduces students to the fundamentals of book design and printing technology. Students will learn about book anatomy, layout principles, typography, image integration, and basic binding techniques. Emphasis is placed on audience-centered design, effective visual communication, and hands-on experimentation with materials.

Objectives:

Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:

- Design comprehensive book layouts, including covers, interior pages, and structural elements.

- Select and apply appropriate typefaces, sizes, and visual elements to enhance readability and engagement.

- Integrate illustrations and hands-on application of materials effectively within book layouts.

- Demonstrate proficiency in basic bookbinding techniques.

- Adapt design choices to suit specific audiences and contexts.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submlit to the teacher 01 day after the course.

clos.LO Details: Apply the Fundamentals of book design: Understand the essential elements of book anatomy and design principles for effective layouts. Select appropriate typefaces, visual elements to effectively communicate content and engage different audiences.

Master Manual bookbinding techniques and Creative material use: Demonstrate proficiency in basic bookbinding methods (folding, stitching, gluing). Experiment with materials and techniques to achieve unique visual and tactile effects.

Explore Art book design concepts and Ideation: Analyze diverse examples of art books and their unique approaches. Develope creative concepts for book projects, considering form, content and audience engagement.

Conduct Design research and Project execution: Formulate research questions to guid the book design process. Design and execute the book project, demonstrating  conceptual thinking and technical skills.

Evaluate Design solutions and Adapt to context: Critically assess book designs, considering their suitability for cultural and technical contexts. Select and justify the use of manual and/or digital methods to achieve specific design goals.

Develop Professionalism and Collaborative skills: Exhibit a dedicated work ethic, attention to detail, and a willingness to experiment and refine designs. Contribute effectively to team projects and the ability to give and receive constructive feedback.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: In this course, students will learn to design and produce exhibitions for museums, galleries, libraries, private businesses, specialist trade events and conferences, and large commercial public events. …The focus of this course examines the role that exhibitions and events play in communicating knowledge and explores the variety of display methods within the language of exhibits.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submlit to the teacher 01 day after the course.

clos.LO Details: Understand the way people communicate visually and communication design organizes experience in variety of structures. Denotation and connotation are two levels of meaning we assign to messages.

Understand the concept of The ideal brief and the types of information that may be included. Describe and analyze The visitors and targeted audiences. Analyze The site: opportunities and constraints, their impact on design strategies.
Plan an exhibition strategy based on the brief. Devising a major path for visitors.
Describes how the exhibition strategy by sketches, models and computer visuals are then used to develop the final design plan
Using the right and appropriate graphic elements in each practical space. Ensure legibility of text and images on large-format printing and production issues
Apply interactive techniques, both digital and non-digital, can be used to stimulate visitor involvement in an exhibition.
Responsibility to use skills, positive attitude and a professional working style
Skills in proficient in presentation and teamwork skills.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Mobility Applications Design 1 _Thiết kế ứng dụng cho các thiết bị di động 1
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: This course aimed to provide students knowledge related to Interaction and UX Design in mobility world including smartphone devices and other wearable ones. In this course, student will be taught the common principles which dominates on mobile interface design in general. Specified principles corresponding three popular mobile platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows are going to be discussed, too. An agile for researching and designing Interaction and UX in mobility will also be introduced and applied through out this course. At the end of this course, student will obtain practical experience via a three phase projects in which they have to apply learned principles. A high fidelity prototype tools and paper prototype techniques will be explained in this course.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Follow instructions from teachers in class

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course

clos.LO Details: Discuss about common principles of interaction and UX design in mobility including smartphone and other wearable devices.
Identify and analyze about design principles specified for platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows Phone.
Understand how to conduct an Interaction and UX design research by following an agile process.
Apply the obtained knowledge to implement a research and designing process for a real product.
Develop Paper Prototype and High Fidelity Prototype for the application on InVisionApp
Design a product and conduct an evaluation process to measure usability, satistfactional and emotional of users
Perform improvement cycles to continous improve the design product

general_details.Syllabus Name: Brand Identity Design_Thiết kế nhận diện thương hiệu
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description:The objective of this course is to equip students with basic knowledge of Branding and Brand Identity Design: Basic theory of Branding in the digital age and artificial intelligence; Methods of market research and customer understanding; Process of brand building, operation and management of brand identity; Building appropriate brand promotion strategies.

Objectives: The course will prepare students with knowledge of the branding process and brand management. Skills in designing a brand identity system and managing this design system according to standards on many different media; The course will help students perfect a variety of skills in researching branding projects and applying research to problem solving; The course helps students understand the trends in brand identity design and choose the appropriate artistic direction.

Teaching method: Self-study of documents, Under the guidance of lecturers, Research and analysis of real projects, Practice of individual exercises combined with group exercises, students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to build and perfect a brand identity system.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Mobility Application Design_Thiết kế ứng dụng cho các thiết bị di động
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: Description: This course aims to provide students with knowledge related to Interaction and UX, Ui Design in the mobile world including smartphone devices and other wearable devices. In this course, students will be taught the common principles that prevail in mobile interface design in general. Specific guidelines corresponding to three popular mobile platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows will also be discussed. A nimble tool for Interaction and UX research and design, Ui in Mobility will also be introduced and applied through this course. At the end of this course, students will gain practical experience through a project that has phases: research, user segmentation, user persona, userflow, wireframe, Agile Project Management ..., in which they must apply principles have learned. This course will help students perfect the app.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: 'The purpose of this course is to equip students with the detailed understanding and knowledge of the package. It will also equip students with the essential practical and technical skills necessary for packaging design. Scope of evaluation will include target customers, brand language, personality and persuasion, concept creation, colour application, ergonomics, layout design, print finishing and materials... The challenges of designing for the future will also be considered; ensuring that environmental and ethical issues relating to the packaging industry are measured and applied.

clos.LO Details: Understanding the Fundamentals of packaging design: Combine the functional, aesthetic, and legal aspects of packaging

Analyze Materials, printing techniques, and market research: Merge the knowledge of materials and printing with market analysis skills. Evaluate packaging designs through a sustainability lens, considering material choices, life-cycle impact, and end-of-use strategies (recycling, composting, etc).
Develop Branding concepts and design: Focus on the brand creation process, including naming and visual design implementation
Research, Ideation and Collaborative design: Combine research, analysis, brainstorming, and teamwork for design development
Presentation and Communication skills: emphasize the importance of presenting and defending design choices, along with group collaboration.
Market Awareness and adaptability: highlight the need to understand market trends and adjust designs accordingly, building upon the proactive attitude from.
Professional Work ethic: reinforce the importance of working under pressure, adhering to legal requirements, and maintaining a proactive approach.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Google Ads and SEO - Google Ads và SEO
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course is designed to teach students to optimize website content for the best possible search engine ranking. Students will learn the theory behind Google search and other search engine algorithms, as well as build practical, real-world skills that can be applied to a career in digital marketing or online content development, including on-page and off-page optimization, optimizing for local and international audiences, conducting search-focused website audits, and aligning SEO with overall business strategies. Students will also learn how to create and execute search campaigns on Google Ads Search (formally AdWords). Through an introductory overview, students are guided through the official Google Ads Search training materials. Beyond Google materials, practical campaign creation and optimization best practices and exercises are provided to ensure the acquisition of practical skills and knowledge.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
general_details.Tools:
- Laptop computer

- Internet

- Class room for lecture sessions

general_details.Description: This course aims to provide student understanding on techniques, tools and skills to do a practical application design project. To study this course, student must have basic knowledge related to Interaction and UX Design, understanding principles and agile process applied in a mobile design project. In this course, student will perform a design project individually and have to work with programmer to transform an idea to a product. They will learn how to do from a research to design and implement an application project. They will learn about how to run a study of domain interested, how to make use-case list and draw flow diagram. They will be taught about the way to write a proposal for a project. In design phase, there are alot of things student must aware about, so they will be taught about them including rules, principles and good practices such as Realism, Fitts's Law, Animation, Speed and etc.. Testing techniques such as A/B Testing, Usability Testing will also be explained in this course. Student will be evaluated according to how his/her applied knowledge gained from this course to the course's project.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Follow instructions from teachers in class

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course

general_details.Description: This course provides an introduction to aesthetic and the phylosophy of arts for students and provides them with the knowledge and skills to communicate their ideas and processes in a visual form more effectively. As a means of questioning and applying fundamental theories, concepts and techniques, students conduct research and produce practical projects. The course examines the basic elements of visual communication and how context shapes visual forms production and reception.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 31,5h contact hours + 13,5h study on course (online) + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: This course provides students with fundamental knowledge of human body structure and proportions, as well as skills in drawing and sketching human figures. It is a foundational course for quick sketching and animation design. The course is offered in conjunction with Coursera's "Anatomy for the Character Design Artist". Throughout the course, students will learn about the history of anatomy, study the structure of the human body in motion, and learn how to draw the proportions of the head, shoulders and arms, legs and feet, and torso. Students will then apply these skills to practice drawing humans in various poses. Finally, students will be able to create character designs that maintain harmonious and visually pleasing human anatomy proportions.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook and references in advance

- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Students practices drawing. Lecturer evaluates and grades the student's drawings.
Scoring scale (10 points):
- Built up: create overall ratio of the object accurately. Ratio of every single object, part must be match with overall layout. Build up object's structure correctly without distortion. Draw bones and muscles structure correctly. (4 points) 
- Block and planes: create accurately fragments in accordance to the structure, suitable and appropriate values. (2 points)
- Demonstration: demonstrate values correctly in accordance to real space of objects, hence enable virtual space upon drawings. Though such demonstration, material and shade of objects are presented. (1 point)
- Technique: clear outline, good dark-bright and bold-light contrast, describe properties of objects (1 point) 
- Emphasis: emphasis object's details reasonably (1 point).
- Emotion: the drawing demonstrates feelings and aesthetic (1 point).
- Student gets 0.2 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.

general_details.Description: This course provides students with fundamental knowledge of human body structure and proportions, as well as skills in drawing and sketching human figures. It is a foundational course for quick sketching and animation design. The course is offered in conjunction with Coursera's "Anatomy for the Character Design Artist". Throughout the course, students will learn about the history of anatomy, study the structure of the human body in motion, and learn how to draw the proportions of the head, shoulders and arms, legs and feet, and torso. Students will then apply these skills to practice drawing humans in various poses. Finally, students will be able to create character designs that maintain harmonious and visually pleasing human anatomy proportions.

- Read the textbook and references in advance

- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

assessments.Question Type: practice
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledges on main-text, Slide, Teacher's Resource, Coursera. Module 2
assessments.Grading Guide:
Students practices drawing. Lecturer evaluates and grades the student's drawings.
Scoring scale (10 points):
- Built up: create overall ratio of the object accurately. Ratio of every single object, part must be match with overall layout. Build up object's structure correctly without distortion. Draw bones and muscles structure correctly. (4 points) 
- Block and planes: create accurately fragments in accordance to the structure, suitable and appropriate values. (2 points)
- Demonstration: demonstrate values correctly in accordance to real space of objects, hence enable virtual space upon drawings. Though such demonstration, material and shade of objects are presented. (1 point)
- Technique: clear outline, good dark-bright and bold-light contrast, describe properties of objects (1 point) 
- Emphasis: emphasis object's details reasonably (1 point).
- Emotion: the drawing demonstrates feelings and aesthetic (1 point).
- Student gets 0.2 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.

general_details.Syllabus Name: INFORMATION GRAPHIC DESIGN_Thiết kế đồ họa thông tin
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description:

The course equips students with the basics of graphic language used to visualize information, the methods and skills needed to create successful, outstanding and communicative infographic works to the audience. This course will also provides a series of accompanying exercises to reinforce the knowledge of visualizing information including a printed infographic artwork, a digital infographic artworks and a deconstruct wayfinding system of an existing place.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

 - Actively participate in class activities 

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

 - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

 - Read the textbook in advance 

 - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.
general_details.Tools:
- Internet access

- Microsoft Word

- Adobe Creative apps

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 50h online + 3h offline + 1h final exam + 96h self-study
general_details.Description: This six course specialization is designed to prepare you to take the certification examination for IBM AI Enterprise Workflow V1 Data Science Specialist. IBM AI Enterprise Workflow is a comprehensive, end-to-end process that enables data scientists to build AI solutions, starting with business priorities and working through to taking AI into production. The learning aims to elevate the skills of practicing data scientists by explicitly connecting business priorities to technical implementations, connecting machine learning to specialized AI use cases such as visual recognition and NLP, and connecting Python to IBM Cloud technologies. The videos, readings, and case studies in these courses are designed to guide you through your work as a data scientist at a hypothetical streaming media company. Throughout this specialization, the focus will be on the practice of data science in large, modern enterprises. You will be guided through the use of enterprise-class tools on the IBM Cloud, tools that you will use to create, deploy and test machine learning models. Your favorite open source tools, such as Jupyter notebooks and Python libraries will be used extensively for data preparation and building models.  Models will be deployed on the IBM Cloud using IBM Watson tooling that works seamlessly with open source tools.

general_details.Description:
This specialization is designed for those with little or no background in AI, whether you have technology background or not, and does not require any programming skills. It is designed to give you a firm understanding of what is AI, its applications and use cases across various industries. Students will become acquainted with terms like Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Neural Networks. 



Furthermore, it will familiarize you with IBM Watson AI services that enable any business to quickly and easily employ pre-built AI smarts to their products and solutions. Students will also learn about creating intelligent virtual assistants and how they can be leveraged in different scenarios.



 By the end of this specialization, learners will have had hands-on interactions with several AI environments and applications, and have built and deployed an AI enabled chatbot on a website – without any coding. 



Learners will perform several no-code hands-on exercises in each of the  three courses. At the end of the last course, learners would have developed,  tested, and deployed a Watson AI powered customer service chatbot on a website to delight their clients.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Machine Learning_Học máy
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Machine learning is the science of getting computers to act without being explicitly programmed. In the past decade, machine learning has given us self-driving cars, practical speech recognition, effective web search, and a vastly improved understanding of the human genome. Machine learning is so pervasive today that you probably use it dozens of times a day without knowing it. Many researchers also think it is the best way to make progress towards human-level AI.



This course provides a broad introduction to machine learning, datamining, and statistical pattern recognition. Topics include: (i) Supervised learning (parametric/non-parametric algorithms, support vector machines, kernels, neural networks). (ii) Unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction, recommender systems, deep learning). (iii) Best practices in machine learning (bias/variance theory; innovation process in machine learning and AI). The course will also draw from numerous case studies and applications, so that you'll also learn how to apply learning algorithms to building smart robots (perception, control), text understanding (web search, anti-spam), computer vision, medical informatics, audio, database mining, and other areas.



This course will be implemented through online mode. Students will learn officially the online course "Machine Learning" on Coursera. During the online learning process, students will be guided by teachers-tutors through some offline sessions on the campus, and through emails

LO1.1. Demonstrate a deep understanding about linear regression model with one variable. 
LO1.2. Understand and calculate the cost function and gradient descent method for Linear regression with one variable.
Demonstrate an understanding about the idea and intuitions behind Support Vector Machines (SVM), for classification and being able to use it in practice.
Demonstrate a understanding about the k-Means algorithm for clustering unlabeled data points.
Demonstrate a deep understanding about Principal Components Analysis, and use it for data compression to speed up learning algorithms as well as for visualizations of complex datasets.
Be able to model a dataset using a Gaussian distribution, and use this model for anomaly detection.
Be able to perfom the recommender algorithms such as the collaborative filtering algorithm and low-rank matrix factorization.
Apply the machine learning algorithms with large datasets.
Master online studying skill and be ready for life long learning.
Be able to implement the learning algorithms in practice using Octave or MATLAB

Obtain a deep knowledge about linear regression model with multiple variables:
LO3.1. Demonstrate a deep understanding about linear regression model with multiple variables. 
LO3.2. Understand and calculate the cost function and gradient descent method for Linear regression with multiple variables.
Being able to classify data into discrete outcomes using logistic regression method. Apply cost function for Logistic regression
Being able to prevent models from overfitting the training data by using regularization.
Demonstrate an understanding about neural networks: what neural networks are, what representations of neural network models.
Demonstrate an understanding about the backpropagation algorithm for training neural networks.
Being able to evaluate performance of the learned models
Demonstrate a understanding about the performance of a machine learning system with multiple parts, and being able to deal with skewed data.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Machine Learning_Học máy
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: The course provides an introduction to Exploratory Data Analysis for Machine Learning (common techniques to retrieve your data, clean it, apply feature engineering, and have it ready for preliminary analysis and hypothesis testing), Supervised Machine Learning (how to train models to predict outcomes and how to use error metrics to compare across different supervised models), , Unsupervised Machine Learning (how to find insights from data sets that do not have a target or labeled variable. Learners will learn several clustering and dimension reduction algorithms for unsupervised learning as well as how to select the algorithm that best suits your data).
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU LMS at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

clos.LO Details: Learners should be able to use common techniques to retrieve data from multiple data sources: SQL, NoSQL databases, APIs, Cloud
Implement a mini capstone ML project includes steps: data collection, data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, model development, model evaluation, and reporting
Learners should be able to describe and use common feature selection and feature engineering techniques
Learners should be able to use a variety of techniques for detecting and dealing with outliers
Learners should be able to describe and use supervised models
Learners should be able to use a variety of error metrics to compare and select a supervised model that best suits your data
Learners should be able to use oversampling and undersampling as techniques to handle unbalanced classes in a data
Learners should be able to explain the kinds of problems suitable for Unsupervised Learning approaches
Explain the curse of dimensionality, and how it makes clustering difficult with many features
Learners should be able to describe and use common clustering and dimensionality-reduction algorithms

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
The initial course for students to become familiar with AI problems. Through sample tutorials, students can understand the practical application of AI, how to perform step-by-step, the knowledge to equip the field of AI (computer vision, natural language processing, data science, robotics..). 

The Project provides students, working in groups, with a significant project experience in which they can integrate much of the material they have learned in their program, including matters relating to introduction, design, human factors, professionalism, and project management. 

Students will be guided to develop a software system, employing knowledge gained from courses throughout the program.
general_details.StudentTasks:
# Choose appropriate project and form group.

# Divide and schedule work among members.

# Produce document and product according to project requirement and member work share.

# Defend work infront of examination board, showing both project results and individual responsibility.

It enables students to further apply their knowledge and skills which they have found especially interesting or beneficial to them.



As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the capstone project and gain an understanding of standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This capstone project will be completed by a group of 2-3 students.  Students will be supported by a supervisor, who will provide them with essential guidance in conducting a research, designing & implementing the product, writing the dissertation in formal format and defending their arguments in front of the examination board.

general_details.Description:
The AI Capstone Project course is an integrative experience that consolidates the knowledge and skills acquired from the undergraduate AI curriculum into a practical, real-world application. The design of this course challenges students to apply their analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills to solve complex problems using AI technologies.

Throughout this course, students will engage with all facets of the AI project development lifecycle, including problem identification, data collection and preprocessing, model design and implementation, evaluation, and deployment. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the professional standards and expectations required to successfully execute a project of this nature.

This course is structured to be completed by small groups of 3-4 students, fostering collaboration and teamwork. Each group will be assigned a supervisor, who will offer critical support and guidance throughout the research and development process. The supervisor will assist students in refining their project ideas, conducting thorough research, developing and implementing AI solutions, composing a report on their capstone project, and preparing for the final presentation in front of the examination board.

By the end of the course, students will have not only deepened their understanding of AI principles and techniques but also demonstrated their ability to apply these concepts effectively in a team-based project. This capstone project not only serves as a significant portfolio piece but also prepares students for professional careers in the field of artificial intelligence.
general_details.StudentTasks:
(1) Select a project within the chosen AI concentration: Teams should choose a project that aligns with their interests and the scope of the AI concentration. This may involve identifying a real-world problem that can be addressed with AI solutions.
(2) Divide and schedule work: Once the project is chosen, teams should allocate tasks among members based on each individual's strengths and skills. A detailed schedule should be created, outlining milestones and deadlines to ensure timely progress.
(3) Attend all scheduled meetings with supervisor: Teams must commit to regular meetings with their assigned supervisor. These sessions are crucial for receiving guidance, discussing progress, resolving any issues, and making necessary adjustments to the project plan.
(4) Produce document and product according to project requirements: Teams are expected to produce comprehensive documentation and develop the AI product according to the specified requirements. This includes but is not limited to, designing algorithms, coding, testing, and validating the AI model(s). Documentation should detail the problem, methodology, implementation, results, and conclusions.
(5) Present and defend individual contributions in front of the examination board: Each team member must be prepared to present and individually defend their specific contributions to the project in front of the examination board. This includes explaining the rationale behind their approach, the challenges faced, and the solutions implemented.

general_details.Syllabus Name: AI with Tensorflow_AI với Tensorflow
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
The developing of cloud computing, big data, open source software, and improved algorithms kicked Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the mainstream of focus in technologies nowadays. AI technologies are fundamentally changing the ways we work, live, and manage businesses. This course is designed to present to student the coherent body of ideas and methods which were contributed to the development of Artificial Intelligence discipline. Student will be acquaint with the basic programs in the field and their underlying theory and will explore this through problem-solving paradigms, logic and theorem proving, language and image understanding, search and control methods and learning. This course aims to create following results on students:



1. Graduates will have ability to work with Tensor Flow machine learning library as a framework in developing AI their applications

   MO-1a: An ability to build models by plugging together building blocks with the user-friendly Keras sequential API.

   MO-1b: An ability to build models then write the forward and backward pass, create custom layers, activations, and training loops by using a define-by-run interface for customization and advanced research from Keras functional and subclassing APIs.

2. Graduates will have a broad understanding of the fundamental theories, concepts, and applications of Artificial Intelligence.

   MO-2a: An ability to apply knowledge of Artificial Intelligence appropriate to the discipline.

   MO-2b: An ability to analyze a problem and identify and define the AI requirements appropriate to its solution.

   MO-2c: An ability to design, implement, and evaluate an AI system to meet desired needs.

3. Graduates will be prepared for careers in Artificial Intelligence field.

   MO-3a: An ability to use current methodologies, techniques, skills, and tools necessary for AI practice. 

4. Graduates will communicate effectively, both orally and in writing of Artificial Intelligence-related works.

   MO-4a: An ability to communicate effectively in AI-related works.

   MO-4b: An ability to discuss about how to control and to manage APIs of Tensor Flow library effectively.

general_details.Syllabus Name: 3D Character Animation_Tạo chuyển động trong môi trường 3D
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite: Passed (ANR401 or ANR402) or passed (AMR401 or AMR402)
general_details.Description: This course covers character rigging and animation in Maya. Students will learn to rig characters, animate with keyframe techniques, analyze body language and expressions and apply animation principles for realistic motion. They will be able to create and render a short animation scene using Maya and compositing software while also developing a positive and professional working style.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

 - Actively participate in class activities 

 - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

 - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes.

 - Read the textbook in advance 

 - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information.

general_details.Description: This course focuses on the standards for TV and features. Students will first study backgrounds and will gain the technical knowledge needed to create them. Students will then make thumb- nail paintings and continue on to finished paintings, including large pan scenes.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook and references in advance

- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment. 

- Computer with some version of photograph editing software such as Ps, Ai, Ae, Pr 

- Have papers, Pencils, scissors...

- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course

clos.LO Details: Students understand the role of backgrounds, the process of building the background in 2D animation.
Understand the foreground and background in a scene.
Know the camera movements to separate objects from backgrounds.
Analyzes the storyboard to find out the number of backgrounds needed for each movie.
Splitting layers of each scene and arranging them from back to front.
Choosing right colors for each layer according to the content.
Setup camera movements and position the layers based on the storyboard.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Character Design_Thiết kế nhân vật
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: This course focuses on the complete process of character design for animated films, from creating rough representations based on research to executing full designs with color, turnaround sheets, facial expressions and action poses. Students will analyze characters, evaluate designs for improvement, and apply their knowledge to create character sets for 2D animations, while developing teamwork, self-study, and professional skills. The final outcome of the course is a product in digital format.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities 

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Read the textbook in advance >

- Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

materials_table.Author: 3dtotal Publishing

materials_table.MaterialDescription: The Silver Way: Techniques, Tips, and Tutorials for Effective Character Design
materials_table.Author: Stephen Silver

clos.LO Details: Understand and memorize the basic knowledge of animation character design, Key design principles, and the character construction process.
Analyze characters based on plot, script, and character descriptions.
Create rough representations based on character research.
Carry out a complete character design, including cleanup, color, turnaround sheet, facial expressions, and action poses.
Check and evaluate character designs, identifying areas for improvement.
Create a character set for a 2D animated movie by applying learned knowledge to design.
Demonstrate teamwork skills, develop self-study abilities, and apply professional attitudes in a working environment.

general_details.Time Allocation: 30 slots (1 slot = 90 minutes)
general_details.Description:
This course will prepare you:

This course covers the fundamentals of working in CG (Computer Graphic) with Maya. It’s only a starting point, though. As with any artistic pursuit, CG is a lifelong process of learning. With what you learn in this course forming a solid foundation, you can continue exploring all the complex, interesting facets of creating CG imagery

Teaching methods:

- Student is the center, practice combined with theory

- Help students have a self-study method

- Presentation method combined with group working method

- Teachers are instructors, organizing activities

- The result is a combination of teacher and student evaluation

general_details.Description:
This course covers the fundamentals of creating 3D character UVs, creating textures with Substance Painter, and working with lighting and rendering. Substance Painter is clearly a very powerful texture drawing software. It helps 3D Artists to draw textures in a simpler & more intuitive way based on the available intelligent material inventory

Mastering this software also helps 3D Artist understand the properties of each material, thereby easily combining with other 3D software.

general_details.Description: This Specialization lays a primary foundation for experimentation and exploration of video game design, story, character development, and winning gameplay before programming begins. These four courses emphasize the self-reliance and personal expression of the gaming artist, and encourage you to take conceptual risks and develop new modes of expression and form through gaming. In the final Capstone Project, you’ll put your creative skills to work by generating an engaging game design document for a personal game project, outlining the conceptual, narrative and aesthetic elements of your game.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assignments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus
general_details.Note:
1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

general_details.Description:
'Description:

   This course is designed to enable students to write scripts for short movie or TVC based on an idea or a literature work.

The students can understand the principles and structure to develop a script. Through a series of instruction sessions, work analysis and personal exercises, after the course, students can write comprehensive scripts for short movies or TV by themselves.

Objective: 

· Understand the concept of scripts for short movies and TVC

· Construct a script in the standard format.

· Analyze and understand structure of the scripts for short movies and TVC.

· Develop the character arches and their worldviews.

· Develop a comprehensive script based on an idea or a literature work.

· Understand steps to build up idea for an effective TVC. 



Teaching method:

Under lecturer’s instruction, through a series of instruction sessions, work analysis and personal exercises, students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to develop and complete a comprehensive script for short movies and TVC based on an idea or a literature work.

general_details.Description: This course focuses on animation and illustrative storytelling. Topics include structural elements of storytelling, storyboarding formats, motion and animation and character development. The course will take a step-by-step approach to story development, using the medium of storyboards. The creation and use of animat- ics will also be introduced and explored.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Introduction to Automotive System_Nhập môn ôtô
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course equips students with knowledge about car structures, including knowledge related to the structure and operating principles of cars. This knowledge will help students understand cars and be helpful in their future work in programming car systems. The module content also introduces software applications in the automotive industry. In addition, the module also equips students with career orientation, soft skills as well as professional ethical foundation, customer care and initial experiences with cars.
general_details.StudentTasks:
Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Constantly follow announcements on LMS at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information regarding assignment submission and feedback on assignments and project work.

clos.LO Details: Understand the basic structures of vehicles (explain the basic components and functions of the main systems in vehicles).
Describe in detail the structure and operating principles of the main systems
Understand the global electric vehicle market and development trends
Understand and describe the role of software applications in the automotive industry
Be able to simulate basic vehicle systems and evaluate performance metrics
Understand and apply legal standards and requirements related to automobiles
Be able to develop essential soft skills, including teamwork, communication, and problem-solving

general_details.Description: This Specialization aims to make branding concepts accessible to every learner and to teach them to analyze and apply all the relevant concepts, using the broad and diverse toolkit of branding.  It provides you with the necessary tools so that you are able to understand the brand behavior, understand the language of a brand and learn about the rational and emotional elements behind brands.  It also attempts to make you understand the language of images. The amount of audiovisual content we receive today makes it hard for brands to break through that noise. It ends up teaching how to understand branding efforts in the context of customer experience.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Brand Identity Design_Thiết kế nhận diện thương hiệu
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description: 'The aim of this course is to equip students with the basic knowledge of Brand Identity Design: Brand basics (what is brand, brand identity, branding; brand strategy...), Brand ideals (flexibility,value, differentiation, sustainability…), Brand elements (brandmarks, wordmarks, symbol, characters…), Brand dynamics (Social media, Mobile, …; Private labeling, Brand licensing, Certification…); Brand identity design (Logotype + signature, Color, Typography, Trial applications, Presentation…), Brand book (Standards + guidelines..), (Managing, Measuring, Decision making, Intellectual property, Design management...)

Objectives: 

'- The Branding & Identity Design course will prepare students to design and establish visual identities and brand standards across a variety of mediums. The course will help the student look beyond logo design and acquire a fundamental understanding of the aspects of designing a brand system that is scalable and replicable, regardless of application

'- Throughout this course, emphasis will be placed on the use of logo, including its use as a valuable analytical tool for the visual communication professions.

Teaching method:

Under lecturer’s instruction, through a series of instruction sessions, researchanalysis and personal exercises, students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to develop and complete a brand identity system

general_details.Syllabus Name: BUSINESS DECISION MAKING
general_details.Time Allocation: Contact time: 30 sessions; 1 session = 90'
general_details.Description:
In business, good decision making requires the effective use of information. This unit gives learners the opportunity to examine a variety of sources and develop techniques in relation to four aspects of information: data gathering, data storage, and the tools available to create and present useful information. Specifically, learners will use spreadsheets and other software for data analysis and the preparation of information. The use of spreadsheets to manipulate of numbers, and understanding how to apply the results, are seen as more important than the mathematical derivation of formulae used.

Learners wil lgain an appreciation of information systems currently used at all levels in an organisation as aids to decision making.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.lms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Description: This course is designed to develop knowledge, skills, and perspectives to support the application of managing products and developing brand strategies in the marketing area. It helps students to gain insights into the role of product and brand management in gaining and maintaining customer loyalty.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities 

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Read the textbook in advance

assessments.Grading Guide:
Option1: Report + Presentation

Task Description:

Students will work in groups of 4 or 5 and immerse themselves in an extensive analysis of a specific brand as well as the company that owns it.  As this is an extensive analysis, it will involve qualitative and quantitative research, and literature/market/industry review. Students are encouraged to select a brand for which public information is readily available. 

Brand managers, research managers and C-level executives are supposed to be the target audience for the brand audit report. Accordingly, the report should have multiple components including Brand History and Overview, Key Challenges Facing Brand, Brand Inventory, Brand Exploratory and maybe, Brand Resonance Pyramid. 

Presentation:

For the 20-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates to help them gain insights into the brand you have chosen. 

Report: Include the following sections in your report

1. Brand History and Overview 

Summarize the evolution of the brand, including its past and present positioning.

2.Key Challenges Facing Brand 

Explain the key challenges facing the brand and lay the foundation for the brand audit focus and outcomes.

3. Brand Inventory: Brief description/summary of each item 

4. Brand Exploratory: Focus Group Insights

 5. Reflections and Recommendations  

Generate marketing recommendations that address specific branding issues.

6. Appendices 

Notes: The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

Each student will need to conduct at least one interview/survey (choice of person interviewed to be approved by the instructor) and include the full transcript of the interview in the annex section of the report.

An example of a completed brand audit appears in the textbook.

Task Description:

Based on their Brand Audit, students will continue working with their teammates again to create one brand campaign in order to address brand’s challenges and embrace brand image. The brand campaign should follow brand voice guidelines and is able to highlight thoroughly the brand personality of the organization. For this assessment, students will practise with and apply the brand strategy model and methods to a real world brand of your choosing. Students will learn the difference between brand campaign strategies and other types of campaign strategies. 

Presentation:

For the 20-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates.Your presentation should showcase how we are able to increase brand awareness and brand equity by using the right strategies, content and media platforms.

Report:

Students will apply all of the knowledge they have gained so far to create a simulated campaign again with the purpose of enhancing brand awareness and brand equity. 

The structure of the report will be revealed and modified during the class based on the brands the studens choose to focus on.

'- Objective: The course aims to provide students a solid foundation on different aspects of advertising and other major integrated marketing communications tools, and the role of these tools in the marketing process.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
- This course satisfies the Graphic Design Faculty component of FPT University. Students will engage with technical, practical, and concept based problems involved with the practice of watercolor painting.  Color theory, techniques, materials, and application will be explored throughout the term.  Projects will include painting from the still life, model, landscape and images. 



- This course presents students with the basic techniques and concepts that are common to various painting media, with the emphasis placed on the watercolor medium. students in watercolor course will be exposed to both subjectively and technically. This course will also examine the interdependence of medium and image. Further more the course will provide basic knowledge of color application in visual design.



- This course will be organized in a studio. During class time, practice exercises will come right after each of theories. Students create art works after lectures and tutorials. These art works will be analyzed and evaluated by students under the control of lecturer. Finally, they will be graded by the lecturer.



- Students collect all of their art works to make the portfolios.

general_details.Tools:
MATERIALS TO CLASS

Paper:

 - 2 pads of Newsprint 1 pad of multi use drawing paper, watercolor paper!

A few sheets of high quality paper for some projects, Sketch book

 - To start: 5 sheets of Arches 140 lb. (or 300lb) Cold pressed Watercolor paper (22x30 inches)

 - Note that you will need to get additional paper as the term progresses. 



 Additional Supplies:

 - Erasers.  Both Plastic and Kneaded

 - Palette: Something with a white base is best and with space for colors and adequate mixing area

 - Water container

 - Sponge

 - Towel

 - Drawing Board: Something big enough for A3  paper 

 - Roll of masking tape.

 - Graphite pencils, 3B, 4B, 6B

 - Two jars for water storage

 - One watercolor palette

  - Watercolor sticks

 - Tool chest for carrying materials 

 -  Portfolio (paper is fine.  It is fine if you want to make one out of cardboard or other stiff material.)  Minimum 26 x 34 inches



Brushes:

 - #6, #12 Round (Sable)

 - 1” or larger flat brush

 - Inexpensive round brush that can be used for masking fluid (be sure that it comes to a tip for detailing)

 - Brushe Fibers: Sable, Squrrel, Ox, Goat, Sabeline, Synthetics,Blends

Brushe Styles: Rounds, Flats, Brichts, Filbets, Oval Mops, Scripts and Riccers, Bamboo, Hake, Large Wash Brushs, Retractable Brushes

clos.LO Details: Define and identify basic concepts
Understand Cultural Influences on different Communication Contexts including business, education and health care context; the challenges of intercultural comminucation.
Understand the relationship between Communication and Culture and their elements;
Recognize the Deep Structure of Culture: Lessons from the Family;
Understand Cultural History of different countries/ religions;
Understand the Cultural Explanations of Life and Death; concepts related religions and some popular religions in the world;
Identify Cultural Values and apply some Guidelines for Behavior
Understand the concepts and relationship between culture and identity;
Deepy understand and apply verbal language in communication;
Deepy understand and apply non-verbal language in communication;

Crisis Management Plan (In the class)

Type: Crisis Group Project

Weight: 35%

Including: Presentation (15%) + Report (20%)

Task Description:

Students working within a small group setting of maximum 4 students should select one crisis accepted by the lecturer. Each team will be asked to complete a crisis management plan to address this crisis. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, including: the three-stage approach, the proactive management functions and the crisis communication system. Students will deliver a final report with their plan to their “organisation” and deliver a 30-minute presentation on its highlights to their “partners” as well as their "organisation's representatives". 

The crisis communication plan should contain sections which include:

1. Organizational history

2. Risk assessment

3. Strategic communication action plan

4. Evaluation

5. Crisis appendix

Notes: 

Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

Task Description:

For this assignment, you will choose an organisation and identify some of its key issues and stakeholder groups.  You will investigate how the issues may impact, or have the potential to impact, on the organisation’s relationship management and public image. 

For this, you will need to examine a range of sources including organisational documents (e.g. annual reports, website), media (e.g. news coverage and social media platforms) and academic literature (e.g. journal articles and books).

Based on your research you will write a 2000-word report which includes key recommendations for the organisation that you have analysed.

The lecturer, through class discussion, is expected to answer student's questions about what they are not sure. The lecturer will summarise the key points and emphasize what students have to keep in mind while writng this report.

Throughout that, students will be equipped with practical experience and skills to be ready for their future career path in the communications field.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Individual Assessment (At home)
Type: Essay
Weight: 15%
Length: 2,000 words
Task Description:
Choose from the list of crisis case studies provided by the lecturer before and analyse one organisational crisis.
Your essay will include an overview of the crisis, a description of the organisation, a crisis timeline, actions and responses taken, a media analysis, stakeholder impacts, lessons learned, recommendations, and use appropriate matrix/models. 
The essay should address the criteria as outlined in the assessment task and rubric mentioned during the class. 
Studens should use a mix of scholarly references, media coverage and organisational materials.
Based on student's performance

assessments.Question Type: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to make one crisis communication plan
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1-8, with an emphasis on Chapter 2-5)
assessments.Grading Guide:
Group Assessment
Type: Crisis Communication Plan (At Home) + Presentation (In the class)
Weight: 25%
Task Description:
Students working within a small group setting of 4-6 students to select one organisation in Vietnam, which must be accepted by the lecturer, then propose a crisis communication plan for that organisation. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, and be delivered as a final report to their chosen organisation.
AI Application (maximum of 10% of this assessment's grade): Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing templates in the crisis communication plan, which include (but aren't limited to) prewritten news release(s) and media alert. 

Presentation: For the 15-minute presentation, each group have to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates.

Notes: 
The detailed structure of a crisis communication plan could be found in the textbook (P98, ebook)
Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
assessments.Note: The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Group Assessment
Type: Simulated Media Conference (In the class)
Weight: 20%

Based on your crisis communication plan, each group will prepare for a media conference based on the scenario which will respond to a simulated crisis of your chosen organisation. Your media statement should be no more than 15 minutes in total and will be followed by a 15-minute Q&A from the “journalist” members of the class.
Before the media conference, your group have to prepare:
1. a media alert
2. a media kit, including the press release (to be delivered at the conference)
3. a one-page summary of key message

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to corporate communications and public relations: it is for anyone with an interest in corporate communication, or anyone seeking to understand the growing importance of communication for corporations. Corporations increasingly need communication to survive, as they need to entertain relations with a variety of stakeholders to prosper. This includes not only external factors to the organization – customers, governments and civil ociety organizations, but also stakeholders within corporations themselves, such as employees, managers and investors.



The first weeks of the course focus on the basics of corporate communication: what is it, and what are its historical roots? This is important, as it demonstrates how the position of communication is increasingly considered to be managerial function – and as such should be involved in the key decision-making processes. After these introductory weeks, we turn to two core theories of corporate communication: stakeholder theory and corporate identity. These form the basis for much of the more specific and applied topics covered in the following weeks. In the last two weeks before the midterm exam, we discuss how corporations can construct communication campaigns – which will be useful as you will be tasked with creating your own communication campaign during the course. After the midterm exam, we tackle specific topics of corporate communication, such as employee communications, how corporations interact with media and journalists, and how corporations should communicate in times of crisis.
