clos.LO Details: Use different reading strategies for different tasks, identify what critical reading is (and what it is not);  understand the importance of critical reading skill; make questions and find answers as you read critically; differentiate between critical reading and other reading strategies; Develop and integrate criticality into reading practices.
Analyze the key components of a critical review; differentiate between a critical review and a research essay; structure a critical review

Evaluate whether or not a text is academic; describe the peer-review process works; evaluate why peer-reviewed texts are preferable for academic study; understand the importance of the publication date of a text
Analyze the importance of knowing something about the author of a text and the people quoted by the author;  recognize and reason bias
Identify the author’s stance; how the author’s intended audience influences the text; why the author’s purpose is important
Distinguish facts from opinions
Evaluate conclusions drawn from author experience; recognize the steps of the scientific method; evaluate important information as reading reports of empirical research

Identify and evaluate evidence not based on author experience: anecdotes, visual items, statistics and quotations from others; how authors try to persuade readers using no evidence at all; how to evaluate these kinds of evidence

Analyze the importance of considering the text in its broader context; recognize a school of thought and understand the importance of knowing the schools of thought in your area of study; how to approach a text that presents an opinion or theory very different from anything else you have read
Explain why it is important to ask yourself whether the text supports your own experiences; why it can be difficult to do this

general_details.Syllabus Name: Electronic Circuits_Kỹ thuật mạch
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course equips students with comprehensive knowledge of electronic circuits, starting from the fundamentals of semiconductor materials and advancing to the design and analysis of amplifier, operational amplifier (Op-Amp), and signal conversion circuits. It covers essential topics including diodes, Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs), Field-Effect Transistors (FETs), analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion, and the operation of timer circuits, with practical applications in circuit design. Through a combination of theoretical foundations and hands-on practice, students will develop skills to analyze circuit behavior, design efficient electronic systems, and utilize simulation software for modeling and testing. The course also emphasizes safety, professional ethics, and environmental considerations in electronic design.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 
- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

materials_table.Author: Adel S. Sedra; Kenneth C. Smith

clos.LO Details: Understand the properties and characteristics of semiconductor materials and diodes, and apply diodes in practical circuit designs.
Explain the operation of Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs) and design and analyze BJT amplifier circuits.
Describe the operation of Field-Effect Transistors (FETs) and analyze their biasing configurations.
Investigate the functionality of operational amplifiers (Op-Amps) and design practical Op-Amp circuits for various applications.
Utilize simulation software to model, simulate, and analyze electronic circuits effectively.
Demonstrate proficiency in constructing and testing electronic circuits, while applying safety practices and responsibility in laboratory settings.
Integrate professional ethics, social responsibility, and environmental considerations into the selection, design, and lifecycle management of electronic components.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Interpretation 1_Phiên dịch 1
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 0.5 hour final exam + 104.5 hours self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite:
Passed ENW401 or (ENS412 & ENS422) or ENT503
K15 onward: Passed EAL201 & SSC302c & LTG202
general_details.Description: This introductory course provides an instructional manual to equip students with a theoretical basis for, and essential skills in, Interpretation. Two common types are put into focus; Consecutive Interpreting and Simultaneous Interpreting. The objective is to train students to be capable of interpreting in various fields and settings.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by the teacher after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

materials_table.Author: Aline Ferreira (Editor) & John W. Schwieter (Editor)

clos.LO Details: Explain the correlation between a good public speaker and an interpreter.
Organize, select and develop interpreting skills in various fields and settings.
Recognize the preparation stage and the attitute to overcome several problems that may occur during the actual interpreting setting.
Develop a personal note-taking technique.
Use several strategies to help cope with the combined difficulty of complexity and speed.
Identify units of meaning in the speech and recognize the importance of two kinds of clusters.
Use general adverbial clauses in various proper ways.
Translate the importance of identifying figures of speech and technical measurement to convey the meaning.
Use several strategies to cope with quotations, allusions, and transposition.
Understand the value of teamwork skills and attitudes in interpretation.

clos.LO Details: Explain the correlation between a good public speaker and an interpreter.
Organize, select and develop interpreting skills in various fields and settings.
Recognize the preparation stage and the attitute to overcome several problems that may occur during the actual interpreting setting.
Develop a personal note-taking technique.
Use several strategies to help cope with the combined difficulty of complexity and speed.
Identify units of meaning in the speech and recognize the importance of two kinds of clusters.
Use general adverbial clauses in various proper ways.
Translate the importance of identifying figures of speech and technical measurement to convey the meaning.
Use several strategies to cope with quotations, allusions, and transposition.
Understand the value of teamwork skills and attitudes in interpretation.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to interpreting in a business setting.
assessments.Grading Guide: Location/Procedure of teacher's choice
assessments.Note: Teacher is asked to write a field trip proposal with specific details and send it to the person in charge; or organize a project that facilitates the subject.

assessments.Question Type: Pair work
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 1-3) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.Grading Guide: In-class test
assessments.Note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.Question Type: pair work
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 4-6) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.Note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 7-9) to simultaneous interpreting.
assessments.Note: The teacher shall prepare 5-6 audio files (≈2minutes/file) relating to several specific topics, of which the students will be informed in advance. On the test day, students will be divided into groups of 4 or 5. All members will be standing at different positions in class, simultaneously listening to the same audio and recording their interpretation using a smartphone. Upon completion, students are asked to send the record to the teacher immediately.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to consecutive interpreting (both ENG-VIE and VIE-ENG processes). Topics: 1. Education 2. Entertainment 3. Technology 4. Environment/Nature 5. Business, Economics and Finance 6. Tourism 7. Family and Friends 8. Health 9. Culture 10. Arts
assessments.Grading Guide: Exam room
assessments.Note:
The length of one audio is 220-250 words.

Students take the exam individually. Students will randomly pick 2 topics to interpret. Students will listen to one audio in English for E-V interpretation, and listen to audio or the examiners reading a text in Vietnamese for the V-E process. 

Students are allowed to take notes in the exam room.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Phiên dịch tiếng Anh 2
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 0.5 hour final exam + 104.5 hours self-study
general_details.Description: This course is designed to supplement Interpretation 1 through offering more advanced theoretical approaches to interpretation, ensuring an advanced understanding of professional interpreting practice. By providing a guidance in developing sufficient background knowledge in subject areas for interpreting, students are expected to be equipped with experience of dealing with problems in interpreting at the advanced level, being capable of working in various interpreting settings.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by the teacher after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

clos.LO Details: Identify the issue that some meanings could not be brought out totally and how to improvise by using equivalents.
Deeply and broadly understand the principles of advanced interpretation, and master interpreting skills used for various fields and settings.
Understand the role of logic and emotion when argueing and the professionalism of interpreters when interpreting arguments.
Understand the importance of word choice and how to handle shades of language.
Understand the strategies to interprete in formal situations with a proper consideration to balance the language richness.
Identify the challenges posed by the interpretation of policy address.
Have a well-developed political and/or economic knowledge in order to successfully convey the meaning of related problems.
Identitfy challenges when conveying the concept of humour.
Understand how to deal with tasks that involve the use of Latin.
Understand the value of teamwork skills and attitudes in interpretation.

general_details.Description:
Demonstrate basic foundational principles, recognize second or foreign language learning theories, and design and plan lessons to teach English as a second or foreign language effectively.



This specialization is the first of two specializations that make up the TESOL Certificate from Arizona State University. In this specialization, students will learn about the basic foundational principles of language acquisition and the basic techniques founded upon those principles. It will describe second or foreign language theories, and basic studies in second language acquisition and their pedagogical implications. It will elaborate upon basic design for lesson plans and provide access to professional resources. In the final Capstone Project, in collaboration with Arizona State University’s Global Launch, students will apply the skills they learned by designing a lesson plan which includes learning outcomes, assessments, materials, classroom management techniques and the learning activities themselves.  When completing this specialization, students are eligible to continute the second specialization in order to complete the TESOL certificate experience.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Research Methods_Phương pháp nghiên cứu
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including assessment, projects and assignments preparation time)
general_details.Description: The purpose of this course is to provide an overview of research design. This overview consists of understanding the preliminary considerations that go into selecting a qualitative, quantitative, or mixed methods research design. These include knowing the definition for these different approaches, considering philosophical worldviews, reviewing the literature, understanding the use of theory, anticipating ethical issues, and developing writing strategies. We will discuss the process of research as it relates to each approach. This process includes writing an introduction, specifying a purpose statement, and developing research questions and/or hypotheses. This course will also discuss the methods and procedures for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods studies. Gen-AI tools are also integrated to enhance writing quality and facilitate research processes.

Compare and contrast the use of theory in qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods research

Be able to draft a purpose statement
Be able to draft research questions and hypotheses

Apply critical thinking skills to write the key elements of a qualitative research proposal

general_details.Time Allocation: Online study + 7.5 hours offline + 1 hour exam
general_details.Pre-Requisite: Passed ENS311/ ENS321/TRS401/ENT303 or equivalent subjects
general_details.Description:
This module aims at improving students' listening comprehension and speaking skills. Listening to class lectures and practice of note taking benefit studens in enhancing listening skills. In addition, discussion and presentation tasks offer students opportunities to practice speaking and improve their presentation skills. 



Assessment Scheme: 

1) Ongoing assessment: 

     Student gets 0.25 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.    

2) Theoretical Exam (TE) 

3) Final Result (FR) =min (10,  TE+ Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria:  FE>=4 and FR>=5.

1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1.5 hours final exam + 103.5 hours self-study

general_details.Description:
The course helps to build and develop the translation skills for 3rd year students so that at the end of the course learners will be well-versed in the English-Vietnamese and Vietnamese-English translation. 



Students are expected to acquire and apply basic knowledge of theoretical aspects covering from translation methods, translating process, equivalence, and cultural issues... in their translation.



By applying the basic theoretical knowledge, students are expected to be able to efficiently handle compiled jobs in a classroom hypothetical environment, maintain and develop basic English language skills in accordance with translation of 4 main types of texts (C1 standard) including: narrative texts,descriptiom texts, discussion texts, and dialogues.

clos.LO Details: Acquire basic knowledge of translation and its history, the application of theoretical research into translating and editing practice
Acquire knowledge and skills of analyzing a text in translation. Be able to apply the theory of text analysis to translation.
Acquire knowledge of translating process. Be able to apply the process to the translation of Vietnamese into English and vice-versa.

Acquire knowledge of language functions, text categories, types of texts. Be able to apply the theory to the translation of narrative texts (Vietnamese into 
English and vice-versa)

Acquire knowledge of different translation methods: (Word-for-word translation, literal translation, adaptation, free translation). Be able to apply different methods to translation of description texts (Vietnamese into 
English and vice-versa)
Acquire knowledge of different translation methods (Semantic & Communicative translation). Be able to use different methods to English-Vietnamese translation of discussion texts.

Acquire basic translation strategies in dealing with non-equivalence at word level, with idioms and fixed expressions, with cove, number, and person. Be able to apply these strategies to translation of idioms, fixed expressions, dialogues. (Vietnamese-English and vice-versa).

Acquire knowledge of cultural issues in translation. Know how to deal with
cultural issues to translation. Be able to apply the theory to the translation of related texts.
Have a professional working attitude and have ability to work in a team.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Biên dịch tiếng Anh 1
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1.5 hours final exam + 103.5 hours self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite:
ENS411 & ENS421 & ENR401 & ENW401  & ENP101 & ENG301
K15 onward: Passed ERW411 & LTG202
general_details.Description:
The course helps to build and develop the translation skills for 3rd year students so that at the end of the course learners will be well-versed in the English-Vietnamese and Vietnamese-English translation. 



Students are expected to acquire and apply basic knowledge of theoretical aspects covering from translation methods, translating process, equivalence, and cultural issues... in their translation.



By applying the basic theoretical knowledge, students are expected to be able to efficiently handle compiled jobs in a classroom hypothetical environment, maintain and develop basic English language skills in accordance with translation of 4 main types of texts (C1 standard) including: narrative texts,descriptiom texts, discussion texts, and dialogues.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

clos.LO Details: Acquire basic knowledge of translation and its history, the application of theoretical research into translating and editing practice
Acquire knowledge and skills of analyzing a text in translation. Be able to apply the theory of text analysis to translation.
Acquire knowledge of translating process. Be able to apply the process to the translation of Vietnamese into English and vice-versa.

Acquire knowledge of language functions, text categories, types of texts. Be able to apply the theory to the translation of narrative texts (Vietnamese into 
English and vice-versa)

Acquire knowledge of different translation methods: (Word-for-word translation, literal translation, adaptation, free translation). Be able to apply different methods to translation of description texts (Vietnamese into 
English and vice-versa)
Acquire knowledge of different translation methods (Semantic & Communicative translation). Be able to use different methods to English-Vietnamese translation of discussion texts.

Acquire basic translation strategies in dealing with non-equivalence at word level, with idioms and fixed expressions, with cove, number, and person. Be able to apply these strategies to translation of idioms, fixed expressions, dialogues. (Vietnamese-English and vice-versa).

Acquire knowledge of cultural issues in translation. Know how to deal with
cultural issues to translation. Be able to apply the theory to the translation of related texts.
Have a professional working attitude and have ability to work in a team.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Translation 2_Biên dịch 2
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including projects preparation)
general_details.Description:
This course instructs students how to apply translation techniques in dealing with interlingual translation of different types of texts including administrative forms and documents (degrees, certificate, contracts..); business forms and documents (business transaction agreement, financial statements); technical news and documents; socio-cultural news and documents.
After taking this course, students should be able to:
- Demonstrate a clear understanding of different types and formats of texts
- Demonstrate a clear understanding terms used the administrative documents, technical, economic, scientific, socio-cultural news and documents...
- Translate the mentioned kinds of news and documents from Vietnamese into English and vice-versa.
- Use Gen-AI tools to enhance translation quality and facilitate translation processes
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
'- Actively participate in class activities
'- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
'- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes
'- Read the theory in advance
'- Use Gen-AI tools in an appropriate and ethical manner

general_details.Syllabus Name: Biên dịch tiếng Anh 2
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including projects preparation)
general_details.Description:
This course instructs students how to apply translation techniques in dealing with interlingual translation of different types of texts including administrative forms and documents (degrees, certificate, contracts..); business forms and documents (business transaction agreement, financial statements);  technical news and documents; socio-cultural news and documents.

After taking this course, students should be able to: 

- Demonstrate a clear understanding of different types and formats of texts

- Demonstrate a clear understanding terms used  the administrative documents, technical, economic, scientific, socio-cultural news and documents...

- Translate the mentioned kinds of news and documents from Vietnamese into English and vice-versa.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Read the theory in advance

general_details.Description:
Based on the study results of English language and specialized subjects in the previous semesters, students shall complete a Graduation thesis with the content and format appropriate to the research area to meet all course requirements. Thus, the students are equipped with the knowledge and skills in scientific research and are able to present a research paper in English.



For each student, the Graduation thesis is the capstone project of their undergraduate program. Through the Graduation thesis, the students are equipped with the skills of finding a topic and persistently surveying, researching, and pursuing that topic, as well as practicing writing skills to present their arguments in a logical way. Hence, they can pursue self-learning even after graduation and nurture a capability of expressing their own thoughts and ideas. 

The Graduation thesis is conducted in GROUPS including 04 students (in case the students cannot be divided evenly, there can be a group of 3 or 5 students)

The instruction on the Graduation thesis is organized in two ways: in-class and in separate groups. The in-class instruction is conducted in the first one week with the content regarding the rules, regulations, and things to be noticed during the process of writing the Graduation thesis. From week 2 onwards, the groups shall meet with the Thesis supervisor separately to discuss more in-depth about the group's topic. 

The discussion with the Thesis supervisor can take place in many different forms appropriate to the availability of the supervisor and the students (meeting in class, discussion via Skype and email etc.). The content shall be recorded in the form of reports (based on the forms provided).

Thesis topic: the students can choose their topic in one of the following directions:

 (1) Specialized English

 (2) English in IT

 (3) English in Economics and Trade 

 (4) Issues in applied linguistics

 (5) Issues in English language teaching and learning

general_details.Description:
Objectives: The goal of this course is to assist students in methodically learning the fundamentals of morphology including morphemes, allomorphs, and morphological processes. The course equips the students with the knowledge and skills to analyze word structures. After the course, students will apply key theoretical frameworks of morphology (such as Lexical Morphology, Distributed Morphology) to analyze linguistic data. They also explore how morphological processes interact with syntax, focusing on word formation and sentence structure. 



Description:

This course provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamentals of morphology and its crucial role in the study of linguistics. Students will explore the functions of words, dictionaries, and the mental lexicon in morphological analysis, gaining insight into familiar processes of lexeme formation, such as derivation and compounding, and understanding how new words are created. Furthermore, it addresses the fundamental relationship between morphology and syntax, illustrating how morphological processes can influence phonological forms. Lastly, students will engage with the basic concepts of different morphological theories, enriching their understanding of the field.



Teaching and Learning Methodology

This course employs an interactive and communicative approach, fostering engaging discussions that enhance understanding of morphology. It incorporates comprehensive guidelines for pre- and post-lesson activities, allowing students to apply and reinforce the skills they have learned. Additionally, the course supports the expansion of knowledge in related fields such as philosophy and applied meaning analysis. A receptive attitude towards questions and potential miscommunications is encouraged, creating an inclusive environment that promotes active learning and collaboration. Finally, linguistic data analysis is used for morphological analysis across specific languages.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill:
Suggested topics: 1.Present word formation rules and Compounding and clarify the contents with specific examples./2. Analyze Productivity versus Creativity. Give examples for each phenomenon/
 3. Demonstrate Internal stem change and provide it with examples./4. Survey sorts of inflection (person, number, gender and noun class, tense and aspect, voice, mood, modality, and evidentiality) that can be found in the languages of the world./
 5. Survey five languages to see what morphological resources they make use of./6. Investigate the relationship between morphology and syntax./7. Describe the intersection between morphology and phonology based on the chapter "Sounds and Shapes: The Interface between Morphology and Phonology". Use specific examples to clarify your ideas./
 8.Discuss the relation between morphology and syntax which can be kept separate from one another.
assessments.Grading Guide:
- The purpose of this activity is to assess students' understanding of the concepts and morphological process, the ability to research thoroughly, summarize, and synthesize the knowledge. In addition, students are equipped with presentation, communication, teamwork and active learning skills.
Instruction:   
- The students in class are divided into groups of about 5 students. They choose randomly the topics related to the chapters in the textbook. 
- Each group will have oral presentation to summarize, analyze and apply the content of an assigned chapter (in 25-30') and demonstrate it by specific instances.
- The lecturer will facilitate, consolidate, review, and give comments. 
Expected Outcomes:
- explain examples and process of word formation 
- comparing morphological phenomena across languages
- conducting linguistic research by investigating topics, finding relevant examples
- develop the ability to respond to questions from peers and instructors

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

The course is designed to help undergraduate students  enhance their business communication via authentic and various written forms such as emails, cover letters, and CVs. With practical tips and detailed guidelines, students will be able to write more effectively and appropriately in business contexts, assuring success in delivering key messages.



Description

ENB101 addresses a wide-ranging spectrum of business communication with the straightforward seven-step method. These easy-to-follow steps save students time from start to finish, and helpful checklists will boost their confidence in business writing. Students will learn to promote themselves and their ideas clearly and concisely―whether putting together a persuasive project proposal or dealing with daily email. The course also provides comprehensive examples for all the most popular forms of communication, including slide presentations, résumés, cover letters, web copy, and a thorough guide to the art of crafting e-mails and instant messages. Insightful sidebars from experts in various fields demystify the skills of self-editing, creating content, and overcoming writer’s block, and the author’s reference-ready resources on style, punctuation, and grammar will keep students' writing error-free.



Teaching Methods:

The teaching & learning process includes a variety of methods:

From teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections; From students’ side: discussions, reading, research, writing and self-study.



Assessment scheme:

1) On-going assessment                                                       

-  Assignment      01*20%     20%

-  Progress Tests     02*20%     40%

2) Final Examination:      01*40%     40%

3) Final Result                        100%

4) Completion Criteria:  

   a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0

   b) Final Examination >=4

   c) Final Result >=5

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

The course is designed to help undergraduate students  enhance their business communication via authentic and various written forms such as emails, cover letters, and CVs. With practical tips and detailed guidelines, students will be able to write more effectively and appropriately in business contexts, assuring success in delivering key messages.



Description

ENB101 addresses a wide-ranging spectrum of business communication with the straightforward seven-step method. These easy-to-follow steps save students time from start to finish, and helpful checklists will boost their confidence in business writing. Students will learn to promote themselves and their ideas clearly and concisely―whether putting together a persuasive project proposal or dealing with daily email. The course also provides comprehensive examples for all the most popular forms of communication, including slide presentations, résumés, cover letters, web copy, and a thorough guide to the art of crafting e-mails and instant messages. Insightful sidebars from experts in various fields demystify the skills of self-editing, creating content, and overcoming writer’s block, and the author’s reference-ready resources on style, punctuation, and grammar will keep students' writing error-free.



Teaching Methods:

The teaching & learning process includes a variety of methods:

From teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections; From students’ side: discussions, reading, research, writing and self-study.



Assessment scheme:

1) On-going assessment                                                       

-  Assignment      01*20%     20%

-  Progress Tests     02*20%     40%

2) Final Examination:      01*40%     40%

3) Final Result                        100%

4) Completion Criteria:  

   a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0

   b) Final Examination >=4

   c) Final Result >=5
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of course sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and tasks given by instructor in class or at home and submit them on time

- Students use laptops in class only for learning purposes

1 course = 30 sessions

general_details.Description: This course is designed to review and build upon students’ grammatical command of English structures in order to enhance their written and spoken performances in academic settings. The course seeks to achieve this goal in a manner that differs from typical foundational grammar courses, in that this course does not examine grammatical features in isolation from one another (e.g., spending a week on the past tense without looking at other tenses); instead, this class examines grammar points as smaller systems lodged within a larger system (e.g., examining all verb tenses together to understand how they function as a group). Students will practice covered structures, and will produce several original works that will grammatically evolve over the course of the quarter (as more and more material is covered).

general_details.Description:
This course aims at:

- Introducing advanced and complex grammar concepts to students

- Instructing students to blend verb tenses effectively and how to punctuate sentences correctly

- Helping students improve their academic English  

*Assessment scheme:

1) Ongoing assessment: 

  Student gets 0.25 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.    

2) Theoretical Exam (TE) 

3) Final Result (FR) =min (10,  TE+ Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria:  TE>=4 and FR>=5

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus ( Optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus

Practice acquired advanced grammar points in writing

LO4.2	Practice use various grammar points in writing

general_details.Syllabus Name: Advanced English Grammar_Ngữ pháp tiếng Anh nâng cao
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 104 hours of self-study + 1 hour for the final exam 
1 session = 45 minutes
general_details.Description: The course is designed to consolidate and enhance students' grammatical knowledge. It aims to achieve this by giving learners exposure to grammar as it is used in real life situations, offering them comprehensive explanations for grammatical forms and meanings, providing contextualized practice of various structures, and developing their use of such structures as well as their critical thinking skills through communicative activities. Students will also be informed of how to recognize common grammatical errors in their written work and encouraged to apply learned grammar in writing.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptops in class only for learning purposes
general_details.Note:

- 01 Project: 30% 
- 03 Progress tests: 30%

Conditions to pass: 
Each on-going assessment's component's mark: >=3/10
Each progress tests' components' mark >0
Each final exam's components' mark >0
Final exam's mark: >=4/10
Grade average >=5/10

clos.LO Details: Analyze how grammar is used in many contexts from a variety of reading and listening texts
Assess whether structures being used are appropriate for written and spoken communication

Compose grammatically accurate spoken and written texts of different topics

CLO3.1: Recall basic and advanced structures of English and their meanings
CLO3.2: Identify and correct common grammatical errors in both written and spoken English
CLO3.3: Explain how and why basic and advanced structures of English are used in different contexts
Proactively collaborate with peers for group work and problem-solving

assessments.Question Type:
*Option 1:
Students work in a group of 5:
- Each group contacts lecturers of ENT/TRS classes, BEN's writing classes (EAW, ERW, ENB) or ENM classes to ask for some written work (paragraphs, essays or emails) in which grammatical mistakes are largely present. 
- Each member in a group is in charged of identifying, correcting any grammatical mistakes in 2 pieces of writing obtained, and rewriting the texts.
- Each group collects their corrections and rewritten versions of the texts in the form of a booklet. In the booklet, they write a summary of the most common grammatical errors they can find in the pieces of writing they are in charged of and put forward suggestions on how to avoid them.
- The groups send their booklets to the lecturer in charge for marking and give a presentation on how they have worked on the texts in class for feedback.
- The groups edit their booklets and send them to the lecturers of the classes mentioned above, who will send the booklets to their students or use them as teaching materials.                                                                                                              

*Option 2: Lecturer's choice

general_details.Description:
1. Objectives:

• build confidence in professional skills such as dealing with enquiries, marketing destinations, offering advice, negotiating, writing emails and speaking

to groups

• develop language awareness through an integrated grammar and skills syllabus

• acquire the specialized vocabulary needed by tourism professionals

• practise language skills in realistic Case studies that reflect issues in the tourist

industry today. 

2. Description: English for International Tourism is a three-level series designed to meet the

English language needs of professionals working in the tourism industry and students of tourism in further education. 

3. Teaching method: lecture and seminar format

4. Assessment scheme: 

On-going assesment: 50%                   

Final examination:      50 % 

Completion Criteria: Every on-going assessment component >0, Each part of the final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10.

general_details.Syllabus Name: ACADEMIC ENGLISH 1
general_details.Time Allocation:
Course Time:30 sessions

1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
The main objective of the course is to help students develop the academic language and academic skills especially Listening and Speaking skills. Besides, the course aims at providing students with strategies necessary to achieve proficiency in English.  

1. Developing skills:

1.1 Listening skills: Prediction, Listening for signpost words, Classification, Understanding illustration: map, visual information, Note taking, Listening for paraphrase, etc.  

1.2 Speaking skills: Giving factual information, Expressing opinions /attitudes /preferences / reasons/feelings, Describing, Comparing and contrasting, Speculation, etc.

2. Developing language:

Increase academic vocabulary, including collocations, and sentence structures through the topics in academic context.

3. Dealing with tests/exams: provide students with different kinds of listening and speaking tasks simulating exams for practice.
general_details.StudentTasks:
Regularly attend class-meeting hours and complete assignments and homeworks

For BBA students: must attend at least 80% of the total course time in order to be admitted to the final exam

general_details.Syllabus Name: Business English 1 - Tiếng Anh thương mại 1
general_details.Time Allocation: Online study + 4.5 hrs offline + PE (Interview 7-10 mins/student)
general_details.Description:
The course is designed to enable students to:

- develope English language and communicate skills for the workplace, do business, cross-cultural understanding, and business case study analysis

- apply these skills in the final Capstone Project by analysing a current business case study and providing recommendations to a target audience in both presentation and written formats.



1) Ongoing assessment: 

Student gets 0.5 bonus points for each course completed on time. The total bonus point is not greater than 1.    

2) Practical Exam (PE) 

3) Final Result (FR) =min (10,  PE+ Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria:  PE>=4 and FR>=5
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (optional)

6. Must complete all required MOOCs with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus

general_details.Syllabus Name: BUSINESS ENGLISH -  Level: Elementary 1
general_details.Time Allocation:
1 course = 30 session   

1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to improve learner's business English skills, confidence and fluency in using the English language within various situations and context. Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

* understand different business concepts and re-affirm grammar rules at the beginner’s level and extend their business vocabulary; 

 * develop listening skills and enhance  their comprehension of gist and listening for detailed information skills. 

* improve their speaking skills and discuss business topic and concepts with confidence and apply wider communication skills in a variety of business situations and contexts.

* enrich their reading skills involving informative, stimulating, and up-to-date business-related texts. 

* develop writing skills, with specific focus on writing short e-mails. 

Skills development

Students will be assisted in developing their skills in reading, writing, listening and speaking through business English syllabus with exercises exploring:

* skimming, 

* scanning, 

* detailed reading, 

* guessing unknown words from context, 

* understanding text organization, 

*recognizing argument and counter-argument; 

* distinguishing between main information and supporting detail, fact and opinion, hypothesis versus evidence;

* summarising and note-taking.

Writing skills will encompass:

* Essay content and structure (patterns of organization, paragraphing, discussion – developing balanced argument and counter-argument, exposing advantages and disadvantages of issues discussed with original ideas in a coherent and cohesive manner with correct punctuation). 

* Functions (generalization, definitions, exemplification, classification, comparison and contrast, cause and effect, process and procedure, interpretation of data). 

* Style (avoiding passive constructions and verbosity). 

Listening skills will include:

* conversations between several businesspeople in a variety of business situations requiring students to listen for gist and detailed information and evaluate the importance of information. 

* supplementary fun and stimulating audio-visual files exploring grammar and English in social situations. 

Speaking skills will include:

* developing effective business communication skills through debating, pitching for a point, agreeing and disagreeing, clarifying, questioning and concluding. 

* Understanding and using simple presentation skills encompassing introductions, stating a purpose, signposting, highlighting key points of a paragraph, summarizing and developing convincing and logical conclusions. 

* listening to and comprehending equivalent to IELTS score 4.5-5.0);

* speaking to peers and lecturers (within the framework of Breakthrough level-A1).

general_details.Description:
This course is designed to help students improve their ability to communicate in English in a wide range of business situations. Besides, it also helps students acquire and develop business knowledge through the authentic sources such as Financial Times. In addition to the Market Leader unit outlines the course is enhanced with supplementary activities corresponding to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. In particular the course will help students:

* Communicate effectively in discussions, meetings, negotiations, socialization events

* acquire and effectively use professional skills including telephoning, presentations, correspondence exchange, and problem solving.

* enrich knowledge of business in the fast-changing world

* Communicate effectively in discussions, meetings, negotiations, socialization events

* acquire and effectively use professional skills including telephoning, presentations, correspondence exchange, decision making, and problem solving.

* enrich knowledge of business trends in the fast-changing world

This course applies instructional, communicative and interactive methods which

*provides inducive environment for communication between teacher and students as well as between students themselves

*develops confidence and fluency through participation in case studies as simulations of business scenarios; 

*enhances skills and knowledge application through individual and group works and self-study

general_details.Syllabus Name: Business English – Level 1_Tiếng Anh Thương mại - Cấp 1
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 100-minute final exam + 103.25 hours self-study

1 session = 45 minutes
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to help students further improve their ability to communicate in English in a wide range of business and business-related situations. It also helps students develop the necessary knowledge and skills to succeed in business. In addition to the business-focused contents, the course is enhanced with supplementary activities corresponding to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. In particular, the course will help students:

* Communicate effectively in discussions, meetings, negotiations, socialization events

* acquire and effectively use professional skills including telephoning, presentations, correspondence exchange, decision-making, and problem-solving.

* enrich knowledge of business trends in the fast-changing world

* enhance students' employability
general_details.StudentTasks:
'- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Access the course website (https://fu-edunext.fpt.edu.vn/) for group discussions to construct knowledge, for practicing and assessment

materials_table.Author: Iwonna DubickaMarjorie RosenbergBob DignenMike HoganLizzie Wright
M O'Keefe, Lewis Lansford et al.

clos.LO Details: Demonstrate knowledge of business vocabulary, terminology and concepts in digital business, finance, management, and operations to convey messages clearly and effectively

Build awareness and understanding of business situations, including how to communicate in different business contexts and working across cultures with authentic content from the Financial Times and other news sources

Apply the principles of effective business communication, including clarity, conciseness, and formality; Demonstrate a professional attitude in all forms of business communication, showing respect, politeness, and consideration for others.
Apply language skills, soft skills and business skills to work and communicate effectively in various international business settings
Demonstrate critical thinking skills to analyze business problems and scenarios critically
Write e-mails, cover letters, memo, proposal and brief reports and other creative commercials
Be cooperative, supportive, and responsible in group work.
Apply the processes involved in job hunting, including writing resumes and cover letters, preparing for interviews, and networking  that enhances employability

Identify key points, main ideas, and specific details in business news reports and conversations, recognize different communication styles used in business settings and distinguish between different speakers and identify their roles in a conversation.

general_details.Syllabus Name: BUSINESS ENGLISH -  Level: Upper- Intermediate_Tiếng anh thương mại
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1.6 hours final exam + 103.4 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to help students further enhance their ability to communicate in English in an almost real business and business-related situations. It covers not only general business administration area but also deals with more complex issues such as management style and crisis management. It also helps students develop necessary knowledge and skills to excell in their future career. In addition to the business-focused contents, the course is enhanced with supplementary activities corresponding to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, with a focus on developing students' own style in communication as a plus in their professional communication strategy. In particular the course will help students:

* Enhance confidence, accuracy and fluency to communicate professionally and effectively in business-like contexts e.g. discussions, meetings, negotiations for the best business results;

* acquire and practice professional communication skills at a higher level of complexity, including dealing with complaints, persuading for loan, negotiating for the best terms in M&A , information-based decision making and problem solving.

* expand knowledge of business concepts and business trends in the fast-changing world



Teaching and Learning Methodology

This course applies instructional, communicative and interactive methods which

*provides inducive environment for communication between teacher and students as well as between students themselves

*develops confidence and fluency through participation in case studies as simulations of business scenarios; 

*enhances skills and knowledge application through individual and group works and self-study
general_details.StudentTasks:
* be punctual for all the lessons

* attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination.

* take an active role in class activities.

* fullfil tasks and assignments given by instructor
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Net-Challenge Simulation Software (CD accompany with the textbook)
general_details.Note:
The course applies an on-going assessment scheme with progress tests, mid-term test and final examination structured as follows

1) On-going assessment                                                    

'- Progress Test: 2*15%     = 30%

- Assignment: 2*10% = 20%

2) Final Examination (FE)                                                               50%

3) Final Result                                                                                  100%

4) Completion Criteria:  Every on-going assessment component >0, each part of the final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10.

clos.LO Details: * employ key grammar items(of upper-intermediate level) and business collocation and idiomatic vocabulary to present information, to express and exchange opinions and ideas on a certain number of business-related topics in both spoken and written contexts so as to achieve the set communication targets.

* give out rational judgement, comments and arguments, using data supports, in various business-like contexts (meetings, negotiations, complain handling, networking, etc.) with higher level of accuracy and etiquet in both oral and written forms;
* solve simulated business problems using knowledge and information presented in verbal, numerical or graphical form;

* listen to and understand others' talks so as to have appropriate responses that help maintain and develop conversations and other oral exchanges for 10 - 15 minutes on the learnt topics then maneuver well in spontaneous situations
* organize and present ideas and statements in a clear, logical and appropriate form of presentation within 15 minutes to achieve the set business communication targets.
* read and understand various business-related texts including articles and reports of upto 1,000 words as well as commercial articles
* write e-mails, letters, memo, brief reports (upto 1,500 words) and other creative commercials to serve different business purposes.

clos.LO Details: Demonstrate knowledge of business vocabulary, terminology and concepts (of level  B2+) in digital business, finance, investment, management, relocation, strategic alliances, and operations to convey messages clearly and effectively

Build awareness and identify business situations, including how to understand and communicate in different business contexts and working across cultures with authentic content at B2+ level from the Financial Times and other news sources

Apply the principles of effective business communication at B2+ level ( language skills, soft skills and business skills), including clarity, conciseness, and formality in various international business settings ; Demonstrate a professional attitude in all forms of business communication, showing respect, politeness, and consideration for others.

Write e-mails of proposal and business report summary
Be cooperative, supportive, and responsible in group work.

general_details.Description:
-Objective:  Help students work on their pronunciation and speak English with neutral accent, fluency and comprehension; identify diversity of sound systems.

-Description: 'This course will cover different aspects of pronunciation in English for practical uses including letters and sounds, combining sounds, word stress, stress patterns, intonation, speed, tone, accents and phonemic symbols.

clos.LO Details: Recognise and demonstrate the way to pronounce and spell consonant sounds of English; the way to make the differences between the sounds clear.
Recognise and demonstrate the way to pronounce and spell vowel sounds of English; the way to make the differences between the sounds clear.
Recognise and demonstrate the way to pronounce and spell the dipthongs tripthongs of English; the way to make the differences between the sounds clear.

Demonstrate the fluency when speaking, an ability to present a clear statement of constraint, change intonation and determine suitable sentence stress to be able to show different modes of meanings and feelings.
Apply the rules of connected speech to sound more fluent when students speak
Practice and refine the lifelong learning behavior of collaboration by working together as a group

general_details.Time Allocation:
Hours Per Course: 30 sessions

1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
Listening:  

Students can listen to understand a speaker’s main ideas, explanations and examples. 

Students also listen to know strategies needed in academic situations such as listening for results, special terms, advantages and disadvantages, …

Students also listen to handle the information they hear by using such strategies as understanding cause and effect, event sequences, recognizing definitions, predicting, interpreting speaker’s attitude. 



Speaking:

Students know how to express what they think and/or feel, and how to make themselves well understood by handling issues related to techniques or strategies used in daily speaking encounters.

Students are also able to use pronunciation strategies to express correctly what they want to say in everyday speaking situations. 

Students also know how to speak correctly what is related to academic issues such as presentations, debates and self- introductions.

general_details.Syllabus Name: SKILLFUL 1 - LISTENING & SPEAKING 2
general_details.Time Allocation:
Hours Per Course: 30 sessions

1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
Listening:  

Students can listen to understand a speaker’s main ideas, points, and intentions. 

Students also listen to know strategies needed in academic situations such as listening for summaries, for note taking, for supporting statements…

Students also listen to handle the information they hear by using such strategies as understanding cause and effect, event sequences, recognizing definitions, predicting, interpreting speaker’s attitude. 



Speaking:

Students know how to express what they think and/or feel, and how to make themselves well understood by handling issues related to techniques or strategies used in daily speaking encounters.

Students are also able to use pronunciation strategies to express correctly what they want to say in everyday speaking situations. 

Students also know how to speak correctly what is related to academic issues such as presentations, debates and self- introductions.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of in-class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Use CD-ROM provided with the textbook

- Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (300h) = 105 contact hours (70 slots) + 1.5 hours final exam + 193.5 hours self-study

Interactive Classroom Teaching

1 slot =90'
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to further develop the learner's confidence and fluency in using the English language and to enrich their learning experience through interactive lessons and communicative exercises. 

Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

1. Demonstrate knowledge of a vocabulary range covered in lessons (including meaning, opposites, spelling and pronunciation)

2. Show understanding of grammar rules taught through exercises, know of the role of conjunctions, articles and prepositions in writing, and understand the simple present and past tense

3. Show understanding of the reading texts by responding to text questions 

4. Make simple 'wh' and ‘yes/no’ questions, use vocabulary, acceptable expressions, and grammatical structures to respond to social communicative tasks

5. Use simple sentences correctly to respond to writing exercises in the textbook appropriately and write paragraphs on simple topics (my favorite subject, a person I like, the most beautiful place, etc…)

6. Listen and respond (orally and in writing) to each other, recorded texts and video clips

7. Develop effective communication and teamwork in different academic and social tasks

8. Develop ethics, self-study, professionalism, respect in different disciplines, group work, and creativity.

general_details.Syllabus Name: ENGLISH 2
general_details.Time Allocation:
Course = 100 slots  x 1,5h = 150 hours

Interactive Classroom Teaching

1 slot=90'
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to further develop the learner's confidence and fluency in using the English language and to enrich their learning experience through interactive lessons and communicative exercises. 

Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

a.   Integrated Language Skills based on the prescribed textbook

1. Demonstrate knowledge of a vocabulary range covered in lessons (including meaning, opposites, spelling and pronunciation).  

2. Speak confidently and use acceptable expressions in daily communication.  

3. Listen and respond (orally and in writing)  to each other, recorded texts and video clips

4. Show understanding of the reading texts by responding to questions

5. Respond to writing exercises in the textbook appropriately

6. Demonstrate understanding of grammar rules taught through exercises.

b.  Vocabulary Development based on text book and reference books

1. Show understanding of new words learnt in textbook

2. Know of meaning of synonyms,  antonyms and simple homonyms

3. Do word puzzles and play word games

c.  Additional Writing & Grammar

1. Write simple and compound sentences correctly.

2. Know of the role of conjunctions, articles and prepositions  in writing

3. Understand the simple present and past tense system

4. At the end of the course, write simple paragraphs on simple topics.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Use CD-ROM provided with the textbook

- Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Tiếng Anh 2
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (300h) = 105 contact hours (70 slots) + 1.5 hours final exam + 193.5 hours self-study

Interactive Classroom Teaching

1 slot =90'
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to further develop the learner's confidence and fluency in using the English language and to enrich their learning experience through interactive lessons and communicative exercises. 

Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

1. Use a vocabulary range covered in lessons to describe (healthfulness of food/trips/travel experience/good or bad deals/ products), express disappointment, state and sympathise with the problem

2. Understand grammar rules taught in lessons and use them in both the spoken form for social communication and write well-organized forms for topics covered in the course (simple present, present continuous, simple past, modal verbs, conjunctions,  comparison, and simple sentence structures)

3. Understand various types of recordings and videos and apply different listening techniques (classifying, inferring, identifying main ideas or details, summarizing) to respond correctly to the social situations covered in the course

4. Understand different reading texts by applying a variety of reading strategies (skimming and scanning, making inferences and predictions, bar graph interpretation, summarising and paraphrasing, identifying supporting details, applying information, drawing conclusions, clarifying information)

5. Use appropriate colloquial expressions, and conversational strategies covered in the course in social conversations

6. Use different learning tools (books, Internet, online platforms, audios, videos, etc.) appropriately to perform various learning tasks creatively

7. Develop effective communication and teamwork in different academic and social tasks

8. Develop ethics, self-study, professionalism, respect in different disciplines, group work, and creativity
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Access the course website for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Net-Challenge Simulation Software (CD accompany with the textbook)
general_details.Note:
1) On-going assessment : 50%                                                     

2) Final Examination (FE): 50% 

3) Final Result:      100%                                                                    

4) Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, each part of the final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10.

general_details.Description:
This course is designed to further develop the learner's confidence and fluency in using the English language and to enrich their learning experience through interactive lessons and communicative exercises. 

Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

1. Apply the knowledge of a vocabulary range covered in lessons in academic and social disciplines

2. Understand grammar rules taught in lessons and use them in both the spoken form for social communication and writing well-organized forms for topics covered in the course

3. Understand different reading texts by applying a variety of reading strategies (skimming, scanning, making inferences and predictions, summarising and paraphrasing, comparing and contrasting)

4. Understand various types of recordings and videos and apply different listening techniques (classifying, inferring, identifying main ideas or details, summarizing) to respond correctly to the social situations covered in the course

5. Develop ethics, self-study, professionalism, respect in different disciplines, group work, and creativity

6. Use  appropriate colloquial expressions and various conversational strategies covered in the course in social conversations

7. Develop effective communication and teamwork in different academic and social tasks

8. Apply cultural knowledge or personalize or express appropriately in social situations

9. Use different learning tools (books, Internet, audio, videos, etc.) appropriately to perform various learning tasks creatively
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by the instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Access the course website for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Net-Challenge Simulation Software (CD accompany with the textbook)
general_details.Note:
1) On-going assessment : 50%                                                     

2) Final Examination (FE): 50% 

3) Final Result:      100%                                                                    

4) Completion Criteria: On-going assessment >0, each part of the final exam must be >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Writing 1
general_details.Time Allocation:
1 course = 30 sessions

1 session= 90 minutes
general_details.Description: The course is designed to develop and sharpen learners' academic and professional writing skills and strategies in English. Each unit guides the student through the structured writing process with plenty of full colour illustrations, examples, and exercises to engage the student and build confidence. This course aims at providing students understanding and skills from writing sentences to a full paragraph.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Description: The course is designed to develop and sharpen learners' academic and professional writing skills and strategies in English. This course aims at providing students understanding and skills from writing a paragragh to developing a full essay.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Academic Writing Skills_Kỹ năng viết học thuật
general_details.Time Allocation: 84 hours online study + 3 hrs offline (2 slots) + 1hr exam + 62 hours self-study
general_details.Description: The skills taught in this Specialization will empower you to succeed in any college-level course or professional field. You’ll learn to conduct rigorous academic research and to express your ideas clearly in an academic format. In the final Capstone Project, all the knowledge that you’ve gained over the span of these courses will culminate into an academic research paper on an issue of your choice.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus
general_details.Note:
1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

2) Theoretical Exam (PE) 

3) Final Result (FR) =min (10, PE + Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria:  PE>=4 and FR>=5

materials_table.Note: MOOC 02: Getting Started with Essay Writing
MOOC 04: Introduction to Research for Essay Writing
MOOC 05: Project: Writing a Research Paper

clos.LO Details:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
 - identify the correct verb tenses to use
 - use commas effectively
 - utilize several different sentence types
 - write more effectively in English

After completing this course,  students will be able to:
 - create effective thesis statements for essays
 - plan and write compare/contrast, cause/effect, and argument essays
 - write well-developed body paragraphs

After completing this course,  students will be able to: 
 - plan and write a more sophisticated argument essay
 - identify plagiarism and explain how to prevent it
 - read and analyze several articles to form students' own opinion on a topic
 - make connections between several articles
 - form thesis statements from students' readings
 - use sources effectively when writing an essay

After completing this course,  students will be able to:
 - choose appropriate research topics for college classes
 - write detailed outlines for research papers
 - find and evaluate reliable sources for research papers
 - take notes for research
 - use academic style and tone 
 - document sources by creating a Works Cited list in MLA format
 - avoid plagiarism

In this capstone project, students will:
 - conduct research on an academic topic of their own choice
 - create an outline for the research paper
 - write a short annotated bibliography 
 - write a 7-8 page research paper
 - use MLA In-text Citations and MLA Works Cited Page correctly

clos.LO Details:
After completing this course, students will be able to:
 - identify the correct verb tenses to use
 - use commas effectively
 - utilize several different sentence types
 - write more effectively in English

After completing this course,  students will be able to:
 - create effective thesis statements for essays
 - plan and write compare/contrast, cause/effect, and argument essays
 - write well-developed body paragraphs

After completing this course,  students will be able to: 
 - plan and write a more sophisticated argument essay
 - identify plagiarism and explain how to prevent it
 - read and analyze several articles to form students' own opinion on a topic
 - make connections between several articles
 - form thesis statements from students' readings
 - use sources effectively when writing an essay

After completing this course,  students will be able to:
 - choose appropriate research topics for college classes
 - write detailed outlines for research papers
 - find and evaluate reliable sources for research papers
 - take notes for research
 - use academic style and tone 
 - document sources by creating a Works Cited list in MLA format
 - avoid plagiarism

In this capstone project, students will:
 - conduct research on an academic topic of their own choice
 - create an outline for the research paper
 - write a short annotated bibliography 
 - write a 7-8 page research paper
 - use MLA In-text Citations and MLA Works Cited Page correctly

general_details.Syllabus Name: Persuasive Communication_Giao tiếp để thuyết phục
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 0.5 hour final exam + 104.5 hours self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite: Passed ERW411 and SSC302c and SSG103 or SSG104
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

	The course is designed to help undergraduate students to grasp the key concepts and practices of persuasive communication today. Through real-life situations as well as authentic materials, students will be able to develop their communication and persuasion skills.



Description

	EPC301 provides students with a comprehensive yet accessible overview of the study and practice of persuasive communication. It also demonstrates how theories and research illuminate and adapt to the present digital era, with continued attention to ethical implications and today’s big topics. The course includes up-to-date definitions of key terms in the field as they relate to present-day practice; an integration of persuasion theories and the ubiquity of online influence; new examples and cases to illustrate persuasive communication’s approach to health campaigns, attitudes, communicator appeals, dissonance, and ethics; and a thorough reflection of the most current scholarship in the field.



Teaching Methods:

	The teaching & learning process includes a variety of methods:

	 From teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections; 			 From students’ side: discussions, presentations, research, writing and self-study.



Assessment scheme:

1) On-going assessment                                                       

-  Assignments      02*20%     40%

-  Presentation     01*20%     20%

2) Final examination (Project): 40%

3) Final Result                        100%

4) Completion Criteria:  

   a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0

   b) Final examination: >=4

   c) Final Result >=5

general_details.Description:
This Specialization is intended to prepare students with professional skills in the workplace.



Through four courses, students will explore the use of emotional and social intelligence, practice a formula for problem solving, cultivate a growth mindset, and build skills related to adaptability and resilience in an ever-changing environment. These skills show up in business relationships and communication and ultimately impact professional effectiveness. Students will be able to demonstrate sound judgment by engaging in critical thinking to reach decisions and solve problems independently. Students will be able to develop a competitive advantage by learning, adapting, and harnessing insights from past endeavors. Students will assess your own expectations in their current or anticipated work roles and settings, and how those may align with or differ from what is required by employers and other stakeholders now and in the future.
