general_details.Syllabus Name: Ngữ dụng học Tiếng Anh_English Pragmatics
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
- Course objective: The aim of the course is to enable students to critically evaluate how context impacts the interpretation of meaning in communication. Additionally, students will be equipped to apply their understanding of pragmatics in order to produce precise and contextually appropriate content in English for various communicative purposes. 



- Course description: This course focuses on how context influences the interpretation of meaning in communication. The course provides understanding on contextual meaning so that students will be able to analyze how context, including cultural background and situational factors, shapes the meaning of utterances. 1. Emphasize the practical skills that students will learn in this course. 2. Observe coherence and consistency in using active voice statements. 3. The course includes an exploration of speech act concepts, illustrating how utterances can serve as requests, commands, questions, or statements based on the context in which they are used.

Concepts of speech acts, including how utterances can function as requests, commands, questions, or statements, depending on context are provided with . Mastery of pragmatics equips students with the ability to navigate complex social and professional situations, fostering better negotiation, collaboration, and overall communication competence, which are invaluable assets in careers such as business, education, law, media, and international relations. 



- Teaching and Learning Methodology: This course applies instructional, communicative, and interactive discussions. Instructions on pre-lesson and post lesson exercises are designed to apply learnt skills. Open minded approach to questions and any misunderstandings that may arise during lessons is preferred. Group work and pair work are encouraged to foster interaction and discussion. Group presentations are carried out to reflect students' comprehension on pragmatic aspects in the course. Linguistic data analysis may particularly be included as the students are required to do the Assignment across specific languages.

assessments.Question Type: Presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Relevant knowledge and skills learnt from units 1-8
assessments.Grading Guide:
- Students are divided into groups of 5 members to give a group 
oral presentation (within 25 minutes) on a topic given by instructors. 
 - The presentation content must include sufficient content on the topic learned in the 
course with practical examples, sufficient explanations and similarities and differences 
between English and Vietnamese regarding the pragmatic aspects observed. 
 - The presentation has two main parts for assesement: 
 (1) group score 50%: organization, subject knowledge, slides; 
 (2) individual score 50%: language use, presentation skills
Rationale: to deepen students' understanding of key concepts in pragmatics and enhance their ability to communicate these ideas clearly. Each group will explore a specific topic related to pragmatics, providing theoretical insights and practical examples to help the audience connect with the subject matter.
assessments.Note:
Topics for group presentation:
1. The Role of Context in Pragmatics: Exploring how different contexts shape meaning and communication structures.
2. Speech Act Theory in Everyday Communication: Analyzing the functions of speech acts and their impact on interactions.
3. Cooperative Principle and Its Applications: Investigating how the principles of cooperation guide effective communication.
4. Politeness vs. Impoliteness: A study of strategies used in varying cultural contexts to navigate politeness and impoliteness.
5. Critical Discourse Analysis and Power Dynamics: Examining how language reflects and influences power relationships in society.
6. Intercultural Pragmatics: Bridging Communication Gaps: Analyzing challenges and strategies for effective communication across cultures.
7. Implicature in Communication: Understanding how speakers imply meanings beyond the literal interpretation of their words.
8. Conversation Analysis and English as a Lingua Franca (ELF): Exploring how conversation analysis can enhance communication in multilingual settings.
9. The Impact of Culture on Indirect Communication: Investigating how cultural norms shape preferences for directness or indirectness in conversation.
10. Teaching Pragmatics in Language Education: Strategies for integrating pragmatic competence into language learning curricula.
Each presentation should be:
Informative and Analytical: provide a clear overview of the assigned topic, delve into its theoretical background, and analyze its practical applications. Emphasis should be placed on making complex ideas accessible and engaging for the audience.
Interactive: include activities, questions, or discussions to involve the audience and encourage engagement with the material.
Concise and Structured: be well-organized, with clear sections covering introduction, main content, practical examples, and a conclusion. Each section should be purposeful and connected to the topic’s key ideas.

general_details.Description:
This course offers a comprehensive, yet approachable, guide to public relations plans for students. The knowledge and techniques presented and discussed in this text serve as an effective guide for enhancing students' public relations planning skills.

Course objectives:

Master the  fundamental strategies, tactics, and tools of public relations and those who wish to learn them in the context of the rapidly changing entertainment industry:

 - Exhibit an advanced understanding of the relationship between entertainment and communication. 

- Exhibit an advanced understanding of the theories of humanities and social science 

- Plan a publicity campaign, manage public image, leverage the effects of digital media, and write a compelling press release

- Construct professional media and communication practices
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities 

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Read the textbook in advance

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

	The course is designed to help students develop skills of critical reading, thinking and writing in various academic topics. Through interacting actively with texts of different kinds, students will be able to read, think and write better, at an upper-intermediate level.



Description

	Read, Think & Write 1 focuses on reading and writing in one course to help students read from a writer's viewpoint and write with a reader in mind. It is also designed to provide a systematic introduction to and an in-depth analysis of how to integrate reading and writing skills. The course provides a cohesive instructional framework to accelerate college readiness through unique resources.



Teaching Methods:

	The teaching process includes a variety of methods, from teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections and from students’ side:  discussions, idea brainstorming and writing and self-study.



Assessment scheme:

1) Assessment                                                       

-  Assignments      04*15%     60%

-  Final Exam   01*40%.   40%

2) Final Result                        100%

3) Completion Criteria:  

   a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0; Final exam >= 4

   b) Final Result >=5
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptops in class only for learning purpose

general_details.Syllabus Name: Read-Think-Write 2_Kỹ năng tư duy Đọc - Viết 2
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including projects preparation time)
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

	The course is designed to help students develop skills of critical reading, thinking and writing in various academic topics. Through completing a number of authentic projects of reading and writing and through teacher’s guide as well as feedback, students will be able to further their skills, at an advanced level.



Description

	Read, Think and Write 2 focuses on reading and writing in one course to help students read from a writer's viewpoint and write with a reader in mind. It is also designed to engage students in real-world, college-level projects to gain the literacy skills they need to succeed. The course provides detailed knowledge and practice of using sources effectively, avoiding plagiarism as well as writing well-crafted sentences.



Teaching Methods:

	The teaching process includes a variety of methods, from teachers’ side: lectures, guided learning, feedback and corrections and from students’ side:  discussions, idea brainstorming and writing, peer corrections and self-corrections.



Assessment scheme:

1) On-going assessment                                                       

-  Projects                  02               55%

- Peer corrections    02*5%.      10%

Final exam      01     35%

2) Final Result                           100%

4) Completion Criteria:  

       a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0

       b) Final Result >=5
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible for doing all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptops in class only for learning purposes

general_details.Syllabus Name: Sociolinguistics_Ngôn ngữ học xã hội
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

This course is designed to introduce to the students the basic concepts of Sociolingusitics and the relationship between language and society, and how language is used in multilingual speech communities. 

Description:

The course helps students:

~Understand sociolinguitic termology or concepts to apply in research and real-life practices. 

~Use language appropriately in different social contexts.

~Interpret the social relationships in a community, and the way people convey and construct aspects of their social identity through their language.

~Examine some similarities and differences in the way people use their language to convey meaning in association with society.

Teaching method:

This course applies instructional, communicative, and interative disccusions with:

~instructions on lessons and exercises meant to apply learnt skills.

~researching features of sociolinguistics through presentations and project work.

~open-minded approach to questions and issues that may arise during lessons.

~lectures and seminars to enhance interest in the field of sociolinguistics.

Assessment scheme:

   +On-going assessment: 50% 

      1. Progress Test 1: 10%

      2. Progress Test 2: 10%

      3. Assignment 1:Presentation: 15%  

      4. Assignment 2:Discussion Leading: 15%

   +Final exam: 50%

On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10
general_details.StudentTasks:
~Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

~Be punctual for class.

~Actively participate in class discussions.

~Preview and review the lessons.

~Check vocabulary for comprehension.

~Do the exercises before, during, and after the class.

~Hand in homework and class requirements.

~Work with a group for group discussions and activities.

clos.LO Details: Understand and define sociolinguistic theories. Explain how language is used in mutilingual communities (differnt languages used in different settings or situations)
Examine how language is maintained and some factors lead to language shift.
Analyse and how language varies in nations with different types of language used and how a language is planned to become a national language.
Explain how language differs in regions in terms of accents and dialects and the influence of age and gender on language use.
Understand the way people use their language to signal their enthicity, the influence of social networks on the way people speak, and reasons for language change
Examine how language varies according to its style and context.
Analyse different functions of speech, politeness, cross culture communication, gender and stereotypes
Study the language-perception relationship as well as language-culture relationship; and how discourse is viewed by pragmatics.
Practice and refine the lifelong learning behavior of collaboration by working together as a group.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Cú pháp học tiếng Anh_English Syntax
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Course description: 

This course offers an introduction to the practical analysis of English sentence structure and is designed for English learners who are into the field of linguistics.The course provides key concepts in English sentence structure such as constituency, category and functions, employing tree diagrams and practices of drawing tree diagrams which help learners make sense of the knowledge provided. The exercises are relevant, not only for reviewing syntactic aspects and discussions of in-text exercises but also for constructing interrelationships between syntactic knowledge in different languages and ones of related areas in linguistics. References for further reading are given at the end of each chapter to offer learners choices for extensive reading about related subjects. 

Course objective: 

The course aims to provide students knowledge of syntax for applying to their studying linguistics and for generating accurate content in English for different communication purposes. 

Teaching and Learning Methodology: 

This course applies instructional, communicative, and interactive discussions. It is appropriate for different teaching and learning tendencies involving instructors' instructions on pre-lesson and post lesson exercises meant to apply learnt skills; ancillary lectures and seminars to enhance active interest in the topics; or interactive discussions leading by students followed by instructors' feedback and conclusions. Open-mindedness and questions from both students and instructors are encouraged if  misunderstandings related to the subject knowledge arise.

Deconstruct structures of clauses and complex sentences by identifying appropriate functions of constituents
Transform phrases, clauses, and sentences into syntactic tree diagrams by using phrase markers or triangles

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Lessons learned in the course; evaluating, comparing and contrasting, synthesizing content from various resources
assessments.Grading Guide:
- Students are divided into small groups of 4-5 members to give a group oral presentation (within 25 - 30 minutes) on a topic given by instructors. 
- The presentation content must include sufficient content on the topic learned in the course with practical examples, common syntactic errors identified among language learners, and similarities and differences between English and Vietnamese regarding the syntactic aspects observed. 
- The presentation has two main parts for assessing: 
(1) group score 50%: organization, subject knowledge, slides; 
(2) individual score 50%: language use, presentation skills
For more details, please refer to the Appendix.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 68h online + 3h offline + 1h Final exam + 78h self-study
general_details.Description: This course provides students with the knowledge and experience necessary for success in the entertainment industry. It comprises two parts: First, "Entertainment Business Foundations," which focuses on the music industry, provides a comprehensive overview, including the industry's history and role dynamics. In the second section, you'll explore the intersection of fandom, popular culture, and digital media, learning how to analyse popular culture products, map fan networks, and understand the links between popular culture and the political and commercial factors that shape its production, distribution, and consumption.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Understanding Language Testing_Phương pháp đánh giá năng lực ngôn ngữ
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including assessments, projects and assignments preparation time)
general_details.Pre-Requisite: Passed ESL101, ELT401, ELI401, ERW421, EOB301
general_details.Description:
Objectives:

The course is designed to help students have the essential foundation of stones of language assessment with ample practical examples to illustrate application in language. Students will be able to develop assessment literacy by understanding, addressing issues and applying concepts.

Description:

The course introduces students to fundamental principles and tools for language assessment. Concepts are presented with practical, understandable explanations and concise references to supportive research.  Students can recognize different forms of testing and assessment and are equipped to design and evaluate practical, effective assessment techniques and apply them to classroom contexts. 

Teaching Methods: The teaching process includes various methods:

- Lecture the lessons and exercises varied from individuals, pair or group work, whole-class discussion.

- Guide students' learning with research, self-study with feedback.

- Have interactive discussions of questions and issues that may arise during lessons.

- Manage group work and enhance their interests in testing and assessments throughout the course.

Assessment scheme:  

1) On-going assessment: 100%                                              

- Progress test: 20%

- Assignment 1: 50%

- Assignment 2: 15%

- Assignment 3: 15%

2) Final Result: 100%                     

3) Completion Criteria:  

       a) On-going assessment >0, Each component >0

       b) Final Result >=5

Be responsible to do all exercises, and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time.

Participate actively in class discussions.

Use laptops in class only for learning purposes.

clos.LO Details:
Understand assessment concepts and issues
LO1.1 Understand differences between assessment and testing
LO1.2 Distinguish among five different types of language tests and apply them in different contexts
LO1.3 State primary current assessment issues
LO1.4 Appreciate historical antecedent and language assessment research.

Understand principles of language assessment
LO2.1 Understand the five major principles of language assessment and subcategories
LO2.2 Analyze the relative, variable importance of each principle
LO2.3 Apply each principle to classroom-based assessment instruments.

Design classroom language tests
LO3.1 Analyze the purpose of a proposed test 
LO3.2 State the specific abilities to be assessed 
LO3.3 Understand test specifications for a proposed test 
LO3.4 Design a variety of items (test methods) for a proposed test 
LO3.5 Administer a classroom test 
LO3.6 Construct a rationale for scoring, grading, and giving feedback on a proposed test.

Understand standards-based assessment
LO4.1 Understand the crucial role of standards in educational instruction and assessment
LO4.2 Examine a set of standards for a specified age, level, and context and apply them to contexts
LO4.3 Analyze the purpose, advantages, and disadvantages of standards-based assessment 
LO4.4 Apply principles of standardization to the construction of teacher-based standards.

Develop a standardized test
LO5.1 Appreciate the link between standards-based assessment and standardized testing 
LO5.2 Evaluate and adapt standardized tests 
LO5.3 Analyze the steps taken to perform a construct validation of a standardized test 
LO5.4 Examine constructs underlying various standardized language proficiency tests.

Design four skills assessments, including listening, speaking, reading, and writing
LO6.1 State a rationale for assessing each skill separately and with an integrated approach
LO6.2 Develop assessments that focus on one or several micro-and macro skills of each skill performance 
LO6.3 Design assessments that target one or several modes of each skill performance.

Design grammar and vocabulary assessments
LO7.1 State a rationale for treating form-focused assessment 
LO7.2 Discern, through the backdrop of the nature of grammar, the purposes and contexts for assessing grammatical knowledge 
LO7.3 Analyze the components of lexical ability and apply them to the assessment of vocabulary knowledge 
LO7.4 Design assessments that target one or several of the modes of performance.

Apply guidelines for assigning letter grades
LO8.1 Develop scoring rubrics to assess student performance and provide feedback
LO8.2 Evaluate that goes "beyond" letter grading.
Understand consideration of the ethnics of testing in an educational and commercial world driven by tests and respect in group work.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
-Objective: Upon the rapid growth of the meeting, expositions, events and conventions industry (MEEC), the subject is aimed to provide an introduction to the MEEC industry and an opportunity for the learner to describe, analyse and evaluate the resources required to organise an MEEC, basing on that to develop a full plan and to implement an event. 

-Description: It gives a comprehensive overview of the burgeoning field of planning and producing MEEC — meetings, expositions, events, and conventions with the study of varied segments of the field, along with discussions of new trends. 

-Teaching method: lecturing in combination with case study analysis, MEEC practice
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Meetings, Expositions, Events, and Conventions: An Introduction to the Industry
materials_table.Author: Fenich G. G.

clos.LO Details: To describe the profession and the structure of the MEEC industry
To critically identify the role and functions of each key player in the MEEC industry, including organisers, sponsors, DMOs, venues, contractors, destination management companies
To examine the use of facilities for meetings and conventions
To clarify the structure of and the organisation issues in the exhibition sector
To analyse different planning elements in MEEC industry, including food & beverage, legal issue, technology, green issue, international issues
To develop and implement a full plan for an MEEC of different aspects
To build a professional manner as an MEEC planner

general_details.Syllabus Name: Event management and operation_Vận hành và giám sát tổ chức sự kiện
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
-Main objective: The main aim of the coures is to train students in analyzing, marketing, planning and in successfully running a event.Therefore,The course provides an opportunity for students to involve with producing events followed the school academic structure. Students will learn the skills necessary to write a project proposal, realistic timelines, budgets and financial records, and create professional documentation; to practice interacting with the necessary support staff needed to produce events.

-Description: In the process, Students will be divided into 2 or 3 teams to run an event by their own concept. Students will meet with the instructor group by group and one by one throughout the course discussing production issues to ensure event completed step by step. 

-Teaching Method: Lecture, Project based learning, Cooperative Learning
general_details.StudentTasks:
Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Comply with the time and regulation

- Respect and protect school asset.  

- Strongly communication and teamworking.

clos.LO Details: Identify the event organization process; organizational structure, functions and tasks of the executive and event management department
Explain the steps in the process of operating and managing events;
Explain the process and principles of management of incidents and risk situations in the operation and management of events;
Plan, manage and organize meetings; Manage and use human resources to organize and organize events.
Supervise and manage activities at the event, personnel, budget, sponsors, partners;
Have a sense of discipline, professional manners and a high sense of responsibility at work; Flexibility in handling situations, ability to work independently and in groups.

general_details.Description:
- This course will provide students with essential knowledge and tips on starting a start-up efficiently and effectively.

- The course covers the most important aspects of modern entrepreneurship.

- Students will study by watching videos shared by prolific startup founders on various topics. Each week, there will be a face-to-face session with an instructor, typically a faculty lecturer of business administration experimented in entrepreneurship, who will re-cap and check on students' understanding of the week's main topic.

Students are grouped into teams of 4 to 6. Each team must be formed from at least 2 different majors.

- Each team will have to develop a startup idea and work on the project with guidance and support from instructors and mentors throughout the course.

- There will be seminars or workshops with guest speakers who are entrepreneurs  or venture capitalists, who will share their extensive experience and unique perspective in the entrepreneurial world of startups.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 85' practical exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Learn front-end web development for implementing a multi-platform solution:

- This subject introduces an overview of client-side web UI frameworks, in particular Bootstrap. The student will learn about grids and responsive design; Bootstrap CSS and JavaScript components; CSS preprocessors, Less and Sass. 

- The basics of Node.js and NPM and task runners like Grunt and Gulp.

- Explores Javascript based front-end application development, and in particular the React library: JavaScript ES6 for developing React application, Reactstrap for Bootstrap based responsive UI design, React components, React router and its use in developing single-page applications, designing controlled forms. 

- The student will be introduced to the Flux architecture and Redux. Explore various aspects of Redux and use it to develop React-Redux powered applications. 

- Use Fetch for client-server communication and the use of REST API on the server side.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Front-End web development with React_Phát triển web Front-End với React
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 85' practical exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Learn front-end web development for implementing a multi-platform solution:

- Overview of client-side web UI frameworks, focusing on Bootstrap. Students will explore grids, responsive design, Bootstrap CSS, and JavaScript components.
- Basics of Node.js, npm
- JavaScript-based front-end development with the React library: ES6 for React applications, Reactstrap for Bootstrap-based responsive UI, React components, React Router for single-page applications, and designing controlled forms.
- Hooks to leverage React features like state and lifecycle in functional components, reducing reliance on class components.
- Flux architecture and Redux, covering Redux principles and building React-Redux powered applications.
Fetch for client-server communication, integrating REST APIs on the server side.
- Modern syntax and patterns for ReactJS development, paired with foundational knowledge to ensure long-term relevance.
- AI Integration: Use of AI tools (e.g., code generation with GenAI) to enhance development efficiency, with emphasis on transparency and ethical usage.
- Assessment Methods: Evaluation through practical labs, assignments, and reviews using stratified sampling, scored via Likert scales (1-5) for syntax, logic, customization, and transparency, converted to a 10-point scale.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots to be eligible for the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises assigned by the instructor in class or at home and submitting them on time.
- Regularly check announcements on FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for the latest course updates, including assignment submission deadlines and feedback on assignments and project work.
-  AI-Related Task: Utilize AI tools (e.g., GenAI for code generation or debugging) responsibly in assignments and projects, and clearly document their usage (e.g., prompts, outputs) in submissions to ensure transparency and ethical application.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Financial modelling_Mô hình tài chính
general_details.Time Allocation: Online 49 hours+ 2 slots offline (optional)+108 hours self study
general_details.Description:
The Startup Valuation and Financial Analysis Specialization teaches two of the most often used methods to find the value of a startup. You’ll learn how to find the value of founder’s ownership before and after additional funding, how to read financial statements and make pro-forma statements, and how to determine the financial health and status of a startup and estimate future earnings and value. You’ll then use various investment criteria, such as Net Present Value (NPV) and Individual Rate of Return (IRR), to make a decision about whether and where to invest your money. 

Note: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus

general_details.Syllabus Name: Monetary Economics and Global Economy_Kinh tế tiền tệ và kinh tế toàn cầu
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: The course is an intermediate-level course in macroeconomics, including topics in international, monetary, and financial economics. The goal of the course is to provide a coherent framework for analyzing macroeconomic events, such as business cycles (recessions and booms) and long-run growth, their impact on financial markets, and to discuss macroeconomic policy. In all parts of the course, theories will be applied to current economic events. Particular emphasis will be placed on the relation between macroeconomic events and financial markets. Finishing this course, students will be well-versed in macroeconomic and finance areas, be able to realize the implications of real-life macroeconomic policy/ events on the global financial markets.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

This course is a follow-up to FIN202 and FIN303, in which students touch on fundamental concepts of finance in general and corporate finance in particular. After the theoretical foundation established in FIN202 and FIN303, students now have chance to acquire indepth knowledge about Derivatives valuation and investment strategies.  

Topics include: Futures and Forwards Valuation and Strategies, Option Valuation and Strategies, Swaps, Commodity Forwards and Futures, Financial Risk Management.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Front Office Operations and Management
general_details.Time Allocation: 30 sessions;  1 session= 90 minutes
general_details.Description: FRONT OFFICE OPERATIONS & MANAGEMENT introduces concepts of organization, communication, ethics and policy within a hotel. The primary focus is the front office, housekeeping, reservations and night audit departments and other departments are discussed to provide and understanding of how they relate to the front office. An introduction of basic analyses, techniques and trends in both policy and technology are reviewed, and the text gives students a “real world” understanding of the hotel industry balancing its past, present and future. Indepth coverage of The Property Management System is included and additional chapters feature analysis of the physical makeup of hotels, yield management, operational techniques, hotel guest and hotel employee
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Develop an organization chart depicting the functional relationships among hotel divisions and departments.

Explain the function and operation of the various systems, forms, equipment, and
computer applications found in the front office.
Construct an efficient reservation system that records crucial information while avoiding problems in processing various types of reservations.

Construct a registration system that helps ensure a hotel's profitability while meeting the needs of guests by using effective guestroom sales techniques and efficient credit establishment procedures.

Develop an efficient communication system to operate within the front office and between the front office and departments such as housekeeping and maintenance.. LO6. Develop procedures regarding hotel safety and security, with particular emphasis on key control and emergencies.
Develop procedures for handling complaints.
Follow basic hotel accounting procedures ranging from posting accounts to conducting cash and check transactions at the front desk.
Develop and follow check-out and settlement procedures.
Explain and perform the steps involved in the night audit process.

general_details.Description:
This course addresses the comprehension and application of Digital Forensic Investigations. Students will evaluate and synthesize technical and legal issues in relation to digital evidence. Students will apply various skills and techniques, combined with numerous investigative software tools to analyze seized electronic media. Students subject to background investigation prior to admittance.



Assessment scheme:

- Participation in Discussions:        10%

2) 01 Final Exam:                                30% 

3) Final Result                                   100%

Completion Criteria:  

1) Every on-going assessment component >0

2) Average Lab Score >= 4

3) Final Exam Score >=4 & Final Result  >=5

clos.LO Details: Defining Digital Forensics and examining how it’s being used.
Understanding the underlying technology powering cell phones and GPS units, as well as the potential evidence they could contain.
Understanding how computers create and store digital information is a perquisite for the study of digital forensics.
Examining digital forensic environment, hardware and software, and standards used on a regular basis, to accredit labs and validate tools.
Collecting digital evidence, establishing a chain of custody, and understanding its major role when admitted into court.
Understanding many of the common Windows artifacts and how they are created.
Examining tools and techniques used to hide or destroy data with the aim to recover digital evidence, deleted files, and the like.
Explaining the legal aspects of digital forensics in searching.
Understanding social networks, e-mail, chat logs, and Internet history representing some of the best evidence.
Understanding how networks are attacked and what role digital forensics plays in not only the response, but in how perpetrators can be traced.

general_details.Description:
This course provides students with knowledge of visual arts principles

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand basic design and visual rules to lay out the composition of art works

2. Analyze, evaluate the effect of design elements in each composition

4. Understand and apply 5 rules of design principles on contemporary artworks (Unity & Harmony, Balance, Scale & Proportion, Contrast & Emphasis, Rhythm)

4. Define the beauty of nature and analyze how it inspires designers to art works

5. Apply visual principles in doing excersises and making art works during career

6. Use drawing tools more effectively with both hand drawing and digital artworks.

6. Plan and organize visual products in the most effective way

general_details.Time Allocation:
Duration 15 weeks

Contact times: 15 times, 90 minutes/times x 1 times/w x 15 w = 22,5 hours (totally equivalent to 10 sessions for each group of students).

general_details.Pre-Requisite:
1. Passed on the job training (OJT). 
2. Pass 80% of total credits (PHE_COM* and  OJT excluded)
3. • Completed 3/4 subjects: GDS301, GDG401, GDW401, GDA401 or Completed 6/8 subjects: ANS301; ANT401; ANR401; ANA401; WDL301; WDT401; ADH301; ADT401.

• For K9 students: in order to choose Branding or Packaging as specialized graduated courses, the pre-requisite is Book and Packaging Design - ADG301
general_details.Description:
As the culminating course in the Graphic Design curriculum, CAPSTONE PROJECT is a comprehensive design course allowing students the opportunity to apply the combined understanding gained from earlier courses and projects to more fully realized work. 



Students will take a project from idea, concept to final design and presentation. Students work closely with the department head, interpreting a project brief and developing design elements. 



The project is executed in four stages with feedback and discussion at each stage. Students are expected to discuss, design, present, and critique their work with a high level of professionalism, and implement research strategies that contribute to the overall finished project.

- Meet with the instructor

- Implement assigned tasks

- Defend assigned tasks with the instructor and give presentation in front of a board of examiners

-  Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

Demonstrate proficiency In communication, presentation, and business skills necessary to engage In professional practice In graphic design including the ability to organize and manage design projects and to productively collaborate with others In a team. this competency is based on an understanding of organizational structures and working patterns In design, intellectual, economic, technological, and political contexts.

Main objectives:

Create a professional digital animation project following the design process: Research, define problems, reasons & goals, target audiences, competitors, define art directions, create moodboards, animation directions, scope of works, production timeline, throughout to the final products.

The final products must present strong aesthetic abilities, acting skills in animation following 12 principles of animations, editing & composing techniques. The final works should bring a certain meaning to the community.

Selected fields including: 2D Animated short film; 3D Animated short  film; Stop-motion film; mixed-media film; Game (if the student passed ANO301).

Students must work in a group. The number of members for each group, decided by the Head Academic of campus, could be variable from 2 to 3 students



The project is done in 4 stages with feedback and discussion at each stage. Students are expected to discuss, organise, present and critique their work with a high level of professionalism, and implement research strategies that contribute to the overall finished project

general_details.Description:
In order to remain competitive, hospitality organizations of today, in particularly highend hotels are very much focused on the “guest experience”. They are under high

pressure to deliver high service standards as today’s consumers are looking for more

value for their money. This course covers the topic of managing hospitality organizations by using academic studies and real life experiences from companies and is written in three sections: Strategy, Staffing and Systems. Each chapter includes at suggested hospitality activities for students, in which students are encourages to visit local organizations to talk with guests, employees and managers to obtain a variety of perspectives on the guest experience.

general_details.Description:
Main objectives:

'As a course within the Media and Communication curriculum, the Capstone Project is comprehensive, allowing students to apply the combined knowledge acquired from earlier courses and projects to the production of more fully-realized work. The main objectives of the course are to:

- Exhibit an advanced understanding of the relationship between media and communication;

- Exhibit an advanced understanding of the theories of humanities and social science;

- Create a self-project as a media and communication professional; 

- Develop personal/ team work on a professional level of quality;

- Construct professional media and communication practices;

- Demonstrate proficiency in communication, presentation, and the necessary skills for professional practice, such as the capacity to organise and manage projects as well as collaborate effectively with others. This competency requires knowledge of organisational structures and work patterns in the fields of economics, media, and communication.

Description: 

- This course requires real-work projects completed by a group of 3–5 students, each student must defend their contribution to the group project individually in front of a professional committee/examination board.

- Students are strongly encouraged to form groups and actively seek their supervisor(s), who will provide the necessary guidance as they develop their projects from initial concepts or ideas to completion.  

- By the completion, students are expected to acquire a comprehensive understanding and skills in the field of media and communication.



The project consists of Five (05) main phases:

(1) Research and development,

(2) Pre-implementation/Pre-production,

(3) Implementation/production, 

(4) Post-implementation/post-production, distribution (if applicable), and 

(5) Evaluation

Students are required to conduct 30% and 70% progress reports to present and defend their work in front of the Department's professional committees and supervisor(s). Students are expected to demonstrate a high level of professionalism when discussing, organising, presenting, and critiquing their work, as well as when implementing research strategies that contribute to the completion of the project in response to constructive feedback from supervisor(s) and professional committees.



Completion Criteria: 

- Progress on Project (04 reports): 20% 

- Final report/Production Book: 30%

- Oral Project Defense: 50%



Overall Final Project Mark: 100%

Mark of each report must be >= 4/10

Final Report/Production Book >= 4/10

Oral Project Defense >= 5/10

Final Report/Production Book must be submitted before deadline

general_details.Description:
-Objective:

The objective of the Graduation Thesis is to demonstrate students' profound knowledge and understanding of a specific topic in relation to Hospitality Management and relate it to a wider perspective, in a more practical business setting. 



Upon completion of the course, the student shall be able to: 

1. Demonstrate an ability to integrate knowledge and handle complexity, and to plan and carry out advanced tasks independently and as a group member, within specified time limits

2. Use appropriate research methodology to identify problems and suggest suitable, more sustainable solutions to those issues

3. Develop a more critical and creative thinking both theoretically and practically

4. Write, present and defend the thesis fulfilling academic criteria; correctly referencing relevant literature and other materials, which reflect the student’s academic and non-academic development throughout the whole process



-Description:

The Graduation Thesis is an integrative experience that brings together various components of the undergraduate marketing studies in a more applied setting and under a new perspective. It enables students to further their knowledge and skills in marketing and related topics which they have found to be especially interesting or beneficial to them.



As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the graduation thesis and gain an understanding of standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This thesis project will be completed by a group of 4-6 students, however each student will defend the thesis individually in front of a thesis committee. Each group of students will be supported by a supervisor, who will provide them with essential guidance in conducting a research, writing a thesis in a formal format and defending their arguments in front of the examination board. 



The thesis' topic should concern with the following areas: Hospitality and Customer Satisfaction, Tourism and Hospitality Marketing, Hospitality Management, Marketing and Service Quality Management, Foodservice Consumer Choice and Services Strategies, Strategic Management in the Hospitality Industry, Hospitality Marketing and Service Experience and Human Resource Management.

The Graduation Thesis is an integrative experience that brings together various components of the undergraduate international business studies in a more applied setting and under a new perspective. It enables students to further their knowledge and skills in international business and related topics which they have found to be especially interesting or beneficial to them.



As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the graduation thesis and gain an understanding of standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This thesis project will be completed by a group of 4-6 students, however each student will defend the thesis individually in front of a thesis committee. The thesis' topic  is concerned with such areas as (1) international business strategies, (2) contemporary issues of cross-cultural business management, (3) global entrepreneurship, (4) global human resource management - current practices and future trends, (5) FDI in Vietnam, (6) ethical issues in international business, (7) international trade in the current global geo-political landscape and (8) international business practices towards sustainability.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (500h) = 22.5 contact hours (90mins/slot x 15 slots) + 1.5h defense

+ 476h self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite:
1. Passed OJB202 (for Vietnamese students)
2. Passed 80% of total credits (PHE_COM*, OJB202 excluded for Vietnamese students, PHE_COM* excluded for intl. students)
3. Complete concentration courses (GPA>=4):
K14: MKT201, MKT202, MKT301, MKT304, MKT308
From K15: MKT201, MKT202, MKT301, MKT304, MKT318m/DMS301m, MKT328m/DMA301m
general_details.Description:
The Graduation Thesis is an integrative experience that brings together various components of the undergraduate marketing studies in a more applied setting and under a new perspective. It enables students to further their knowledge and skills in marketing and related topics which they have found to be especially interesting or beneficial to them.



As part of the course, students will learn about all aspects of the process of developing and carrying out the graduation thesis and gain an understanding of standards and expectations needed to successfully complete their dissertation. This thesis project will be completed by a group of 4-6 students, however each student will defend the thesis individually in front of a thesis committee. Each group of students will be supported by a supervisor, who will provide them with essential guidance in conducting a research, writing a thesis in a formal format and defending their arguments in front of the examination board. 



The thesis' topic  is concerned with such areas as (1) marketing mix analysis and solutions, (2) marketing channels, conflicts and distribution, (3) integrated marketing communications - analysis of campaigns or activities, (4) branding strategy, (5) new product development and innovation marketing, (6) ethics in marketing, (7) marketing in the services context and (8) contemporary issues in marketing in Vietnam.

This graduate business plan will be completed by a group of 4-6 students; however, each student will defend the business plan individually in front of an evaluation committee. The business plan's topic is concerned with such areas as (1) project background (2) market analysis, (3) value proposition (4) key activity plan, (5) financial analysis, (6)  Risk analysis and future roadmap.

general_details.Time Allocation:
1 session = 45 minutes

Total Course Time: 24 sessions in the classroom, 8 sessions for students to study by themself   

Interactive Classroom Teaching
general_details.Description: Cung cấp cho sinh viên những kiến thức cơ bản của Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về những vấn đề cơ bản của cách mạng Việt Nam. Nội dung gồm  8 chương: Chương mở đầu (nhập môn), chương 1:Cơ sở, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh. chương 2: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về vấn đề dân tộc và cách mạng giải phóng dân tộc, chương 3:Tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về chủ nghĩa xã hội và con đường quá độ lên chủ nghĩa xã hội ở Việt nam, chương 4:Tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về Đảng cộng sản Việt Nam, chương 5:Tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về đại đoàn kết dân tộc và đoàn kết quốc tế, chương 6:Tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về vấn đề dân chủ và xây dựng nhà nước của dân, do dân và vì dân, chương 7:Tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về văn hóa, đạo đức và xây dựng con người mới.
general_details.StudentTasks:
Phải có giáo trình tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh, dùng cho sinh viên Đại học và Cao đẳng khối không chuyên Mác- Lênin và tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh của Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo.               

Thực hiện đầy đủ các yêu cầu của giảng viên khi học trên lớp cũng như các chủ đề sinh viên tự chuẩn bị  trước khi đến lớp.

clos.LO Details: Nắm được hệ thống những nội dung cơ bản về tư tưởng, đạo đức, nhân văn và văn hóa Hồ Chí Minh. Cùng với môn học Những nguyên lý cơ bản của chủ nghĩa Mác-Lênin tạo lập những hiểu biết về nền tảng tư tưởng, kim chỉ nam hành động của Đảng và của cách mạng nước ta.
Góp phần xây dựng niềm tin, lý tưởng cách mạng cho sinh viên.
Từng bước xác lập thế giới quan, nhân sinh quan và phương pháp luận chung nhất để tiếp cận các khoa học chuyên ngành được đào tạo.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Thời gian học (100h) = 22.5 giờ học trên lớp (30 tiết) + 1 giờ thi cuối kỳ + 76.5 giờ tự học

Study hour (100h) = 22.5 contact hours (30 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 76.5 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
Giới thiệu môn học: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là kết tinh của truyền thống hàng nghìn năm dựng nước và giữ nước của dân tộc Việt Nam. Trên nền tảng đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đã gạn lọc các hạt giống trí tuệ của phương Đông, phương Tây, vận dụng sáng tạo và phát triển chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin vào điều kiện cụ thể của nước ta. Dưới góc độ triết học, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là hệ thống các quan điểm toàn diện, sâu sắc về những vấn đề cơ bản của cách mạng Việt Nam. Mục tiêu của tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là hướng tới giải phóng giai cấp, giải phóng dân tộc và giải phóng con người. Do đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đã trở thành tài sản tinh thần vô giá và là ngọn cờ dẫn dắt cách mạng Việt Nam đi từ thắng lợi này đến thắng lợi khác.

Course introduction: Ho Chi Minh ideology is the crystallization of the thousand-year-old traditions of national construction and defense of the Vietnamese people. On that basis, Ho Chi Minh ideology has collected intellectual values of absorbing Eastern, Western, creatively applied and developed Marxism-Leninism to Vietnamese practices. From a philosophical perspective, Ho Chi Minh's thought is a comprehensive and profound system of views on fundamental issues of the Vietnamese revolution. Its goal is aiming at class liberation, national liberation and human liberation. Therefore, Ho Chi Minh ideology has become precious spiritual asset and a torch leading the Vietnamese revolution to gain one victory to another.



Mục tiêu môn học:

- Cung cấp những hiểu biết có tính hệ thống về tư tưởng, đạo đức, giá trị văn hoá trong tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh.

- Tiếp tục cung cấp những kiến thức cơ bản về chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin.

- Cùng với môn học những nguyên lý cơ bản của chủ nghĩa Mác-Lênin tạo lập những hiểu biết về nền tảng tư tưởng, kim chỉ nam hành động của Đảng và của cách mạng nước ta.

- Góp phần xây dựng nền tảng đạo đức con người mới

Course objectives:

- Providing systematic understanding of ideology, morality, and cultural values in Ho Chi Minh's thought.

- Continuing to provide basic knowledge of Marxism – Leninism.

- Creating an understanding of the ideological foundation, action guideline for the Party and the revolution in Vietnam together with the subject The basic principles of Marxism - Leninism.

- Contributing to building ethical foundation of new human.



Nội dung môn học: Học phần Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh gồm có 6 chương cung cấp cho sinh viên kiến thức cơ bản về: Đối tượng, phương pháp nghiên cứu và ý nghĩa học tập môn học Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; về cơ sở, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; về độc lập dân tộc và chủ nghĩa xã hội; về Đảng Cộng sản và Nhà nước Việt Nam; về đại đoàn kết dân tộc và đoàn kết quốc tế; về văn hóa, đạo đức, con người

Phương pháp dạy học: Thuyết giảng và kết hợp trình chiếu các slide bài giảng. Hướng dẫn, giao bài tập đề tài theo nhóm. Tổ chức và hướng dẫn sinh viên thảo luận nhóm.

Content of the course: The module consists of 6 chapters providing students with basic knowledge of Object, research methods and meaningful learning of the course Ho Chi Minh ideology; of the basis and the process of formation and development of Ho Chi Minh ideology; of national independence associated with socialism; of the Communist Party and State of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; of the great unity bloc with international solidarity; of culture, ethics, people. 

Teaching method: Giving lectures and slide presentations. Guiding and assigning groupwork assignments. Organizing and guiding students to discuss in groups.

general_details.Description:
-Objective: To provide a basic understanding of the hospitality and tourism industry by tracing the industry's growth, development, issues facing, and future trends

-Description: The course addresses the tourism and hospitality industry's structure, scope, and measurement. The students will be exposed to the roles of industry business players and governments. This course addresses the knowledge and skill needed for students to understand the development of the hospitality and tourism industry and its challenges.
general_details.StudentTasks:

- Actively participate in class activities

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Lịch sử Mỹ thuật / Art History
general_details.Time Allocation: Thời gian học: 60 tiết. (1tiết = 45')
general_details.Description:
Qua môn học sinh viên được trang bị kiến thức về quá trình hình thành và phát triển của Mỹ thuật Việt Nam và Thế giới, Những kiến thức cơ bản về thành tựu và đặc điểm của mỹ thuật cổ đại, mỹ thuật Phục hưng, những trường phái mỹ thuật lớn góp phần làm thay đổi diện mạo của mỹ thuật cũng được đề cập đến trong môn học này. 

Giới thiệu những trung tâm mỹ thuật tiêu biểu của châu Á như: Ấn Độ, Trung Quốc, Nhật Bản,… tạo điều kiện để sinh viên có cái nhìn tổng quát về mỹ thuật thế giới, đặc biệt là những thành tựu mỹ thuật tiêu biểu.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Đọc sách giáo khoa và các tài liệu khác trước trước khi đến lớp

- Truy cập trang web của khóa học (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) cập nhật thông tin và các tài liệu của khóa học, hỗ trợ trực tuyến từ các giáo viên và các học sinh khác, và để thực hành và đánh giá.

- Tích cực tham gia hoạt động trong lớp 

- Hoàn thành tất cả các bài tập về nhà và các nhiệm vụ khác được đưa ra bởi giảng viên. 

- Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay cá nhân trong lớp cho mục đích học tập

- Không nói chuyện riêng, đến lớp muộn, nghe điện thoại, để chuông điện thoại, nhắn tin có thể phá vỡ môi trường học tập của lớp

- Tham dự hơn 80% giờ học để để đủ điều kiện tham gia kỳ kiểm tra cuối cùng.
general_details.Tools: Trường tạo điều kiện cho SV tham quan 02 bảo tàng về lịch sử và mỹ thuật của VN.

Sinh viên làm quen với kỹ năng làm việc nhóm, tìm hiểu, phân tích và thuyết trình về một vấn đề trong Lịch sử Mỹ thuật.

Sinh viên sẽ phát triển khả năng nhận biết, hiểu, phân tích, so sánh phong cách, ý nghĩa và mô tả tác phẩm nghệ thuật ở các thời kỳ khác nhau thông qua kiến thức được học và các buổi thực tế tại bảo tàng, di tích lịch sử.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Art History_Lịch sử mỹ thuật VN &TG
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course provides knowledge of Art History: Through the course of Art History, students are equipped with the knowledge of the establishment circumstances, the development process, the specialties of the arts and famous artists of the World and Vietnam Fine Arts from primitive to modern.

The course also introduces typical art centers in Asia such as India, China and Japan to help students have an overview of the world's fine arts, especially outstanding artistic achievements. . .... 



This course also provides some basic skills such as research methods, critical thinking, and mind mapping in the study of art history. In addition, this subject requires teamwork skills, oral presentation and paint skills in the process of assessment.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: (Basic Knowledge) Summarize the development process of Art History; Identify and describe the major holdings related to fine art style and movement, avant-garde artists.
(Research Skills) -  Understand the context of the major styles and movements in Art History, in relation to socio-cultural, economic, political, religious..., talented and avant-garde artists.
(Critical Thinking) Analyze and evaluate critically the meanings and descriptions of works of art from different periods of the past in Art  History.
(Communication Skills): Study optional cases in Art  History, organize and express the individual thoughts clearly and coherently both in orally (presentations) and writing (assignments/essays).
Be aware of what is aesthetics of visual art and understand the stages of aesthetic awareness in art history
Evaluate manual and/or digital art works, media and materials appropriately to produce creative ways solutions for specific cultural and technical contexts.
Having a professional style in arts activity. Love to research in art history.
Students have a proficient in presentation and teamworks.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Design history_Lịch sử thiết kế
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (100h)

= 22.5h contact hours + 1h final exam + 76.5h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course provides knowledge of Design History: The milestones of achievements in Design History with understanding of contexts; The relationship between design history and the development of technical capabilities, materials, and other social issues; The information of representative designers, characteristics of design styles and movements. 



This course also provides some basic skills such as research methods, critical thinking, and mind mapping in the study of design history. In addition, this subject requires teamwork skills, oral presentation and writing skills in the process of assessment.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

 - Actively participate in class activities 

 - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

 - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

 - Read the textbook in advance 

 - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

materials_table.MaterialDescription: The Story of Design from the Paleolithic to the Present
materials_table.Author: Charlotte and Peter Fiell

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Graphic Design Referenced - A visual guide to the language, applications, and history of graphic design
materials_table.Author: Bryony Gomez - Palacio and Armin Vit

clos.LO Details: (Basic Knowledge) Summarize the development process of Design History; Identify and describe the main stakes concerned with design styles and movements.

(Research Skills) Understand the contexts of the main styles and movements in Design History, which related to important inventions in manufacture, significant events on the market, talented and pioneering designers.
(Critical Thinking) Analyze and evaluate critically the records of the past in Design History.
(Communication Skills): Study optional cases in Design History, organize and express the individual thoughts clearly and coherently both in orally (presentations) and writing (assignments/essays).

general_details.Description:
This course is an introduction to the fundamentals of ethical hacking. 

Students will learn how hackers attack computers and networks, and how to protect Windows and Linux systems. 

Legal restrictions and ethical guidelines will be taught and enforced. 

Students will perform many hands-on labs, both attacking and defending, using port scans, footprinting, buffer overflow exploits, SQL injection, privilege escalation, Trojans, and backdoors.

general_details.Description:
The digital landscape is evolving at an unprecedented rate with unknown threats lurking around every corner. Cybersecurity resilience in the modern world cannot be just an addon - it's a necessity. Organizations must build cybersecurity resilience, and offensive security professionals like Ethical Hackers and Penetration Testers can help proactively discover unknown threats and address them before cybercriminals do.

Target Audience This course is designed to prepare learners with the Ethical Hacker skillset. Learners will become proficient in the art of scoping, executing, and reporting on vulnerability assessments, while recommending mitigation strategies. By using an engaging gamified narrative throughout the course, with real-world inspired hands-on practice labs, learners develop essential workforce readiness skills to lay a solid foundation in offensive security.

After completing this course, learners can enter cybersecurity careers, either on the offensive security side as ethical hackers or penetration testers, or on the defensive security side by understanding the mindset and tactics of threat actors, while implementing security controls and monitoring, analyzing, and responding to current security threats.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Hotel Operations Management_Quản trị vận hành khách sạn
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
- Main objective: This course provides an overview of the operations of a mid-size full-service hotel, from lodging to food and beverage, marketing and sales, human resources,... The focus of this course will be on explaining the functions of each department in a hotel, the inter-relationships among them, and management skills development. This course offers up-to-date information of multiple aspects in hotel operations, and essential insights for future hotel managers.

-Description: Hotel operational management introduces an overview of thel operation and organization of a midsize hotel. The course focuses on the front office, housekeeping, F&B and how they relate to each other in order to provide excellent service to customers. Other departments are also explained to provide a full understanding of the organization of a hotel.  Students are to practice their analyzing and problem solving skills with up-to-date real life example and current trends. 

-Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, roleplay, project based learning, group work
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

general_details.Syllabus Name: Hotel Revenue Management_Quản trị doanh thu khách sạn
general_details.Time Allocation: Online: 58 hours+ 2 slots offline (optional)+109 hours self study
general_details.Description:
This Specialization covers the basics of hotel demand management, distribution, and revenue management. You’ll learn how e-commerce intermediaries such as online travel agencies are impacting the already-complex hospitality sector, and you’ll explore tools and techniques that will help you effectively market hospitality services and maximize business revenue in this new global industry landscape. In the final Capstone Project, you’ll evaluate the importance of hotel branding in business success through a hands-on, real-world case study. During the sessions, you will hear from senior hotel industry executives commenting on distribution, revenue and demand management issues. We will also interview two leading Online Travel Agents on how to maximise online business for your property, and have partnered with Duetto and SnapShot, two leading hospitality industry companies, to gain access to cutting edge knowledge, thus insuring that the competencies that you gain will make you operational immediately as well as bang up to date on industry trends.

Note: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.
general_details.StudentTasks: Access the specialization on Coursera and complete all courses' requirements to earn a certificate of completion for the specialization, in order to be qualified for the Final Exam.

general_details.Description:
Main objective: This course provides students the understanding of the various approaches, design and strategies for achieving operational success in major service sectors such as health care, technical support services, banking and financial services, transportation; yet mainly focus on  restaurants, hotels and resorts.

-Description: The course addresses strategic analysis and operational decision making in mananing a service bussiness. The course illustrate the steps of creating the service concept and operations strategy, the design of effective service delivery systems, quality management and improvement which ensure operational competitiveness in service businesses.

-Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, roleplay, project based learning, group work.

general_details.Description:
This specialization provides a robust introduction to the key principles, policies, and practices of human resource management. The specialization begins with a foundational course that considers alternative approaches to managing human resources, provides a background to the U.S. legal context in which employees are hired, fired, rewarded, and managed, and outlines the different reasons that people are motivated to work. The remaining three courses tackle three core areas that all managers should understand: hiring employees, evaluating their performance, and rewarding them. Throughout the courses, an accessible, scientific approach is embraced such that best practices and practical tips are informed by research, but presented in accessible, applied ways. 

Upon completing the specialization, learners will have a deeper understanding of what works in the workplace, including a toolkit of best practices for hiring, managing, and rewarding employees.

general_details.Description:
This course is derived from the Coursera Specialization "HRIC Human Resource Associate Professional Certificate." 



Human Resource (HR) professionals are crucial to an organization's success, playing an essential role in recruitment and management of right candidates and talents, policy development, and fostering a positive work environment. Pursuing a career in HR enables individuals to significantly contribute to an organization's overall achievements.



This program is meticulously designed to prepare aspiring HR professionals. It encompasses five modules, offering a diverse array of engaging videos, interactive activities, assessments, and peer-reviewed projects aimed at enhancing professional expertise and providing a comprehensive understanding of Human Resource Management (HRM) fundamentals.



Upon completion of this program, students will understand how to:



- Recruit, select, and onboard new employees effectively.

- Develop and implement employee policies and procedures that align with organizational objectives.

- Foster a positive work culture and enhance employee engagement.

- Understand and navigate legal and ethical considerations in HR.



Graduates of this program will receive a certificate from Coursera and gain the requisite knowledge and skills to excel in the HR field. Additionally, they will be prepared to undertake the HRCI Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR) certification exam, distinguishing themselves as qualified HR professionals.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Risk Management in Information Systems_Quản trị rủi ro trong hệ thống thông tin
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
The course provides a comprehensive view of managing risk in information systems.

It covers the fundamentals of risk and risk management and also includes in-depth details on more comprehensive risk management topics.

Areas of instruction include how to assess and manage risk based on defining an acceptable level of risk for information systems. Elements of a business impact analysis (BIA), business continuity plan (BCP), disaster recovery plan (DRP) and computer incident response team (CIRT) plan are also discussed.

- Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Promptly access at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

b) Final examination: 40%

- Final Exam Score >=4 & Final Result  >=5

general_details.Syllabus Name: Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering_Phân tích mã độc và kỹ thuật dịch ngược
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Information Assurance (IA) is a primary example of a field that can benefit greatly from malware analysis. IA aims to protect and defend information and information systems by ensuring their confidentiality, integrity, authentication, availability, and nonrepudiation. This is mostly based on designing measures that would ensure the protection of such systems and their associated data. This makes malware analysis an essential component of IA.

     This course provides students with an effective immersion into the realm of Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering. It follows a progressive approach that introduces relevant concepts and techniques while preparing students to become effective malware analysts that can use a standard methodology for detecting, analyzing, reverse engineering and eradicating malware.

     Some of the key aspects of this course include reverse engineering malware from various sources and using various programming languages, including Web-based languages such as JavaScript as well as Document-based ones such as VBScript. This is accomplished by using a standard methodology that involves setting up an inexpensive laboratory, isolating it from production environments, and utilizing a selected set of forensic tools in order to dissect the malware, discover its characteristics, and neutralize its effects.

     Scope: The scope of this course includes:

          1. Introduction to Malware Analysis.

          2. Malware Analysis Labs

          3. Methodology to detect, analyze, reverse-engineer, and eradicate malware.

          4. Malware Analysis Applications.

          5. Forensics tools used for Malware Analysis.

     Course Objectives: This course will equip students with the necessary background knowledge in order to become effective Malware Analysis & Reverse Engineering practitioners.

clos.LO Details: Develop a good understanding of Malware Analysis: today’s greatly increasing malware threats, malware activity mechanism and behavior, malware classification, building an environment to do static and dynamic malware analysis, methods and tools to detect, analyze, reverse-engineer, and eradicate malware.

Identify the different types of Malware Analysis methods: static (ASCII, binary, logical signature detection), dynamic (network traffic analysis, memory forensics, dynamic reverse engineering) and hybrid.

Gain a broad exposure to real world applications of Malware Analysis: take control of the incident, incident response, analyze the threat, examine interactions with the environment, mitigate the risks of malware attempting to escape from the lab,
Set up a relatively inexpensive lab for Malware Analysis activities.
Utilize a standard methodology for detecting, analyzing, reverse engineering, and eradicating malware.
Use a Malware Analysis-based approach in order to resolve real world problems.
Recognize common malware characteristics: propagation, infection, self-defense, capabilities, etc.
Bypass some of the advanced malware techniques, such as packing, obfuscation and anti-analysis of armored malware breeds.

general_details.Description:
This course provides an overview of security challenges and strategies of countermeasure in the information systems environment. Topics include definition of terms, concepts, elements, and goals incorporating industry standards and practices with a focus on availability, vulnerability, integrity, and confidentiality aspects of information systems.

Major Instructional Areas 

1. Information Systems Security fundamentals

2. Seven domains of a typical Information Technology (IT) infrastructure

3. Risks, threats, and vulnerabilities found in a typical IT infrastructure

4.Security countermeasures for combating risks, threats, and vulnerabilities commonly found in an ITare infrastructure

5. (ISC)2 Systems Security Certified Practitioner (SSCP®) Common Body of Knowledge – SSCP® domains 

6. Six domains of the CompTIA Security+ certification

clos.LO Details: Explain the concepts of information systems security (ISS) as applied to an IT infrastructure.
Assess the current methods of business communications today and the associated risks and threats.
Describe how malicious attacks, threats, and vulnerabilities impact an IT infrastructure.
Explain the role of access controls in implementing a security policy.
Explain the role of operations and administration in effective implementation of security policy
Explain the importance of security audits, testing, and monitoring to effective security policy.
Explain how businesses apply cryptography in maintaining information security.
Understand malicious attacks, threats, and vulnerabilities and explain the means attackers use to compromise systems and networks and defenses used by organizations.
Use international and domestic information security standards and compliance laws in real-world applications in both the private and public sector.
