clos.LO Details:
Arrange and tell a story about their work in their portfolio in an advanced level of craftsmanship in a way that represents a distinct and personal point-of-view.
Combine the knowledge of how to best discuss their work in their portfolio, along with their design process and design philosophy.
Know what an employer is looking for in entry-level design positions.
Apply the criteria of page layout; grid, composition, balance, and unity to a portfolio of work in both printed and digital media.
Construct a basic portfolio of work in an online/digital environment and other networks.
Compose a compelling, well-written, grammatically correct Business Package including resume, cover letter, business card, and printed and online portfolio.
Actively discuss, critique, and engage in professional reviews of their own and their peers’ works.

general_details.Description:
- Knowledge about programming language has become an essential part of an education in computer science because the realization of ideas, approaches, models, and algorithms is extremely important for the field of education and research as well as production. In order to deploy from an idea to a product, programming language tools are required.

- In recent years, python has emerged as a popular, powerful, multitasking and widely applicable 3rd generation language, especially in some new technology fields such as AI, Fintech, Data Science, IoT, and so on.

general_details.Description: Project managers play a key role in leading, planning and implementing critical projects to help their organizations succeed. In this course, students’ll discover foundational project management terminology and gain a deeper understanding of  the role and responsibilities of a project manager. They’ll gain an immersive understanding of the practices and skills needed to succeed in an entry-level project management role; learn how to create effective project documentation and artifacts throughout the various phases of a project. They will know the foundations of Agile project management, with a focus on implementing Scrum events, building Scrum artifacts, and understanding Scrum roles. Student’s also have a chance to practice strategic communication, problem-solving, and stakeholder management through real-world scenarios.

general_details.Time Allocation: Online:  55 hours+5 slot offline
general_details.Description:
This course will help students master the skills of designing and building cloud-native applications on AWS. They will be introduced to several AWS compute services, different storage and database offerings that AWS provides, AWS’ networking capabilities, monitoring capabilities and the AWS IAM service; how to build an API driven application using Amazon API Gateway for serverless API hosting, AWS Lambda for serverless computing and Amazon Cognito for serverless authentication. 



Modern applications require a modern database. Hence, they will dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB topics such as recovery, SDKs, partition keys, security and encryption, global tables, stateless applications, streams, and best practices. DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale.



Finally, students’ll learn how to use Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer to detect issues and identify recommendations to improve the quality and security of your code.

= 66h online + 3h offline + 1h final exam + 80h self-study
general_details.Description:
This professional certificate provides the knowledge and skills you need to start building your career in cloud architecture and helps you prepare for the AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate exam. You will start by learning key AWS Services for compute, storage, database, networking, monitoring, and security, then dive into how to design architectural solutions, how to create and operate a data lake, and how to prepare for the certification exam.



In Cloud Technical Essentials course, you’ll design a 3-tier architecture using services like Amazon VPC, Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS with high availability and Elastic Load Balancing following AWS best practices. You’ll upload an architecture diagram laying out your design including the networking layer.



In Architecting Solutions on AWS course, you’ll use Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, Amazon SQS, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon SNS to build a serverless web backend.



In Introduction to Designing Data Lakes course, you’ll use Amazon S3, Amazon OpenSearch Service, AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway to create an Amazon OpenSearch Service Cluster. You’ll also use Amazon S3, Amazon EC2, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics, Amazon Elasticsearch Service to create a data ingestion pipeline with the use of high-scale AWS Managed services. 



Finally, we present content on all four knowledge domains that are covered in the exam. It's important to understand that on the exam, questions from all domains are presented in random order.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Type: Individual  Report

Length: 3,000 words including references or indented quotes

Task Description:

The critical essay is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of effective public relations by analysing a key development, change or issue applied to the field of PR and professional communication. 

Students will choose a topic, from the list provided, or they may provide a detailed topic of their own to be cleared in writing by the lecturer. The topics are intended to justify some of the themes covered in the course and provide them with the opportunity to gain their knowledge and examine how their topic impacts on society, publics, consumers and professional practice.

Notes: 

Students should provide clear illustrations/examples

 in their essay to show their understanding of the topic. 

All topics are written as a draft. Lecturers have the privilege to change the content of each topic as much as they want. 

Choose one from the following essay topics:



Topic 1:  Examine Public Relations best practices for going viral and generating UGC (User-generated content)

Research and critically analyse the use of the words “viral” and “UGC” in this context, providing illustrations and academic support for your argument.  

Topic 2: Examine the differences between Advertising campaign and Public Relations campaign.

Additionally, in your analysis consider whether Public Relations has been driven by the Advertising industry. 

Topic 3: Examine the role of Public Relations in social change

Research and critically analyse the use of the words “social change” in this context, providing illustrations and academic support for your argument.  

Topic 4: Students may write their own topic accepted by their lecturer. It must be at a level ‘equal’ to the topics provided.

Note: Students must not submit an essay on an alternative topic that has not been cleared.
assessments.Note: The essay topics should be updated or different at least 30% to the previous ones.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Grading Guide:
Type: Group Project

Including: Written Report/ Proposal + Presentation

Task Description:

Students assume they are working for a public relations agency and responsible for creating a public relations campaign, which must include a realistic strategy for a real-life organization’s product, service or NGO issue/cause.

Students will design, develop and evaluate a campaign for a “real” client. They will meet the client face-to-face, take a brief and be tasked with developing industry-ready materials for a public relations campaign.

Or students will be provided with a list of current issues, and organisations linked to or impacted by those issues. From the list, they will select one issue and one organization to take care of.

Or Students can make an event for a NGO (Combo 2)

A campaign proposal for the client must include at least: 

(1) Executive Summary

(2) Situation Analysis

(3) Target Audience and key stakeholders 

(4) Goal

(5) Objectives

(6) Key Messages

(7) Strategies and Tactics

Including communication tools: electronic/interactive media kit (ex: news releases, photographs, glossaries, fact sheets, FAQs, executive profiles, videos), brochures, digital media platforms (ex: blogs, social media, newsletter, magazine, etc.); print (posters, fliers, etc.), events and other promotional materials and elements

(8) Risk Analysis 

(9) Budget 

(10) Evaluation 



Execution phase can be PR materials, event... 

Notes: 

Students are required to:

1. Obtain formal approval from their lecturer for the selected topic before starting the assignment.

2. Utilize AI tools in PR content creation.

3. Note that while AI tools may be used to produce PR content:

•	Students must acknowledge all AI-generated information in their reports.

•	Students must demonstrate their ability to produce PR content independently if required.

•	The use of AI tools is required but will not be graded separately; the quality of their completed work will be assessed as a whole.

•	The final assessment will be based on the lecturer's provided rubric.



Students should illustrate excellent knowledge of public relations theories and how they can be applied. Critical skills in planning and execution of a public relations campaign also must be showed. 

To broaden the knowledge of various PR functions, students may choose one of the dimensions of PR activities: corporate PR, branding PR activities, personal PR, etc.
assessments.Note:
Students are strongly advised to carefully review all outputs from AI tools. They must also be able to produce PR content independently if required. Students' completed works will be assessed according to a rubric provided by the lecturer



The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

clos.LO Details: Understand and apply fundamental concepts in C/C++ programming, including C/C++ keywords, variable types, Lvalues and Rvalues, operators, strings, arrays, and pointers.
Implement decision-making constructs (if-else, switch), loops (for, while, do-while), and modify program flow using control flow keywords (break, continue, goto).
Define, declare, and implement functions in C/C++, using modular programming techniques such as recursion, function pointers, and parameter passing.

Understand and apply object-oriented programming (OOP) principles like encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. Use pointers, references, dynamic memory allocation, and smart pointers in C++ for efficient memory management. Avoid memory leaks and dangling pointers while working with classes, constructors, destructors, templates, and exceptions.
Open, read, write, and close files using C/C++ file handling functions and streams. Distinguish between binary and text file formats and perform random access operations.

general_details.Description:
The course is Designed to enhance the practical ability of Students. In each session, There are 2 parts of the lecture will be delivered. The theoretical part, given in the form of short-slide, which only focus on the introduction and the key-ideas. The paractical part are given in form of the classworks (exercise in class) will help students understand the introduced topic by a practical approach. During the course, students will learn based on an assignment (given in the form of individual project). Student will decide the topic of the assignment under the supervision of the lecturer. The classworks provide the basic knowledge for the students. Students must investigate them-self and discuss with lecturer to complete the assignment.

Beside the assignment (here we consider as long-homework) , there are few given workshops (short-homework). The workshops aim to help the lecturer to evaluate the learning progress of students. Based on that stackholders can recognize the shortcomings of skills and knowledge of the students.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Basis Cross-Platform Application Programming With .NET_Lập trình ứng dụng đa nền tảng cơ bản với .NET
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 49.5h contact hours + 1h final exam + 85' practical exam + 99.5h self-study
general_details.Description:
Upon completion of this course students should: 

1. Understand the followings:

   • C# language for developing .NET applications;

   • Fundamental concepts of .NET Platform

   • Basic knowledge of  Window Forms in .NET 

   • Basic knowledge of  ASP.NET Core MVC

   • Basic knowledge of  RESTful API .NET

2. Be able to:

   • Develop Cross-platform Desktop applications and support for user experience ( UI & UX )

   • Develop Back-end  applications by ASP.NET Core Web API

   • Develop Distributed applications by Windows Forms and REST APIs 

   • Develop Distributed applications by ASP.NET MVC Core and REST APIs 

3. Be able to work in a team and present group's results
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all assigned exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Visual Studio.NET 2019 version 16.8.3 or later 

- MS SQL Server 2014 or later

- Platform : .NET 5.0 or later

Demonstrate about ASP.NET Core MVC and Back-end applicaiton with RESTful API

general_details.Syllabus Name: Advanced Cross-Platform Application Programming With .NET_Lập trình ứng dụng đa nền tảng nâng cao với .NET
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 49.5h contact hours + 1h final exam +  85' practical exam + 99.5h self-study
general_details.Description:
Upon completion of this course students should: 

1. Understand the followings:

   • Apply C# language for developing Desktop and Web applications;

   • Fundamental concepts of .NET Core Platform

   • Basic knowledge of  Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) and ASP.NET Core Razor Page application

   • Basic knowledge of  RESTful API .NET , Signal-R and apply into ASP.NET Core application

   • Basic knowledge of Asynchronous and Parallel Programming in .NET Core application

   • Basic knowledge of  Dependency Injection apply into .NET Core applications

   • Basic knowledge of  Worker Service and apply to implement Background Tasks

2. Be able to:

  • Develop Cross - platform Web applications by ASP.NET Core Razor Page  

  • Develop Cross - platform Desktop applications by WPF  and support for user experience ( UI & UX )

  • Implement  Real-time applications by Signal R and ASP.NET Core

  • Implement Background Tasks with Worker Service 

3. Be able to work in a team and present group's results
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all assigned exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Visual Studio.NET 2019 version 16.8.3 or later 

- MS SQL Server 2014 or later

- Platform :  .NET 5.0 or later

general_details.Syllabus Name: Building Cross-Platform Back-End Application With .NET_Xây dựng ứng dụng back-end với With .NET
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 49.5h contact hours + 1h final exam +  85' practical exam + 99.5h self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite: PRN221 ( BUILDING CROSS-PLATFORM WEB APPLICATION WITH .NET )
general_details.Description:
Upon completion of this course students shoud: 

1. Understand the followings:

• Apply C# language for develop ASP.NET WEB API ( RESTful Service applications )  

• Fundamental concepts of .NET Core Platform

• Basic knowledge of  ASP.NET WEB API on .NET Core

• Basic knowledge of  RESTful Service and Microservice architecture

2. Be able to:

• Develop Cross - platform Back-end application can be used by  Desktop or Web applications (Cross - platform)

• Develop RESTful Service applications by ASP.NET Web API  and Windows Communication Foundation (WCF)  

• Implement  security in the ASP.NET WEB API

• Implement sending Ajax request to  ASP.NET WEB API 

• Implement security  JWT  in ASP.NET Core Web API

• Develop Distributed applications based on Microservice architecture

3. Be able to work in team and present group's results
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all assigned exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_details.Tools:
- Internet

- Visual Studio.NET 2019 version 16.8.3 or later 

- Platform : .NET 5.0 or later

general_details.Description:
Upon completion of this course students shoud: 
1. Understand the followings:
• Apply C# language for develop ASP.NET WEB API ( RESTful Service applications )  
• Fundamental concepts of .NET Core Platform
• Basic knowledge of  ASP.NET WEB API on .NET Core
• Basic knowledge of  RESTful Service and Microservice architecture
2. Be able to:
• Develop Cross - platform Back-end application can be used by  Desktop or Web applications (Cross - platform)
• Develop RESTful Service applications by ASP.NET Web API  and Windows Communication Foundation (WCF)  
• Implement  security in the ASP.NET WEB API
• Implement sending Ajax request to  ASP.NET WEB API 
• Implement security  JWT  in ASP.NET Core Web API
• Develop Distributed applications based on Microservice architecture
3. Be able to work in team and present group's results

general_details.Time Allocation:
Contact time: 13 sessions 

1 session = 90'
general_details.Description: Alice is an innovative 3D programming environment that makes it easy to create an animation for telling a story, playing an interactive game, or a video to share on the web. Alice is a freely available teaching tool designed to be a student's first exposure to object-oriented programming. It allows students to learn fundamental programming concepts in the context of creating animated movies and simple video games. In Alice, 3-D objects (e.g., people, animals, and vehicles) populate a virtual world and students create a program to animate the objects

general_details.Syllabus Name: C# Programming and Unity _Lập trình C# và Unity
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course based on the C# Programming for Unity Game Development Specialization at https://www.coursera.org/specializations/programming-unity-game-development. 

The course is all about starting to learn how to develop video games using the C# programming language and the Unity game engine on Windows or Mac. C# is a really good language for learning how to program and then programming professionally. Also, the Unity game engine is very popular with indie game developers; Unity games were downloaded 16,000,000,000 times in 2016! Finally, C# is one of the programming languages you can use in the Unity environment.



This course doesn't assume students have any previous programming experience. Students will start at the very beginning and work our way up to building small games by the end of the course. Throughout the course student'll learn core programming concepts that apply to lots of programming languages, including C#, and also learn how to apply those concepts when you develop games.

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

general_details.Description: This comprehensive Basic Unity Training Program is designed to equip participants with essential skills in Unity game development. Starting from the fundamentals of Unity interface and scripting in C#, the course progresses to cover advanced topics such as physics, animations, and user interface design. Through a combination of lectures, hands-on labs, and real-world projects, participants will gain practical experience and confidence in using Unity for game development.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Object-Oriented Programming for Unity Games _Lập trình hướng đối tượng cho Unity Games
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course is a course that builds on the knowledge included in the C# Programming for Unity Game Development Specialization, so the course assumes you have the prerequisite knowledge from the PRU211m. You should make sure you have that knowledge, either by taking those previous courses or from personal experience, before tackling this course. You should make sure you have that knowledge, either by taking those courses or from personal experience, before tackling this course. Throughout this course you'll build on your foundational C# and Unity knowledge by developing more robust games with better object-oriented designs using file input and output, inheritance and polymorphism, event handling and various data structures and design patterns.

Data structures and design patterns are both general programming and software architecture topics that span all software, not just games. Although we'll discuss these ideas in the game domain, they also apply if you're writing a web app in ASP.NET, building a tool using WinForms, or any other software you decide to build.

general_details.Description:
- Môn học sẽ được triển khai trong xưởng thực hành với đầy đủ về yêu cầu về dụng cụ học tập cho môn học.

- Môn học này giúp SV nắm được các nguyên tắc cơ bản về hình chiếu phối cảnh, bóng đổ và phương pháp dựng hình. Thông qua hệ thống lý thuyết và bài tập thực hành trên lớp giúp sinh viên hiểu và vận dụng được hình chiếu phối cảnh để biểu diễn một vật thể hay cảnh vật trong không gian ba chiều lên mặt phẳng hai chiều trong thiết kế đồ họa.

- Bài làm của từng sinh viên sau mỗi bài tập sẽ được Giảng viên và sinh viên trong lớp cùng nhận xét, đánh giá. Giảng viên chấm điểm đánh giá cuối cùng ngay trên lớp.

- Trong quá trình học sinh viên được hướng dẫn bài làm, lưu giữ và tạo Portfolio.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Đọc sách giáo khoa và các tài liệu trước khi đến lớp.

- Làm và hoàn thành bài thực hành trên lớp

- Truy cập trang web của khóa học (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) cập nhật thông tin và các tài liệu của khóa học, hỗ trợ trực tuyến từ các giáo viên và các học sinh khác, và để thực hành và đánh giá.

- Tích cực tham gia hoạt động trong lớp: trao đổi, làm việc nhóm, làm bài thực hành,...

- Hoàn thành tất cả các bài tập về nhà và các nhiệm vụ khác được đưa ra bởi giảng viên. 

- Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay cá nhân trong lớp cho mục đích học tập

- Không nói chuyện riêng, đến lớp muộn, nghe điện thoại, để chuông điện thoại, nhắn tin có thể phá vỡ môi trường học tập của lớp.

- Tham dự từ 80% giờ học để để đủ điều kiện thihojc kỳ.

general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: Perspective is a subject that helps students draw third dimention objects on a flat surface like the image when we look at the object in real life.  Perspective drawing is concerned with achieving a sense of space, of depth and of the third dimension, within the limits of the flat drawing surface. Students can use the rules of perspective in sketching, finding ideas and creativity in designing.For those concerned with freehand perspective is provided all the important printciples, insights and "shortcuts" necessary for effective drawing and life sketching. Essentially, perspective drawing deals with this appearance of things, i.e., with how three dimensional reality "look" and how it is best drawn on two dimensional surface as a canvas, sketch pad, or illustration board.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

materials_table.Author: John Montague

clos.LO Details: Understand the basic rules, concept of perspective

Understand How we see for perspective drawing and Why appearance differs from reality theory, concept of Picture plane, Cone of Vision
 Understand concept of Vanishing points and eyes level, how to find vanishing point, eyes level on the picture plane, vanishing point of specical lines.

Classify types of perspective: One point perspective, two point perspective, three point perspective. Understand and be able to draw one, two, three points perspective of objects with the determined size
Know about concept and application of four, five, six, perspective
Classify shade and shadow.Be able to draw shade and shadow of objects with sunlight source and Local point Sources of light to draw pictures.
Understand concept of Reflection. Be able to draw water, mirror reflections of perspective drawing

Understand Method of perspective sketching , such as:
- Draw perspective of objects from simple shape. 
 -How to determine heights, depths and widths of objects in perspective
-Use Diagonals to divide to equal spacing and determine the center point of objects
-Dividing a Surface into Unequal Space and  Equal Space by using a measuring line and special vanishing point.
Apply perspective drawing methods to draw sketches.
Having a positive attitude and a professional working style

general_details.Syllabus Name: Reinforcement Learning_Học tăng cường
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study;
general_details.Description: This course helps students understand the concepts of Reinforcement Learning including the space of RL algorithms (Temporal- Difference learning, Monte Carlo, Sarsa, Q-learning, Policy Gradients, Dyna, and more). Students will understand how to formalize these tasks as a Reinforcement Learning problem. Students will learn how RL fits under the broader umbrella of machine learning, and how it complements deep learning, supervised and unsupervised learning. Students can implement a complete RL solution and understand how to apply AI tools to solve real-world problems.
general_details.StudentTasks:
'- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

clos.LO Details: Understand the concepts of Reinforcement Learning
Know how to implement dynamic programming as an efficient solution approach to an industrial control problem
Understand several algorithms for estimating value: Temporal-Difference learning, Monte Carlo
Undersatnd and implement a model-based approach to RL: Temporal-Difference, Expected Sarsa, Q-learning
Understand several approaches that affect approximate value functions: supervised learning, fixed basis,  neural network.
Understand how function approximation is used to predict and control in Reinforcement Learning
Understand and implement an RL solution to a problem step by step: problem formulation, appropriate algorithm selection, implementation, and empirical study into the effectiveness of the solution.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Reinforcement Learning_Học tăng cường
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study;
general_details.Description: This course helps students understand the concepts of Reinforcement Learning including the space of RL algorithms (Temporal- Difference learning, Monte Carlo, Sarsa, Q-learning, Policy Gradients, Dyna, and more). Students will understand how to formalize these tasks as a Reinforcement Learning problem. Students will learn how RL fits under the broader umbrella of machine learning, and how it complements deep learning, supervised and unsupervised learning. Students can implement a complete RL solution and understand how to apply AI tools to solve real-world problems.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description: This course is designed to introduce students to properties of foods and changes that occur during preparation. Students will learn basic skills in food preparation and presentation while implementing food safety and sanitation standards. Topics to be covered include prevention of food-borne illness through proper handling of potentially hazardous foods, food safety management, GMP procedures, legal guidelines, kitchen safety, facility sanitation, and guidelines for safe food preparation, storing, and reheating... The program also includes a visit 3-4 restaurants or food production lines.

The course also introduces Vietnamese regulations on food and beverage safety.

- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

clos.LO Details: Develop general knowledge on the origins and development of the beverage industry.
Explain the purpose of effective beverage receiving and storage practices and how to calculate an inventory turnover rate.
Interpret financial data and use decision-making skills and abilities in a variety of managerial and service positions.
Identify local laws and customer in Vietnam pertaining to the service and purchase of alcoholic beverages and liquor law liability
Recognize equipment and glassware used for beverage preparation and service
Assemble the hand tools and equipment needed to mix and serve drinks and prepare garnishes.
Explain the procedures for internal beverage control
Explain the production processes for spirits, wine, beer, and other beverages
Identify and provide the process of preparation, presentation, and service of alcoholic beverages.
Identify and present the knowledge of wines by grape and other fruit variety, country, growing region, and production process.
Explain how to create a workforce of the beverage business operations.

clos.LO Details: Understand the income statement of an food and beverage business

general_details.Syllabus Name: Business Research Methods_Phương pháp nghiên cứu
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course introduces students to a number of research methods useful for academic and professional investigations of business practices. By examining the applications, strengths, and weaknesses of methodologies drawn from both the qualitative and quantitative traditions, this course permits an understanding of the various steps involved in designing and executing a research project so that students will be able to conduct their research later.

A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications. Students learn to use theses tools to :

- support generating and refining research topics, 

- assist in content suggestions, 

- assist in answering questions on Edunext, in-class discussions, and identifying credible sources.

- supports summarizing and concluding research findings through data-driven insights and structured templates.
general_details.StudentTasks:
Students need to

- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and materials of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 4/3h final exam + 103,7h self-study
general_details.Description: This module provides students with an understanding of the quantitative methods for finance and investment and assists their thesis writing. This includes the ability to formulate problems into quantitative models, to aid the successful resolution of the problem. Students will learn how to apply statistical methods to analyze past data and make forecast on future trends. Using output from mathematical and statistical models, students will learn to analyze, interpret and derive potential outcomes from financial information. Topics covered include financial data collection, probability, sampling, panel regression, time series analyses, and decision tree. Teaching method is flexible. Lecturers and tutors can mix between traditional teaching method with project-based learning, problem-based learning and flipped classroom.

clos.LO Details: Understand the econometrics methods necessary for doing empirical analysis in business, particularly in finance
Understand underlying assumptions  of different econometrics models
Be able to identify the advantages and disadvantages of various methods and techniques and choose appropriate methods for specific datasets
Ulitize common statistical packages to conduct empirical research
Be able to conduct, interpret and critically deal with empirical studies in finance and related fields
Be able to work in a team or individually in making business decisions based on quantitative analysis; present one's self decisions.
Apply tools and knowledge to define, design and deliver an academically rigorous piece of research
Show awareness of statistical errors and understand of being ethical when conducting quantitative research

general_details.Syllabus Name: Research methods in Communication_Phương pháp nghiên cứu truyền thông
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 31,5h contact hours + 1h final exam + 13,5h study on course (online) + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course provides knowledge of all basic sociological research methods as well as understanding of specific communication research and assessment instruments. As a result, the students will gain a practical understanding of research, evaluation in academic and professional settings. The course program includes practical acquaintance with contemporary media and social networks monitoring systems.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Media and communication research methods: An introduction to qualitative and quantitative approaches.
materials_table.Author: Arthur A Berger

clos.LO Details: To explain the nature of research in communication field and its process with different steps.
To distinguish different research methods in communication and select the most appropriate one for their research problems.
To apply qualitative research methods in communication field.
To apply quantitative research methods in communication field.
To create report and presentation to communicate their research project
To design and conduct a communication research project to ensure validity and reliablity and avoid ethical issues.
To respect research ethics and conduct communication research in an ethical way

general_details.Description:
This course, "Research for Designers," dives into the world of strategic design research. Students will explore qualitative and quantitative research techniques, the importance of data-driven design, and ethical considerations within the research process. This course teaches how to integrate these insights into design thinking, producing evidence-based solutions that resonate with the target audience. 

By the end of the course, students will gain essential skills in critical analysis, research methodology, empathy building, evidence-based decision-making, and clear communication of findings. This course will transform students into more strategic, insightful, and user-focused designers, ready to tackle the complexities of real-world design challenges.

The course can also help students apply the knowledge they have gained in delivering scientific reports and build and develop report presentation skills at seminars and conferences.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Professional Selling and Management_Kỹ năng bán hàng chuyên nghiệp
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Learners will get accustomed to different valuable sales techniques, which guide them to prepare for sales activities, create better relationship with customers, utilize IT in sales management and deal with key accounts of their business. 

As for sales perspectives, the course brings about the important roles of sales in company's marketing strategy, and helps learners shape their own sales strategy for any kind of given products.

Besides, four chapters in sales environment will also help learners consider various significant issues inside and outside their daily tasks such as, sales setting, customer behaviours, legal aspects and selling internationally.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- 80% attendance is required. 

- Students are expected to finish all the homework and prepare carefully for their next lessons. No late homework or submit on behalf of someone else will be accepted.

- With possible written assignments, students may use the work of others – textbooks, journal articles, the Internet and other sources to study and to prepare their assignments. In that case, they need to cite these sources in Harvard Referencing style. 

- Take part in the final exam

general_details.Syllabus Name: SAP General 1_Tổng quan về SAP 1
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: The course demonstrates concepts, principles, techniques, and applications of ERP systems in general and SAP in particular. The course recalls the components and the structure of an enterprise and introduces the design of SAP that is compatible with this structure. The course also introduces the first three SAP modules, SD (Sales Distribution), MM (Material Management) and PP (Product Planning). general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (300h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 85' practical exam + 252,6h self-study
general_details.Description:
Upon completion of this course students shoud: 
1. Understand the followings:
• ReactJS concepts for building Front-End application
• RESTful API concepts
• RESTful API using Spring Boot's built-in features and frameworks
• Security features (authentication and authorization) with RESTful API
• Handling HTTP requests and responses using Spring Boot's framework
• Error handling and exception management in Spring Boot RESTful APIs
2. Be able to:
• Build RESTful APIs using Spring Boot's built-in features and frameworks
• Implement security features with authentication and authorization
• Handle HTTP requests and responses using Spring Boot's framework
• Build Front-End application using ReactJS components
• Integrate Spring Boot with other technologies and frameworks SQL Server, MongoDB, and ReactJS
3. Be able to work in team and present group's results

general_details.Syllabus Name: Science of Color_Khoa học màu sắc
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description: After completing the course of color science, students can master and apply The Experience of Color / Color Awareness / The Uses of Color / Color-Order Systems / Color Study in their design work. The course focuses on color theory, operation and influence of color in diverse areas of design and user experience. Besides, the subject supports students to form creative ability and arrange layout to form a balanced and coherent whole for the composition. Enhance the perception of backgrounds, colors, layouts and applications in specific decorative products. In addition, the subject helps students practice independent working habits and self-arrange personal work plans. Develop creative thinking ability through the diverse expression of ideas as the foundation for the project system in the following semesters. In addition, form an attitude of being willing to learn and develop yourself when given the opportunity.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submlit to the teacher 01 day after the course.
general_details.Tools:
Individual tools prepared by students:

- 1 folder (size A2).

- Paper (size  A3, A4), A1 backboard paper.

- Color, pencil, eraser, brushes, back ink pen.

- Ruler, paper knife, scissors, paper sticking-plaster, double sized tape, glue.

- Laptop

clos.LO Details: Recognize the relationship between colors and factors related to reading comprehension and analysis, creating meaning for colors
Define and explain color through the connection between 3 properties of color: Hue, Value, Saturation.

Detected Color instability by looking at color composition, Ground and Carried Colors, Placement and Color Change, Equilibrium, Simultaneous Contrast, Afterimage and Contrast Reversal, Complementary Contrast. Then, know how to apply this instability to the design to actively decide the outcome of the product.
Manage the Color Illusions, The Illusion of Depth, Spatial Effects of Colors, Transparence Illusion, Fluting, Vibration, Vanishing Boundaries, Luminosity, Bezold Effect, Optical Mixes
Construct and Organize the color in line with modern trends through understanding the history and theory of color.
Create color harmony in design products
Applying color and light in media and commercial design, interaction design and graphics-related fields
Having a professional style in design activities. Love to research and perfect themselvs in visual arts.

sessions.Topic:
Lab 1

72 ideas in decorating with color              Request:

1. 72 ideas are 72 pictures drawn in small squares measuring 8.5cm each (with 0.25cm white border around)            2. 72 ideas must agree on a visual language, have a unified theme, have the main color and style, express the artist's personality clearly.                        3. After completing the drawing. Students present a report that demonstrates the process of taking this drawing from concept to sketch and color selection and final product.
sessions.Student Materials: Students can draw by machine or by hand. If drawing by hand, students choose drawing materials and types of drawing colors (hint: poster color, acrylic color,...).                                        The practice report - also known as a portfolio or design process report, must be done with design and layout software (Indesign, Ai). Export a PDF file

general_details.Syllabus Name: Supply Chain Management_Quản lý chuỗi cung ứng
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
A supply chain is comprised of all the parties involved in fulfilling a customer request. The integrated management of this network is a critical determinant of success in today’s competitive environment. 

Supply chain management is the systemic, strategic coordination of the traditional business functions within a particular company and across businesses within a supply chain, for the purpose of improving the long-term performance of the individual companies and the supply chain as a whole. The major supply chain processes include planning, sourcing, making or converting, fulfillment, and relationships management. The major dimensions for evaluating the performance of supply chain processes and activities are time, cost, quality and compliance. This course covers the major activities of companies involved in profitably coordinating supply and demand in the marketplace to deliver consumer value.

general_details.Syllabus English: Introduction to Logistics and Supply Chain Management
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: Logistics is an important part of the supply chain, involving the planning, implementation, and control of the flow of goods, services, and related information. Today, supply chains have become increasingly complex and global, with the participation of many partners and the use of advanced technologies to optimize processes, from raw material supply and production to storage and the distribution of finished products. Businesses must overcome challenges such as fluctuations in market demand, risks from unforeseen events (such as natural disasters and pandemics), and the need to comply with environmental protection requirements to maintain efficiency and competitiveness. This necessitates closer and more effective coordination between domestic and international organizations, as well as more frequent and widespread use of technologies like automation, AI, and big data to manage and track the flow of goods. This course not only helps students grasp the necessary techniques and tools in logistics and supply chain management but also enables them to understand the importance of optimizing these processes to improve business efficiency and better meet customer needs, especially as global integration continues to rapidly impact the economy of Vietnam.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only

clos.LO Details: Understand the core concepts, roles, and functions of logistics in business operations and supply chains such as transportation, warehousing, inventory management and their contributions to overall supply chain performance.

Analyze the structure and dynamics of supply chains, including key stages such as sourcing, production, and distribution, and assess the influence of external factors and the roles of key stakeholders.
Evaluate supply chain fundamental strategies to address its common operational challenges.
Demonstrate understanding of basic digital tools and emerging technologies such as automation, tracking systems, or data analytics to support logistics and supply chain decision-making.
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

general_details.Syllabus Name: Procurement and Global Sourcing_Mua sắm và tìm nguồn cung ứng toàn cầu
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course explores the central concepts of organisational procurement, global sourcing and interfaces of these to the other areas of an organisation. This course provides opportunities to examine issues such as organisational procurement process, global sourcing process, supplier selection process, supplier management and other strategic issues.

*Teaching method: This is a blended-learning course, in which students will take a look at the videos & slides and reading on Coursera first at home, then rewatch & discuss key questions with classmates and teachers at classes. 

AI Tools will be used to support students in

(1) generating ideas/structures for their speaking notes and slide structure of important topics of the course.

(2) editing the slide set after students have already finished it.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Access the learning materials on Coursera for self-study purposes

- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be eligible for the final assessment

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Access FU FLM at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

practice the ability to conduct negotiation in procurement
demonstrate understanding of stakeholder management in the given context of an enterprise
analyze the 7-step Strategic Sourcing Process

general_details.Syllabus Name: Introduction to Semiconductor Devices_Nhập môn thiết bị bán dẫn
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
The course includes two parts. 
- The first part covers a sufficient understanding of fundamental physics concepts about electromagnetism. This part explores the principles of electromagnetism, such as electromagnetic field, current, potential, capacitance, resistance, circuit...
- The second part of this course aims to provide a general understanding of semiconductor devices. This part explores the principles and the operation mechanism of semiconductor, such as charge transfer, p-n junction, junction capacitors, and Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors(MOSFETs), the Metal-Semiconductor Contact, Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (MOS) capapcitor, CMOS, Metal-Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MESFETs), Memory and Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) to improve the overall knowledge of semiconductor industry."

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1 h final exam + 85' practical exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course tackles all the problems related to NodeJS-based web servers. Contents to be implemented include:

- Overview of Web protocols: HTTP and HTTPS.

- Introduction of NodeJS and NodeJS: Express modules to build a web server.

- Deploy the application on a web server with basic CRUD operations. Work with NoSQL databases, specifically MongoDB and Mongoose, to access MongoDB from NodeJS.

- Overview of REST and building a RESTful API.

- Learn Authentication and security-related issues for web applications.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Server-Side development with NodeJS, Express, and MongoDB_Phát triển Server-Side với NodeJS, Express và MongoDB
general_details.Syllabus English: Server-Side development with NodeJS, Express, and MongoDB
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1 h final exam + 85' practical exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course tackles all the problems related to NodeJS-based web servers. Contents to be implemented include:

- Overview of Web protocols: HTTP and HTTPS.

- Introduction of NodeJS and frameworks such as ExpressJS, NestJS, Hono to build a web server.

- Introduction of simple templating languages such as EJB and HandleBar .

- Deploy the application on a web server with basic CRUD operations. Work with NoSQL databases, specifically MongoDB and Mongoose, to access MongoDB from NodeJS.

- Overview of REST and building a RESTful API.

- Learn Authentication and security-related issues for web applications.

- Integrate React app with server NodeJs

- Deploy server-based applications with Hosting Services
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Constantly follow announcements on FU CMS at https://cmshn.fpt.edu.vn/ and FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information regarding assignment submission and feedback on assignments and project work.

general_details.Description:
This course is designed as an introduction to the basic techniques and principles necessary for audio devices (microphone, mixer, ...) and audio editing application like Adobe Audition for students are able to record, voice-over, foley as well as edit and chord audio for animation movie, short movie, TVC, Viral, etc,. As a Multimedia course, the student will understand the aesthetics of sound, musically, voice, and as a result, develop critical listening and analysis skills for a movie like short movie, animation movie, TVC, viral, ... through the completion of regular listening exercises. Class critiques will be part of the projects produced.

Objective: After finishing this course, students can make sound for movies, tvc, animation movie,...

general_details.Syllabus Name: Search Engines_Công cụ tìm kiếm
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: The theory, creation, and use of text-based search engines are covered in this lecture-based course. The main content includes experimental assessment, representation of information demands and documents, several significant retrieval models, and statistical features of the text. Besides, the course covers typical components of commercial search engines, such as federated search, vertical search, tailored search results, and diversified search results.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to https://flm.fpt.edu.vn  for up-to-date course information
general_details.Note:
1) On-going Assessment

- 3 Assignments:                   30%

- 2 progress tests:                 30%

2) 1 Final Exam:                    40%

3) Final Result                       100% (The Final result - including bonus score - is not greater than 10)

clos.LO Details: Understanding how search engines work: Students should be able to explain the underlying technology behind search engines, including the algorithms used to crawl, index and rank web pages.
Search engine optimization: Students should be able to apply best practices for optimizing web pages to improve their visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs).
Keyword research: Students should be able to conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models..
Analytics and tracking: Students should be able to use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance.
Solving problems: Students should be able to apply search engine techniques to solve the real-life problems

general_details.Syllabus Name: Semantics_Ngữ nghĩa học
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1.25 hours final exam + 103.75 hours self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite: Passed LTG202 and ENG302c and ENP101 or ENP102
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to help introduce to the students the basics of Semantics in a step by step process through Semantics 101. In addition to the Semantics a Coursebook unit outlines, the course is enhanced with supplementary activities corresponding to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The course will help students:                                                                                                                                                                                      

	Have a grasp of the basics of Semantics.

	Understand and use the basics of Semantics in oral and written communication.

	Take the exercises seriously at the end of each topic/ lesson.

	Interact confidently with the lecturer and fellow students in dissolving disagreements about their answers.

	Talk about things to help in understanding when working through a problematic case with the help of fellow students and the lecturer.

	Engage in preparing a group presentation using appropriate language in oral and written  communication skills. 



Teaching and Learning Methodology

This course applies instructional, communicative, and interactive discussions with: 

~ instructions on pre-lesson and post lesson exercises meant to apply learnt skills.

~ encouragement on opening the field in learning philosophical and practical study of meaning.

~ open minded approach to questions and any misunderstandings that may arise during lessons. 

~ ancillary lectures and seminars to enhance active interest in the topics.



Assessment scheme:

On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result  >=5/10
general_details.StudentTasks:
	Be punctual for class.

	Actively participate in class discussions.

	Preview and review the lessons.

	Check vocabulary for comprehension.

	Answer the exercises before, during and after the class.

	Hand in homework and class requirements.

	Work with a group for group discussions and activities.

clos.LO Details: Recognize the basic word function in a sentence by labelling the different parts of speech.Define the vocabulary used with understanding of the appropriate usage or sense.Recall previous lessons learned and their applications to rectify grammatical errors.

Understand and use the different concepts of semantics and reaffirm grammar rules at the advanced level.Characterize vocabulary and its definition.Explain ambiguity in sentences and extend understanding by describing basic concepts
Use existing knowledge and/ or apply acquired knowledge in new situations. Apply logical notations to Semantics for practice. Identify problems in organizing data.
Examine and break information in sentences into parts to explore relationships. Analyze the principles of logic to its own Semantics to formulae the situation it describes.

Deduce sentences into its logical notation by drawing conclusions from logical premises involved in the lessons. Assess different cases whether the conclusions follow the valid rules of inferences or show the application of the rules. 
Justify the ideas of compositionality of meaning from the visual tables presented in the lessons.

Design direct and indirect illocutions of utterances for interpersonal and non-literal meanings.Formulate differences between literal and non-literal, abstracts and metaphors, and metonymy and its various kinds.
Practice and refine the lifelong learning behavior of collaboration by working together as a group.

general_details.Description:
The capstone project provides students important skills and initial experiences in participating in the software projects. Student can apply knowledges they have learned to the real current projects include:

- Experiencing across all project phases: requirement, design, coding, testing and release

- Finding out and using the templates and composing documents for each project stage

- Using knowledges of technology that have been taught

- Having the opportunity to research and apply new technologies

- Practicing teamwork and how to interact with colleagues in a project implementation process

- Ensuring the proper implementation of quality requirements and schedule

- Doing troubleshooting



With the team size of 4-5 members, the output product size are required to be equivalent to 20-25 medium use cases (3-7 transactions for each use case; action buttons on the screen, end user interactions to the software screens/functions or database transactions can be counted as transaction)



The capstone project provides students, working in groups, with a significant project experience in which they can integrate much of the material they have learned in their program, including matters relating to requirements, design, implementation, human factors, professionalism, and project management. Students should be expected to deliver one or several iterations of a software system, along with all artifacts appropriate to the process model they are using. These would likely include 

a) Project management Plan (perhaps updated regularly), 

b) Software Requirements Specifications (SRS)

c) Software Design Documents (SDD)

d) Test Plan and other Test Documentation (STD)

e) Software package & the user guides (package content, installation guide & user manuals)



All the documents in the project implementation process and the progress reports are required to write in English.

general_details.Description: This speech processing course comprehensively explains how humans and machines generate, transmit, and process speech signals. The course covers speech production, phonetics, acoustic analysis, speech perception, speech recognition, natural language processing, and speech synthesis. Students will learn about the principles and algorithms behind various speech-processing techniques, including signal processing, machine learning, and deep learning. The course also covers speech processing applications in speech recognition, speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech enhancement. Upon completing the course, students will have a solid foundation in speech processing and be equipped with the necessary skills to tackle real-world speech-processing problems.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Advanced Business Communication_Kỹ năng giao tiếp nâng cao trong kinh doanh
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course addresses the fundamental elements of communication in business environment to equip learners with essential  communication tools to ensure success for both individuals and organization.

Upon the completion of this course, the learners will be able to:                        

(1) communicate effectively in writing the basic and practical business correspondence including emails and letters to internal and external customers (peers, subordinates, superiors, customers, partners, suppliers, and other stakeholders.                                        

(2) communicate effectively in speaking in different business contexts including socialization, staff meetings, meetings with customers and partners where the learners may play the role of participants or presenters.                                                    (3) successfully present their ideas of major research/problem solving in form of business report and presentation.                              

(4) personalize their communication style to enhance communicative effects and leave good impresson on readers/audience

(5) communicate effectively in job preparation
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
general_details.Description:
The course stresses a balanced approach to communication by  in written and oral essential form of business communication. It is also to give the learners opportunities to practice face to face communication, listening and non-verbal messages, presentation skills, job interview;  technology, multicultural and global communication, business ethics and teamwork are integrated in content and applications throughout the course.his course addresses the fundamental elements of communication in business environment to equip learners with essential communication tools to ensure success for both individuals and organization.

Upon the completion of this course, the learners will be able to:   

(1) Communication effectively in writting the basic and practical business correspondence including letters, emails, and advanced ones as reports, proposals, business plans…

(2) communicate effectively face-to-face communication as presenting, listening, feedback, nonverbal messages in different business contexts including socialization, staff meetings, meetings with colleagues, customers and partners...                                                         

(3) successfully in the job search, résume and interviewing communication including writing application letters, CV, and prepare job interview in variety situations..             

(4) personalize their communication style to enhance communicative effects and leave good impresson on readers/audience.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Effective Presentation Skills
general_details.Time Allocation:
1 course = 30 sessions

1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
This course will give you helpful tips for making effective speeches and delivering them well. You'll learn how to organize a presentation, how to make it memorable, and how to communicate clearly. In the course, you'll have several opportunities to demonstrate the presentation skills that you learn. This will help you gain the experience you need to be more confident when you give a speech in a classroom or on the job.



Some materials in this course are taken from the Coursera MOOC "Presentations: Speaking so that People Listen" at https://www.coursera.org/learn/presentations-speaking-so-that-people-listen/home/welcome
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Define the basic concepts of public speaking
Construct an informative speech
Compose an outline for a well-supported persuasive speech
Identify types of reasoning and logical fallcies
Construct and deliver an effective presentation in academic and professional settings
Define the concepts relating to audience analysis and listening and apply this knowledge to improve personal preparation of a speech
Compose appropriate specifc purpose and central idea statements for informative, persuasive, and inspirational/entertaining speeches
Distinguish between types of research and sources of information for a speech
Demonstrate the structure of a presentation and construct an outline for a presentation
List the types of supporting materials
Construct presentation introductions and conclusions
List types of presentation aids and apply them in presentations appropriately
Explain and apply methods of delivery

general_details.Time Allocation: 58 hours online study + 3 hrs offline (2 slots) + PE (5 mins/student) + 89 hours self-study
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin.

2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required

3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at  https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct

3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded)

4. Communicate and discuss in forum

5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional)

6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus
general_details.Note:
1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

2) Theoretical Exam (PE) 

3) Final Result (FR) =min (10, TE + Bonus)

4) Completion Criteria:  PE>=4 and FR>=5

general_details.Description:
-Course Objectives: 
Master the art of persuasion through understanding ethos, pathos, and logos.
Develop strong argumentation and critical thinking skills.
Analyze and adapt to diverse audiences.
Improve public speaking delivery, including vocal variety, body language, and eye contact.
Utilize research to support persuasive claims.
Construct persuasive speeches using various organizational patterns.
Provide and receive constructive feedback on persuasive presentations.
-Course Description: This course is designed to equip students with the essential skills to craft and deliver compelling persuasive speeches. Through a combination of theoretical knowledge and practical application, students will learn to analyze audiences, develop strong arguments, and effectively communicate their ideas. The course emphasizes critical thinking, research, and public speaking skills. Students will have the opportunity to practice their persuasive abilities through in-class presentations and receive constructive feedback from peers and the instructor. By the end of the course, students will be confident in their ability to persuade and influence others and equiped students with the soft skills necessary to thrive in today's competitive job market.
-Teaching method: interactive and contructivist approach and/or Project Based Learning

general_details.Syllabus Name: WORKING IN GROUPS
general_details.Time Allocation: 1 course = 30 sessions; 1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description: This course will cover both classic and current theories of group communication that focus on "how groups work" and include practical information on group communication strategies and skills that emphasize "how to work in groups". Topics included: group development, group membership, group diversity, group leadership, group motivation, conflict and cohesion in groups, planning and conducting meetings and making presentations in groups. Learning in the class will be facilitated through the use of vehicles such as textbook readings, class discussion, exercises/in-class activities, cases and lectures.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

clos.LO Details: LO1: Define common teamwork skills such as group communication, membership, leadership, listening, planning and conducting meeting, verbal and nonverbal communication, conflict and cohesion, problem solving.
LO10: Analyse ways to become effective and powerful leaders.
LO11: Understand leadership theories and model of leadership effectiveness.
LO12: Describe importance of verbal and nonverbal in teamwork and how to  use them effectiveness.
LO13: Identify differences the use of nonverbal communication with gender and culture.
LO14: Discriminate defensive and supportive behaviors and the way to create a supportive communication climate.
LO15: Identify the challenges and types of listening in groups.
LO16: Describe skills and strategies to effective listening in group.
LO17: Discuss differences of listening with factors that gender, personality, cultural, hearing ability.
LO18: Understand how conflicts appear in groups and how to manage them in cohesion.
LO19: Identify decision making skills and problem solving theories
LO2: Identify key elements, advantages, disavantages and the nature of group communication.
LO20:Apply structured and creative problem solving skills to solve group problems.
LO21: Illustrate and analyze problem solving by critical thinking skills with cooperative argumentations.
LO22: Develop a professtional meeting and practice dealing the behavior problems of members in the meeting time.
LO23: Identify the nature of vitural groups, synchronous and ayhchronous goupware
LO24: Discuss group diversity demensions affect to virtual groups, such as age, geography, income.
LO25: Apply of parliamentary principles and summary the basic procedures when organizing the meeting.
LO3: Recognise the principles that help balance the group's activities and ethical issues.
LO4: Describe stages of group development and types of group norms.
LO5: Discuss the goals of the group and how to encourage effective group work
LO6: Explain why member join, stay or leave groups through theory of needs.
LO7: Determine group roles and how each role helps hinders groups from achieving a common goal.
LO8: Describe and apply strategies for reducing communication apprehensions.
LO9: Understand how to become an assertive members and learn how to balance between passivity and aggression.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Communication and In-group working skills
general_details.Time Allocation: 30 sessions, 1 session = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
This course will cover both working in groups and communication skills.  



Assessment structure: 

* On-going Assessment:

- Activity: 10%

- Quiz: 15%

- Group Assignment : 15%

- Group Project : 30%

* Final Exam: 30%

* Completion Criteria: Every on-going assessment component > 0, Final Exam >=4, Final Result  >=5
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities 

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Read the textbook in advance 

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Establish relationships between class members and group organization
Understand leadership theories and model of leadership effectiveness.
Describe and identify importance of verbal and nonverbal in teamwork and how to  use them effectiveness.
Understand how conflicts appear in groups and how to manage them in cohesion.
Develop a professtional meeting and practice dealing the behavior problems of members in the meeting time.
Apply of parliamentary principles and summary the basic procedures when organizing the meeting.
Identify words and develop clear, concise,logical, coherent,and effective paragraphs.
Format business letters using the full block,modified block,and simplified styles.
Format memos and e-mail properly.
Prepare competently a variety of positive and neutral messages using the direct plan.
Prepare effective negative messages for a variety of purposes using the indirect plan
Form a group and conduct group work
Write messages that are used for the various stages of collection
Write formal and informal reports
Prepare targeted and general résumés in chronological, functional,or combination format.
Prepare for a successful job interview
Review the knowledge learned and practice overview
Define common teamwork skills such as group communication, membership, leadership, planning and conducting meeting, verbal and nonverbal communication, conflict and cohesion,
Identify key elements, advantages, disavantages and the nature of group communication.
Describe stages of group development and types of group norms.
Explain why member join, stay or leave groups through theory of needs.
Determine group roles and how each role helps hinders groups from achieving a common goal.
Describe and apply strategies for reducing communication apprehensions.
Analyse ways to become effective and powerful leaders.

Task Description:

Students work on the group project which is based on the approved proposal in the Group Assignment. Products of the project can be a media program (web, page, video clip, publication ...), an event (a contest, charity...)



That project must be conducted in your community and implemented from week 3 to the end of the semester.

sessions.Student's Tasks:
Write a proposal

Including: Presentation + a proposal 

Task Description:

Each group consists of 5 to 7 students working together to develop a social project to achieve 1 or both of the following goals:

- Helping disadvantaged communities, for example: new student's life; poor/street children/people; LBGT...

- Solving some problems in your community, for example: environmental pollution, animal protection ...



Draft and finalize your plan into a group project proposal, then present it to the class for lecturers' approval of the project.



After presentating and getting approved by the lecturer, each group will carry out their project in the community, from week 3 to the end of the semester following lecture's instructions.



* Students are not allowed to put your own money into a project, if you have money, you must raise funds.

Link page of Softskills Projects, there are many projects that has made posted here by students: https://www.facebook.com/FPTUSoftSkills/ 



Presentation:

For the 15 to 30-minute presentation, you are required to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your project proposal in front of your classmates and lecturer.



Components of project Proposal:

Include the following sections in your project proposal:

• Title of the group project

• Table of contents

• Introduction the group project: The introduction provides background information that profiles your group (e.g., location, goals, size, etc.). It describes the purpose of the proposal request. 

• Project/product/service description

• Purpose 

• Problem or need 

• Benefits of the proposal 

• Description of the solution 

• Evaluation plan 

• Qualifications of personnel 

• Time schedule 

• Budget (if any)

• Glossary (if any)

• Appendixes (if any)

• Reference list (if any)

- Method to develop your Problem Solving and Creativity Skills

- How to develop your Critical Thinking Skills

- How to develop your Communication Skills

- Develop a toolkit to be able to identify real problems and goals within ill-defined problem & Recognize and apply analytical & creative problem solving technique

- Identify types of argument, and bias within arguments

- Improve study skills (academic reading, information searching, ...)
