general_details.Description:
This course provides students with personal and interpersonal skills needed for effective leadership and supervision, especially it focuses on creative thinking and problem solving. This course is skill-based approach, therefore requires a lot of practical exercises. After taking this class, the students should be able:

 1. To increase your understanding of core behavioral principles upon which important management skills are based

2. To help foster improved competency in several critical management skills

3. To help prepare you to transfer this learning and improvement to real-life, out-of-class settings

4. To develop individual personal ability and skills to work collaboratively

assessments.Question Type: OP1: The purpose of this assignment is to give students a work-team experience in developing management skills. To arrive at a realistic problem, each group should interview one manager or alternatively carrying out surveys on management problems. The group must assume the role of a consulting firm called in to solve that identified specific problem in the chosen organization. Groups should also use descriptions of current management practices reported in business periodicals. All projects must be approved by the instructor before being started. Each group will make an in-class PowerPoint presentation of about 30 minutes, in PowerPoint on a real or fictitious organizational problem. (The problem must be related to a chapter topic. OP2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report. Specific contacts of interview including phone number, addresses, website must be submitted

general_details.Syllabus Name: Negotiation / Kỹ năng đàm phán
general_details.Time Allocation: 30 sessions;  1 session= 90 minutes
general_details.Description: Vendor contracts, budget allocations, individual performance objective setting, buying and selling or even a daily events are all common activities requiring sophisticated negotiation skills. In addition to formal negotiation and/or mediation, leaders also often find themselves in informal negotiations with various constituents and colleges. This course introduces participants to the techniques of dispute resolution, the process of mediation and facilitation, and various techniques of negotiation. This course will make use of both case studies and simulations. The course will also serve as an introduction to mini case studies, which involves each group working as a management team. Learning in the class will be facilitated through the use of vehicles such as textbook readings, class discussion, exercises/activities, cases, self quizzes and lectures..

assessments.Note:
1. On-going Assessment: 40%

Students work in a project team of 4-5 members on the assignments as appointed by the teacher

The works are organized by iterations with the contents and assessments as below

(each student is assign to practice full-stack codes on assigned/selected function). 

Throughout the process, students are encouraged to use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot), under the following conditions:

     - Must transparently declare AI usage (e.g., what prompt was used, which part was generated by AI).

     -  Must explain AI-generated output using their own understanding.

 a. Evaluation 1 (20%) – Requirement Analysis & Modeling

Create use case descriptions and UML diagrams (static and dynamic models).

AI can assist with modeling, but students must present their reasoning independently.

Required Deliverables: AI prompts (if used), UML diagrams (e.g., PlantUML or Visio), written explanations.

 b. Evaluation 2 (20%) – Software Architecture & Design

Design software architecture, decompose into subsystems, object-oriented design, and database schema.

AI can help propose architecture or generate code samples, but students must refine and justify the result.

Required Deliverables: Architecture docs, diagrams, code snippets, explanation of AI-assisted parts.

2.  Final Project Presentation: 60%

Each team presents their integrated software product and individual responsibilities.

The individual evaluation includes an additional component for AI usage as follows:

- Integrated Software Product Demostration for Software design (30%): Web API , Web Admin, Mobile App...

- Mastery of assigned works: weighted 20%

- Soft Skills & Working Attitudes: weighted 10%

AI Evaluation Rubric (for individual performance – up to 10 points)

- Understanding of AI Output

- Customization and Enhancement of AI Output

- Transparency (Prompt + AI Use Declaration)

- Effective and Ethical AI Usage



To be selected to the Final Presentation, each student needs:

* All on-going assessments (Evaluation 1 & Evaluation 2) >=5/10

* No cheating during the project progress

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 62h online + 3h offline + 1h TE + 2h PE + 82 h self-study
general_details.Pre-Requisite: PRO192 (not applied to the BIT_AI17 and BA programs)
general_details.Description:
SWE201c is for people who are new to software engineering. It's also for those who have already developed software, but wish to gain a deeper understanding of the underlying context and theory of software development practices.



At the end of this course, we expect learners to be able to:



1.) Build high-quality and secure software using SDLC methodologies such as agile, lean, and traditional/waterfall.



2.) Analyze a software development team's SDLC methodology and make recommendations for improvements.



3.) Compare and contrast software development methodologies with respect to environmental, organizational, and product constraints.
general_details.StudentTasks: Student must get the certification of Software Development Lifecycle specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination
general_details.Note:
1. Complete the online course to be allowed to take Final Exam                    

2. Final Exam is included of Final Theory Exam (TE) & Final Practical Exam (PE):  100%

3. Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

4. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & Final PE Score >=4 & FR >= 5

(FR = min(10, (Final TE Score + Final PE Score)/2 + bonus)

general_details.Description:
After studying this subject, you will know the basic concepts in IT project management. The course will lead you step by step to complete an IT project. As a project administrator, you will be instructed to take steps from Project Startup, Planning, Performing monitoring and control and finally Project Completion Management.

Students who can finish their studies can:

- Understand the concepts of projects, project management

- Implement all project stages from beginning to end

- Participate in implementation of start-up, planning, implementation, control and completion of projects.

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course focuses on designing, developing, and integrating the basic Web-based system/application using Java Web  or .NET technologies (with the system requirements, technical framework & DBMS as assigned/agreed by the teacher)

Students are required to build the system in teams, 4-5 members/team as appointed by the teacher.

After the course, students will be able to achieve web programing proficiency with the following skills by practicing with other members in the assigned team

- Proficiency in common web techniques and basic Java or .NET Web development skills

- Proficiency in front end skills (HTML, CSS, JS) required for the industry

- Analyze & design the solution following the object oriented models

- Co-ordinate with the others to complete the project works
general_details.StudentTasks:
'- Build the team & select/receive the software topic to develop with arrangement/guide from the teacher

- Select the team leader and setup/configure project development and management environments (source codes, tasks, issues, milestones) on the GitLab (or GitHub) & project documents management on the OneDrive (or Google Drive)

- Get the detailed assignment from the teacher, plan the project tasks, and execute the project accordingly

- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final presentation.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises given by the teacher in class or at home and submit on time

- Constantly follow the teacher's guides/references for up-to-date course information regarding assignment submission and feedback on assignments and project work. 

- Using the GitLab (or GitHub) to collaborate in every phase of the project by all the team members
general_details.Tools:
One Drive or Google Drive for document management

GitLab (https://gitlab.com/) for issue and code version management

DBMS: as assigned/agreed with the teacher

Java tools

• Tomcat server

• Java JDK version 1.6 or higher, NetBeans 13

.NET tools

• Microsoft Internet Information Services server

• Microsoft Visual Studio version 2019 or higher

general_details.Description:
The capstone project provides students important skills and initial experiences in participating in the software projects. Student can apply knowledges they have learned to the real current projects include:

- Experiencing across all project phases: requirement, design, coding, testing and release

- Finding out and using the templates and composing documents for each project stage

- Using knowledges of technology that have been taught

- Having the opportunity to research and apply new technologies

- Practicing teamwork and how to interact with colleagues in a project implementation process

- Ensuring the proper implementation of quality requirements and schedule

- Doing troubleshooting



With the team size of 4-5 members, the output product size are required to be equivalent to 20-25 medium use cases (3-7 transactions for each use case; action buttons on the screen, end user transactions to the software screens/functions or database transactions can be counted as transaction)



The capstone project provides students, working in groups, with a significant project experience in which they can integrate much of the material they have learned in their program, including matters relating to requirements, design, implementation, human factors, professionalism, and project management. Students should be expected to deliver one or several iterations of a software system, along with all artifacts appropriate to the process model they are using. These would likely include 

a) Project management Plan (perhaps updated regularly), 

b) Software Requirements Specifications (SRS)

c) Architectural and Design Documents (SDD)

d) Test Plan and other Test Documentation (STD)

e) Software package & the user guides (package content, installation guide & user manuals)



All the documents in the project implementation process and the progress reports are required to write in English.



"Final Result = OGA*50% + TDA*50%

In which:"	

"1) On-going Assessment (OGA)

    - Project Introduction (Report 1): 4%

    - Project Management Plan (Report 2): 8%

    - Software Requirement (Report 3): 16%

    - Software Design (Report 4): 18%

    - Testing (Report 5): 18%

    - User Guides (Report 6): 4%

    - Implementation (Report 7): 32%"

"2) Thesis Defense Assessment (TDA)	

    - Project Introduction: 5%

    - Project Management Plan: 5%

    - Software Requirement: 15%

    - Software Design: 10%

    - Testing: 10%

    - User Guides: 5%

    - Implementation: 35%    

    - Presentation Skills: 5%

    - Q&A: 10%"

"Completion Criteria: 

1. TDA >=4/10

2. Final Result  >=5



Before thesis defense, students must wait until the second thesis defense round if they have the OGA less than 5/10 OR they are in one of below cases:

(1) Students complete less than 75% use cases functions/screens as submitted (as mentioned in the submitted Report 3, at the end of the week 3) OR there are less than 20 average (3-7 transactions)  use cases completed.

(2) Students can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output software by themselves

(3) There are more than 3 obvious coding-logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any software functions) in the submitted software.



The student(s) has to re-do the capstone project if the above cases occur with the assessments for the second thesis defense OR there is one OGA with grade (see the list above) less than 2/10.



After thesis defense, student(s) is evaluated as failed the capstone project if they are in one of below cases (no matter when the guiding teacher doesn't evaluate that):

(1) Student can't demonstrate any function or use case

(2) Students can't prove the fact that they prepare any of the project reports or the output software by themselves

(3) There are more than 3 obvious coding-logic defects OR more than 1 show-stopper defects (the defects that prevent end user from completing his/her use case on any software functions) in the submitted software.  "

general_details.Syllabus Name: Software Quality assurance and Testing
general_details.Time Allocation:
Contact time: 30 slots: Lectures:   24 ;  Labs:    6

Home study:    26 slots; 1 slot = 90'
general_details.Description:
• General concepts about quality and quality assurance

• Testing techniques aimed at assuring that appropriate functionality has been implemented correctly in the software system or product, including: a) black box or functional testing, b) clear box or structural testing, c) usage-based statistical testing. 

These testing techniques are organized by their underlying models, including lists, partitions and equivalent classes, finite-state machines. 

• Test activities, management, and related issues, such as testing sub-phases, team organization, testing process, people's roles and responsibilities, test automation, etc., will also be discussed. 

• Other testing, verification and validation techniques…

• Defect prevention: objectives, benefits and techniques

• Some practical quality assessment and improvement issues
general_details.StudentTasks:

- Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Constantly follow announcements on intranet/CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information regarding assignment submission and feedback on assignments and project work.

general_details.Time Allocation:

     Lectures:    30 hrs

general_details.Description:
This course is a model-based introduction to RE, providing the conceptual backgroud and terminology on RE, addressing a variety of techniques for 

- Analysis and Requirements Elicitation; 

- Requirements Evaluation; 

- Requirements Specification and Documentation; 

- Requirements Quality Assurance

and demonstrating the Goal-Orientated Aproach in Requirements Engineering through  

- Modeling System Objectives with Goal Diagrams 

- Modeling Conceptual objects with Class diagrams

- Moddeling System Agents and Responsibilities

- Moddeling System Operations.

During the course students are required to practice the RE techniques in class exercises and Assignments

general_details.Syllabus Name: Software Requirement_Yêu cầu phần mềm
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h TE + 1.5h PE + 102.5h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course is a model-based introduction to RE, providing the conceptual background and terminology on RE, addressing a variety of techniques for  requirements  development including Analysis and Requirements Elicitation; Requirements Evaluation; Requirements Specification and Documentation; Requirements Quality Assurance. To implement these  frameworks, student will be learnt  how to find  appropriate customer representatives, elicit requirements from them, and  document user requirements, business rules, functional requirements, data requirements, and nonfunctional requirements. 

The numerous visual models  that will be represented to illustrate the requirements from various perspectives to supplement natural-language text. Other contents recommend the most  effective  requirements approaches for various specific classes of projects: agile projects  developing products of any type, enhancement and replacement projects, projects that incorporate packaged solutions, outsourced projects, business process automation projects, business analytics projects, and embedded and other real-time systems.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Software Testing_Kiểm thử phần mềm
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h TE + 1.5h PE + 102.5 h self-study
general_details.Description:
• General principles of software testing, including its purposes and objectives. 
• Testing integrated into software development processes, covering test levels, test types, and maintenance testing.
• Static testing basics, including feedback and review processes to enhance software quality. 
• Techniques such as black-box (functional), white-box (structural), and experience-based testing applied to derive test cases.  
• Test activities like planning, estimation, monitoring, risk management, defect reporting, and test automation usage. 
• Tools and methods to support effective testing, emphasizing benefits and potential risks.
• AI is used to explore testing concepts, support static testing, and create/optimize Test Plans.
general_details.StudentTasks:
Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time.
- The use of AI in assessments and exams must comply with the instructions of the course instructor.
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_details.Tools:
- Unit Test Framework
- Bug Management Tool
- Ms Office
- IDE
- Static Analyst Tool
- Automation Tool
- AI Tools: Grok (xAI), ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek
general_details.Note: In the case: (5 > Final TE Score >=4) & (5 > Final PE Score >=4) & FR < 5, the student can choose to take the resit of both TE & PE OR just either TE or PE.

clos.LO Details: Know definitions, concepts and terminologies about Software Testing, using AI to explore testing principles and real-world testing scenarios through effective prompts.
Demonstrate presentation skills and effective teamwork

Understand the software testing process. Distinguish between levels of testing (e.g. unit, integration, system, acceptance) and types of testing (e.g. functional, non-functional) applied to a specific group project (encouraged to choose project in SWP391)

Use static testing techniques to detect errors through a review process, using AI to review documents for defects (e.g., ambiguity, inconsistency) and analyze static code for errors (e.g., code smells, bug patterns).
Use dynamic testing techniques like black-box, white-box, and experience-based testing to design and execute test cases, and determine test coverage.
Develop a comprehensive test plan for an AI-enabled project, clearly defining its scope, goals, resources, and testing schedule.
Analyze and prioritize risks to focus testing efforts effectively. Understand and apply bug logging, bug reporting, and test reporting practices.
Classify and select appropriate testing tools, evaluate the benefits and risks of test automation, and choose an automation tool for testing functionalities in the team project.
Understand and apply Agile testing methods.
Utilize AI tools to support learning and exercises related to the course.

general_details.Description:
Khóa học Khởi sự doanh nghiệp bao gồm 2 phần:

1. Nhận thức kinh doanh để khởi sự doanh nghiệp, bao gồm các chủ đề:

- Đặc tính của những chủ doanh nghiệp thành công và những lý do chính dẫn đến sự thất bại trong việc khởi sự doanh nghiệp

- Đánh giá được tính thích hợp của họ đối với việc khởi sự và điều hành doanh nghiệp

- Ước tính được số tiền họ có để khởi sự doanh nghiệp của họ

- Lựa chọn ý tưởng kinh doanh có tính thực tiễn

2. Lập kế hoạch kinh doanh để khởi sự doanh nghiệp, bao gồm: chuẩn bị kế hoạch kinh doanh và kế hoạch hành động cho doanh nghiệp mới của mình



Khóa học được triển khai với phương pháp lấy sinh viên làm trọng tâm. Dựa trên những hoạt động trao đổi trên lớp, những bài tập tình huống, bài tập thực hành, trò chơi kinh doanh và thuyết trình, sinh viên sẽ được cung cấp kiến thức và thực hành ngay kiến thức đó. Phương pháp này giúp sinh viên hiểu vấn đề bằng cách đối mặt với các vấn đề sẽ diễn ra hàng ngày khi khởi sự doanh nghiệp.

- Hoàn thành nhiệm vụ sau giờ học được giáo viên giao cho

- Chỉ sử dụng máy tính cá nhân cho mục đích học tập môn học

- Đọc tài liệu trước khi đến lớp

- Truy cập vào website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) để cập nhật thông tin và tài liệu về khóa học; cách đánh giá cũng như nhận sự hỗ trợ của giảng viên và các sinh viên khác

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 47h online + 3h offline (optional) + 1h Final exam + 99h self-study
general_details.Description: The Entrepreneurship Specialization examines the entrepreneurial mindset and skill sets, indicators of innovation opportunities, critical steps to bring innovations to the marketplace, and innovation strategies to establish and maintain a competitive advantage. Fundamentals of new venture financing are explored with attention to capital structures for new ventures, term sheets and how to negotiate them, and the differences between early-stage versus later-stage financing. You will develop an understanding of how to develop winning investor pitches, who and when to pitch, how to avoid common mistakes, and how to ‘get to the close’. In the final Capstone Project, you will apply the tools and concepts from the specialization courses by crafting a comprehensive, customer-validated business model, and creating a business plan and investor pitch.
general_details.StudentTasks: Access the specialization on Coursera and complete all courses' requirements to earn a certificate of completion for the specialization, in order to be qualified for the Final Exam.
general_details.Note: Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded.

general_details.Description:
The Startup Entrepreneurship specialization focuses on issues of Innovation, Creativity and Entrepreneurship. It leads the students through the entire process of creating a start-up from an idea.



Part One deals with ideas, and the creative imagination: discovering new ideas, new products, new services, new and better ways to do almost anything.



Part Two focuses on how to build a business (entrepreneurship). This course guides the learner through a series of tools and methods that help take an idea and make it happen, in a way that can sustain the business or organization that delivers it to humanity. general_details.Description:
The Startup Entrepreneurship specialization focuses on issues of Innovation, Creativity and Entrepreneurship. It leads the students through the entire process of creating a start-up from an idea.



Part One deals with ideas, and the creative imagination: discovering new ideas, new products, new services, new and better ways to do almost anything.



Part Two focuses on how to build a business (entrepreneurship). This course guides the learner through a series of tools and methods that help take an idea and make it happen, in a way that can sustain the business or organization that delivers it to humanity. Use this course to build a solid business or organization around the idea you developed during Part One.



Part Three offers Innovation Career Lessons from a Master of proven achievements. During this course you will follow conversations and interviews with Dadi Perlmutter, who until recently was Executive VP of Intel Corporate, the highest ranking Israeli executive of any multinational company.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Travel Agency Business_Kinh doanh đại lý du lịch
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Objectives: 

After completing the course, students will understand the background, operations, and structure of travel agency and tour operation. Students will understand the differences between tour operator and travel agency, and will be able to examine and evaluate how these two types of businesses operate as a foundation for future professional growth.



Description: 

This subject covers Travel Agency philosophy, ideas, and prerequisites for running a travel agency firm. Practical case studies from travel agencies worldwide and in Vietnam will be interspersed with these principles. In these case studies, students must discuss and work in groups so that teachers can assess their knowledge and expertise through presentations and tests.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Understand the basic operations, organizational structure, historical evolution, main characteristics and quality standards of a travel agency"

general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course will cover the primary techniques for mining and analyzing text data to discover interesting patterns, extract practical knowledge, and support decision-making, emphasizing statistical approaches that can be generally applied to arbitrary text data in any natural language with no or minimum human effort. Detailed analysis of text data requires understanding natural language text, which is a difficult task for computers

- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

clos.LO Details: Students will develop a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts and principles of text mining, including techniques for extracting, transforming, and analyzing textual data.
Students can use machine learning/deep learning (neural networks, neural language models, recurrent neural networks, LSMT) for specific text-mining applications.

Students will explore the methods and algorithms used for text classification and clustering tasks. They will learn to apply techniques like Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, and k-means clustering.

Students will learn about different methods for representing text data, such as bag-of-words, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), and word embeddings. They will understand the strengths and limitations of each approach.
Students will be aware of the popular applications in text mining, such as machine translation, question answering, and chatbots to design text mining-related applications in real-world

general_details.Syllabus Name: Text Mining_Khai thác văn bản
general_details.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description: This course will cover the primary techniques for mining and analyzing text data to discover interesting patterns, extract practical knowledge, and support decision-making, emphasizing statistical approaches that can be generally applied to arbitrary text data in any natural language with no or minimum human effort. Detailed analysis of text data requires understanding natural language text, which is a difficult task for computers
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

materials_table.Author: Benjamin Bengfort, Rebecca Bilbro, Tony Ojeda

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Natural Language Processing with Python: Analyzing Text with the Natural Language Toolkit
materials_table.Author: Steven Bird, Ewan Klein, Edward Loper

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Natural Language Processing in Action: Understanding, Analyzing, and Generating Text with Python
materials_table.Author: Hobson Lane, Cole Howard and Hannes Max Hapke

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Text Analytics with Python: A Practitioner's Guide to Natural Language Processing
materials_table.Author: Dipanjan Sarkar

clos.LO Details: Students will develop a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts and principles of text mining, including techniques for extracting, transforming, and analyzing textual data.
Students can use machine learning/deep learning (neural networks, neural language models, recurrent neural networks, LSMT) for specific text-mining applications.

Students will explore the methods and algorithms used for text classification and clustering tasks. They will learn to apply techniques like Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, and k-means clustering.

Students will learn about different methods for representing text data, such as bag-of-words, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), and word embeddings. They will understand the strengths and limitations of each approach.
Students will be aware of the popular applications in text mining, such as machine translation, question answering, and chatbots to design text mining-related applications in real-world

general_details.Syllabus Name: Typography & E-publication (Typography & E-publication)
general_details.Time Allocation: 30 slots, 1 slot = 90 minutes
general_details.Description:
This course will explore existing modern typographical ideas and techniques and attempt to expand on students’ typographical range. Students will investigate the communication of content and the emotional qualities of text.

Students will further develop their visual and conceptual fluency and create integrated communication design solutions. Emphasis will be placed on using typography, aesthetics, and composition to construct meaningful imagery and effectively solve communication problems.

This course uses the art of typography, aesthetic element,..., to build up ideas and apply them in designing products for graphic design such as: publication, branding systems.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment. 

- Computer with some version of photograph editing software such as Photoshop, Microsoft Word for written assignments, and POWERPOINT for presentations

- Have color papers, Color Pencils, scissors...

- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Nhạc cụ truyền thống -Trống dân tộc Traditional Musical Instrument
general_details.Time Allocation:
Thời gian học: 30 slot

1 course = 30 slots; 90 minutes/slot
general_details.Description:
1. Kiến thức/Knowledge:

- Nắm được những nét đăc trựng về lịch sử phát triển và cấu trúc của Trống dân tộc

Understand specific characteristics of the historical development and structure of the traditional drum

- Làm quen với nhạc lý và những kỹ thuật cơ bản của Trống dân tộc

Familiarize students with music theory and basic techniques of the traditional drum

- Tìm hiểu về hệ thống chữ nhạc cổ Hò xự xang... 

Learn about the system of letters Do Re Fa (Hò xự xang)...



2. Kỹ năng/Skills:

- Đánh được 3 bài trong đó có 2 bài hòa tấu dùng trống Huế chơi đại nhạc, 1 bài dân ca đệm trống dàn cho các bạn lớp nhạc cụ

Be able to play 3 songs including 2 ensemble performances using Hue drums to play Great Music, 1 folk song with drum accompaniment to students of other instrument classes



- Môn học sẽ được triển khai theo đơn vị lớp cỡ khoảng 15 sinh viên/lớp.

There will be about 15 students/class.

Trong quá trình học, sinh viên sẽ được giới thiệu, hướng dẫn tìm hiểu và thực hành về các nội dung sau: 

In the course, students will learn:

- Lịch sử phát triển của Trống dân tộc ở Việt Nam 

Historical development of traditional drum in Vietnam

- Cấu trúc và đặc điểm của Trống dân tộc

Structure and characteristics of traditional drum

- Tư thế đánh trống

The playing posture

- Nhạc lý và kỹ thuật cơ bản gồm:

Music theory and basic techniques, including

 + Luyện phát âm

Practice producing sounds

+ Kỹ thuật tay phải - tay trái

Right-hand and left-hand techniques 

+ Học các dạng hình tiết tấu - các dạng nhịp 2/4 , 4/4 - các điệu trống

Learn rhythm patterns - 2/4 and 4/4 time signatures - drumming styles 

- Luyện tập đệm bài dân ca Việt Nam: Lý cây đa

Practice drum accompaniment to Vietnamese folk song: Ly cay da

 - Bài nhạc cổ: Xàng xê, Mã vũ

 Traditional music: Xang xe, Ma vu



* Sử dụng CNTT trong học phần/ Apply IT in the course

a) Cung cấp thông tin, tài nguyên lên mạng : Cung cấp địa chỉ các Website, clip nhạc truyền thống.

Update information and resources on the internet: Provide web addresses and traditional music clips. 

b) Sử dụng các tài nguyên trên mạng: Giảng viên sử dụng có chọn lọc trên nguyên tắc của học phần rồi cung cấp cho sinh viên. Hướng dẫn sinh viên tìm thông tin theo các chủ đề nhất định trên mạng Internet.

Use of online resources: Lecturers use resources selectively based on course regulations and then provide them to students. Instruct students to find information on certain topics on the Internet.



* Phát triển kỹ năng mềm và phát triển cá nhân trong học phần/ Soft skills development and personal development

- Rèn luyện tính kiên trì cho sinh viên, giúp sinh viên tự tin hơn trước đám đông

Improve students' perseverance and help them become more confident in front of the crowd "

- Phát triển kỹ năng làm việc theo nhóm, kỹ năng hoạt động độc lập của sinh viên thông quan các nhiệm vụ mà giảng viên giao.

Develop students' ability to work in groups and work independently through the tasks assigned by the lecturer.

In the course, students will learn:

- Lịch sử phát triển của Trống dân tộc ở Việt Nam 

Historical development of traditional drum in Vietnam

- Cấu trúc và đặc điểm của Trống dân tộc

Structure and characteristics of traditional drum

- Tư thế đánh trống

The playing posture

Music theory and basic techniques, including

Practice producing sounds

Right-hand and left-hand techniques

Use of online resources: Lecturers use resources selectively based on course regulations and then provide them to students. Instruct students to find information on certain topics on the Internet.

general_details.Description:
University Success Oral Communication is designed for English language learners preparing for mainstream academic environments. A flexible three-part approach includes intensive and systematic skill development tied to learning outcomes along with authentic lectures delivered by top professors from Stanford University. The Oral Communication strand provides real-life learning experiences for students who need to achieve academic autonomy.

Upon completion of the course, students should be able to:

LO1. Listening actively to follow a lecture or discussion, taking organized notes and identifying subject relative clause

LO2. Demonstrating an understanding of ideas in a discussion, answering questions about texts, and using tag questions to invite agreement 

LO3. Formulating probing questions, describing conclusions, summarising listening, and connecting ideas with so and therefore

LO4. Comparing similar ideas and contrasting different ideas, understanding relationships between ideas, and utilizing the simple past passive

LO5. Identifying parts of a presentation or lecture, planning for a presentation, making predictions, explaining order with linking words

LO6. Identifying and expressing facts, and opinions, bias, expressing conditions with if

LO7. Making inferences, giving oral summaries to relate ideas, answering inference questions, and expressing present possibility with modal verbs

LO8. Taking note on research lectures, relating source information to an audience, synthesizing information from multiple sources, and using compliment clauses after about

LO9. Identifying main ideas, paraphrasing to relate main ideas, rephrasing to simplify ideas, and constructing the present perfect passive

LO10. Interpreting an listing steps in a process, utilizing visual aids in a presentation, explaining a scientific process, and showing sequence with time adverbs 

LO11. Contributing interesting ideas to make classroom atmosphere more exciting. 

LO12. Budgeting your time wisely and performing certain independent learning. 

LO13. Supporting students with poor academic performance in pair-work/group-work activities.

presentation with clarity and impact

general_details.Syllabus Name: Tourism destinations and routes of Vietnam_Tuyến điểm du lịch Việt Nam
general_details.Syllabus English: Tourism destinations and routes of Vietnam
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description: The module equips students with knowledge about tourist destinations within Vietnam such as geographical distribution, social, economic, cultural, and tourism development of leading source 7 tourism regions. From a geographical point of view, based on the classification of tourism resources, the countries of origin of tourists, or generating areas; and the routes traveled between these two sets of locations teaches students how to design, develop and evaluate a tour itinerary.

Effectively apply AI to the course.



Objectives

This course helps students to master the characteristics of regions and the connections between them, from which students apply this knowledge to design appropriate travel itineraries and to present them in a convincing, attractive way to tourists/customers.



Teaching Method:

The course is designed based on the blended learning method. Students are required to read slides before coming to class. In class, the lecturer recalls the lesson and organizes discussion activities.

The course includes a lot of practical sessions for interpreting and building travel itineraries.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Tour Design and Development_Phát triển sản phẩm du lịch
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
Objective: 

Students understand the various components that contribute to the design of a tourism product, such as local culture, important holidays, nearby resorts, modes of transportation, the availability of intermediary service providers, and the development prospects of that tourism product in the country's tourism industry's future. Students must generate an idea, create a product, and persuade the class that it is effective, viable, sustainable, and has the potential for development, in which students must present analysis of the strategic products of various organizations using case studies.



Description: 

This course teaches the structure, functions, operations, strategies, and other aspects of tourism goods, as well as how to build and implement one or more comprehensive tourism products. The course also analyzes and provides information on specific tourism items such as specific fascination, cultural, religious, and so forth. The course also includes real-life case studies on tourism product design.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

clos.LO Details: Define and analyze the extent of services, evaluate the relevance of services in the economy as a whole, and tourism services in particular.
Distinguish between the marketing mix for tangible products and the marketing mix for intangible services, and investigate the use of service in tourism.
Understand all of the aspects that drive tourism product ideation, design, and implementation, such as destination selection, culture, entertainment, and so on.
Investigate the processes of tourism product development, from concept design to actual execution, as well as the method of tourism product operation.
Understand several fundamental and unique forms of tourist products, such as cultural, religious, resort, beach, and event types, among others.
Define a communication and promotion strategy to extensively spread typical tourism products and stress the sustainability of tourism products using communication methods.
Analyze and evaluate several organizations' tourism product strategies using common case studies.
Develop products that address contemporary issues in the development of tourist products for events, resorts, cruises, and other tourism products.
Acquire professional attitudes and abilities to obtain an understanding of designing tourism products for a wide range of customers.

assessments.Grading Guide:
OP1: Class is divided into 4-5 groups.

The plan of the fieldtrip will be built by class and submitted to teacher for approval before travelling. 

The video is made as a result of the fieldtrip.

Each group will be required to do a task in the trip and recording the task they implement. The details requirements are as follow: 

1. The video record should show the title: "Field trip for Tourism Geography subject". 

2. The video should have university's logo and students should wear school's uniform (if possible). 

3. The video should declare the names of group's members.

4. Each group can record the backstage sceneries for enriching the content of the video. 

5. Topics will be chosen randomly and assign for students by teachers. Topics suggested are:

-  Introduce overview (general) information about the chosen site (i.e. history of establishment, natural/cultural tourism resources, features of the destination's attraction, suitable tourism products).

- Introduce clearly about tourism infrastructure and superstructure of the site (i.e: accommodation, food and beverage, entertainment and recreational activities, etc.).

-  Introduce about tourism route to travel to the site, means of transportation used to visit the site and the stopover(s) during the route of travelling. 

- Travel tips and note for tourists when visiting the site (time, season, climate, what to bring, how to deal with locals, what to try in the site)

- Identify problems/issues of the site and give recommendation to improve the situation (from your own thought of the site). 

An additional written report is submitted together with the video that clearly explain what you've done in the video as requested in each group (it will work as the subtitle for the video).  

On the day of the presentation, each group will spend time answering questions from lecturers and other groups about his field trip

general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
The general objective of the course is to elucidate the intricate relationships existing between travel, transport and tourism and their functioning.



The course focuses on introduction of tourism in general; its links with travel, air transport; airline operation and management; airport functioning; the role played by land and water transportation in tourism; the way the travel industry products are distributed; the value being added during the process of tour operation; functioning and management of tour operation businesses; and the nuances of tour guide. The course also deals with the demand and supply factors, influencing factors, impacts of information technology in travel intermediation and impacts of mass travel and tourism.



Lecturing is the main teaching method in the theory part. However, the lecturer is required to provide relevant practical and hands-on experiences by using case studies or sharing personal experiences. The learners are encouraged to actively participate in lectures by active and student-centered teaching methods such as reciprocal questioning, games, rotating chair group discussions, rountable meeting or by self-learning and preparations before the lecture, Practical training sessions are organized to allow the learners to develop their initial skills and behaviors on the tourism and travel occupational/ opereational standards. assessments.Grading Guide:
Each group of 4-5 students will choose a real company in tourism/travel sector to learn about the aspects:  organizational structure, operation systems, services provided, customer segment, their partners....  

Each group will make an in-class PowerPoint presentation of about 30 minutes.
assessments.Note:
All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission or every 350 words over/ below the limit (see below).

The report and presentation should follow this format: (1) structure and background of firm; (2) description of their current situation; (3) analysis of the business operational practices; (4) conclusions and recommendations; (5) references; (6) annex. Word limit: 3,500 words +/- 10%.

Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report.

Specific contact details of the interviewees including phone number, addresses, website and questions must be submitted in the Annex.

Any plagiarism will be resulted in a failure of assignment

general_details.Syllabus Name: Destination Management and Marketing_Quản trị điểm đến và Marketing
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
-Course objectives: The subject is aimed at providing a vital and comprehensive understanding of destination marketing and management

-Description: Managing destinations is an area of growing importance as tourism regions compete to provide unique experiences and exceptional value to visitors. Principles and concepts of building strong destinations are explored to assist future tourism professionals in establishing stronger regional & international tourism organizations while responding to the needs and wants of community residents.

-Teaching method: Basic input will be given by the lecturer in order to initiate discussions on the relevant topics. Therefore, students are required to prepare the reading material in advance. In class, short group works will take place. This should further stimulate discussion between students and allow them to immediately apply theoretical knowledge to mini-case studies. Additionally, discussion should allow students to reflect on observations of tourist destinations and identify linkages with management and marketing activities.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments, and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Consumer behavior in Tourism_Hành vi khách du lịch
general_details.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
-Objective: The subject is aimed at providing a vital understanding of contemporary tourist behaviour and its application in a variety of sectors of tourism.

-Description: Students will acquire broad knowledge of consumer behavior in tourism and hospitality industry. They will be able to describe and explain tourist behaviors through the perspectives of human psychology.They can also determine the role of tourist behaviors in the process of tourism product development, quality management and other marketing decisions.

-Teaching Method:

Basic input will be given by the lecturer in order to initiate discussions on the relevant topics. Therefore, students are required to prepare the reading material in advance. In class, short group works will take place. This should further stimulate discussion between students and allow them to immediately apply theoretical knowledge to mini-case studies. Additionally, discussion should allow students to reflect on observations of own or (other) tourists’ behaviour and identify linkages with management and marketing of tourism (products).
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

materials_table.MaterialDescription: The Routledge Handbook of Consumer Behaviour in Hospitality and Tourism
materials_table.Author: Saurabh Kumar Dixit

clos.LO Details: To explain the concept and models of consumer behavior in tourism and hospitality industry
To get insight into the how today’s consumers select, purchase, use and experience the tourism and hospitality products.
To identify different market segments and analyse the consumer behavior in different market and across the sectors in tourism and hospitality industry
To update with the development trend and controversial issues of tourism behaviour internationally and in Vietnam
To practice the professional attitude and skills of achieving understanding of consumer behavior before any decision in business decisions
To apply the understanding of the consumer behavior into product development, quality management and other marketing decisions in tourism

Objectives: This course cultivates a comprehensive skillset for students aspiring to thrive in the dynamic field of tour operations.  Graduates will emerge proficient in crafting compelling itineraries, implementing effective marketing and sales strategies, and navigating the intricacies of financial management and risk mitigation.  Furthermore, the course fosters the development of critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, alongside strong communication skills and a commitment to ethical conduct – all essential for a flourishing career in the ever-evolving tourism industry.

assessments.Grading Guide:
1/ Students are required to complete a practical project that they have self-designed (based on what student got from tour project presentation 1 & 2) as part of the practical assessment, which is based on the requirements of the lecturer. 

All point components of the practical project will be evaluated by lectures of the faculty as well as industry specialists. Should students choose to go the practical way, the evaluation will be based on totally the activities of students in tour, which guided in the "evaluation of Tour practical form."

2/ If students do not want to have Tour project practical, they can choose "Tour project report" instead, the written report is the detailed project version.
- The written report should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and can be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission
- A 0 (zero) mark will be given to any form of plagiarism detected.

assessments.Question Type: Progress Presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered in accordance to the lecture of the weeks
assessments.Grading Guide:
- Students must work in groups (5-6 students/ group) to figure out basic content for a practical tour that they will submit to their instructor.
- The student's presentation content in the first session must include several key elements such as:
1/ Students need to comprehend what type of tour they wish to construct (for example: sightseeing tour, green tourism, eco-tourism, etc.), students must also examine which market will be suitable for the tour (use market analysis models such as Pestel, micro environment, macro environment, etc)
2/ Students must submit general tour information (e.g, outbound or inbound, total trip cost, packages/combos/travel products included). Furthermore, in this part, students might include a sample brochure explaining their tour to boost its vividness and appeal.
- After groups have finished presenting, the lecturer should provide relevant comments so that student groups can benefit from their experiences and be prepared to go on to the next stages.

Students will work in team of 5-6 students;
The marking will be based on the application of the theory, the understanding of the potential customer and situation and ability to meet their requirements, the ability to analyse situations, develop and evaluate plans

general_details.Syllabus Name: Sustainable Tourism_Du lịch bền vững
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course focuses on the sustainability of tourism’s relationship with the natural, social, cultural and built environments. Using case studies of the environments in which tourism occurs, students explore tourism’s role in our contemporary world, both as an agent of change, and as a response to it. Creative methods are used to think differently about the future of tourism impact management.

A systematic examination of several approaches to tourism planning and policy making at both national/regional scales and from a business perspective. Develops a critical understanding of the role of decision-makers and planners on tourism development. 

Approach the current status of sustainable tourism projects in the world and in Vietnam.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final project.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by the instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose 

- Promptly  access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

clos.LO Details: Understand and analyse issues and challenges related to the environmental, socioeconomic impacts of tourism.
Understand and analyse issues and challenges related to the impact of tourism on local cultural heritage.
Understand and analyse the roles and interactions of stakeholders in sustainable tourism planning and development.
Analyse collaborative planning and management actions open to stakeholders for dealing with tourism-related impacts in the different environments in the future.
Apply theories, concepts and principles underpinning sustainable tourism planning and development.
Understand and apply sustainable tourism criteria for Vietnam's tourism industry and for enterprises planning in practice.
Analyse and utilise specific techniques and tools in the planning process for sustainable tourism development.
Understand and evaluate Corporate social responsibility (CSR) of enterprise for sustainable tourism
Have a sense of discipline, professional manners and a high sense of responsibility at work; Flexibility in handling situations, ability to work independently and in groups.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Visual Communication (Nguyên lý thị giác)
general_details.Time Allocation: Contact hours: 1 session=90'
general_details.Description:
This course provides an introduction to visual communication design for students and provides them with the knowledge and skills to communicate their ideas and processes in a visual form more effectively. As a means of questioning and applying fundamental theories, concepts and techniques, students conduct research and produce practical projects. The course examines the basic elements of visual communication and how context shapes visual forms production and reception. Topics include: Visual Cues, Visual Theories, Visual Persuation, Visual Stereotypes and Visual Analysis. Case studies introduce major areas: Branding, Packaging, Advertisement, Animation, Web. Assessment includes periodic critique and review sessions that provide formative feedback on work in progress.

'- This course will be organized in a studio

- During class time, practice exercises will come right after each of theories.

- Students are to research and hold mini seminars that focus on different majors areas in graphic design industry.

- Students create art works after lectures and tutorials. These art works will be analyzed and evaluated by students under the control of lecturer. Finally, they will be graded by the lecturer.

- Students collect all of their art works to make the portfolio.
general_details.StudentTasks:

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submlit to the teacher 01 day after the course.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Visual Communication_Nguyên lý thị giác
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
Description: 

This course provides an introduction to visual communication design for students and provides them with the knowledge and skills to communicate their ideas and processes in a visual form more effectively. As a means of questioning and applying fundamental theories, concepts, and techniques, students produce visually meaningful projects. The course examines the basic elements of visual communication and how context shapes visual forms production and reception. Students will also learn to analyze the attention-getting qualities of form that engage people in compelling interactions.

Teaching methods used include: Lectures, Tutorials, Discussions, Laboratory work, Group work, and Seminars to help students approach the subject, understand the subject, apply it to practice, create compositions that communicate effectively by applying knowledge of interaction, interpretation, and experience, and analyze and evaluate design solutions in specific cultural and technical contexts.
general_details.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/gui/Home) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher after the course.

materials_table.MaterialDescription: Visual Communication from Theory to Practice
materials_table.Author: Jonathan Baldwin, Lucienne Roberts

clos.LO Details: Explain the way people communicate visually, and how communication design organizes experience in a variety of structures.
Apply knowledge to arrange the elements - words, images and/or symbols that contribute to the construction of meaning, utilizing tools such as traditional tools, digitals tools, or generative AI.

Analyze the attention-getting qualities of form, which constitute an essential first step to appropriate interpretive behaviors, engage people in compelling interactions, and extend meaning beyond the momentary encounter with the message.
Create a composition that communicates and provides information about relevant interactions among the components of a message by applying knowledge of interaction, interpretation, and experience.
Create visual communication design solutions for specific cultural and digital contexts by applying manual and/or digital methods of retaining and extending meaning.
Have a positive attitude and a professional working style.

The digital video editing course aims to equip students with basic knowledge of the digital video industry, to master the video production process and basic techniques from scenarios, filming, editing, post-production, audio etc.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Video Production _Sản xuất video
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
This practicum course is designed to give students the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge learned before to actual multimedia production situations. This course incorporates in its approach a combination of applied media aesthetics theory and hands-on production experience in Video production. Students will gain a foundation for understanding media production theory, facilitating video production processes as well as creating and evaluating media products relating to a particular issue set by the course lecturer. A component of the course will permit the introduction of current topics such as media issues, professional video production techniques, changing media technology, and job market information.

As a student of the class, you will sample a variety of production work through active team participation. Based on the quality of the video, your product might be published on FPT’s media platforms.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Option 1: 

(Presentation + Report) 

For this group project, you will collaboratively produce a video based on a topical theme selected in class. The video will be screened in class and each group will lead a discussion on their theme.

The movie should demonstrate:

• That it is a justifiable representation of the theme selected in class

• Faithfulness to the original storyboards.

• The technique of in-camera editing.

• Basic technical video production skills, such as awareness of framing, lighting, etc.

The presentation (screening and discussion) should:

• Be facilitated in a communicative/commercial way.

• Be analytical of the topical theme.

• Direct the participants toward the generation of another theme.



The essay should:

• Should discuss a generative theme, link it to the topical theme, and demonstrate an understanding of media production

• Should explain the reason why the students decide to produce their video 

• Should describe the content of the video (including its key message) and how the video can help them to spread the message to their target audiences

Notes: The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

Individual Project

For this individual project, you will get have the privilege to produce a video all by yourself based on the advice and suggestion of your lecturer. The video will be screened in class and you will the one who presents the idea and key message(s) behind your video and explain the reason why you decide to make this video.

Through the screening (presentation), the movie should demonstrate:

• A specific implicit/explicit key message

• Faithfulness to the original storyboards.

• The technique of in-camera editing.

• Basic technical video production skills



The essay should:

• Should demonstrate an understanding of video production

• Should explain the reason why the student decide to produce their video 

• Should describe the content of the video (including its key message) and how the video can help them to spread the message to their target audiences

• Should evaluate the difference between working alone and working in a group

general_details.Syllabus Name: Video Production _Sản xuất video
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 105h self-study
general_details.Description:
This practicum course is designed to give students the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge learned before to actual multimedia production situations. This course incorporates in its approach a combination of applied media aesthetics theory and hands-on production experience in Video production. Students will gain a foundation for understanding media production theory, facilitating video production processes as well as creating and evaluating media products relating to a particular issue set by the course lecturer. A component of the course will permit the introduction of current topics such as media issues, professional video production techniques, changing media technology, and job market information.

As a student of the class, you will sample a variety of production work through active team participation. Based on the quality of the video, your product might be published on FPT’s media platforms.
general_details.StudentTasks:
-Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

 - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 

 - Read the textbook in advance 

 - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

assessments.Grading Guide:
Option 1: 

(Presentation + Report) 

For this group project, you will collaboratively produce a video based on a topical theme selected in class. The video will be screened in class and each group will lead a discussion on their theme.

The movie should demonstrate:

• That it is a justifiable representation of the theme selected in class

• Faithfulness to the original storyboards.

• The technique of in-camera editing.

• Basic technical video production skills, such as awareness of framing, lighting, etc.

The presentation (screening and discussion) should:

• Be facilitated in a communicative/commercial way.

• Be analytical of the topical theme.

• Direct the participants toward the generation of another theme.



The essay should:

• Should discuss a generative theme, link it to the topical theme, and demonstrate an understanding of media production

• Should explain the reason why the students decide to produce their video 

• Should describe the content of the video (including its key message) and how the video can help them to spread the message to their target audiences

Notes: The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Cơ sở Văn hoá Việt Nam
general_details.Time Allocation: Thời gian học: 30 tiết (1tiết = 45')
general_details.Description:
Cơ sở Văn hoá Việt Nam là môn học về đặc trưng văn hoá của dân tộc Việt Nam.

Phần đầu tiên của môn học, giới thiệu về lý luận và cách nhìn nhận chung của văn hoá học. Trên cơ sở đó giúp người học tiếp cận văn hoá Việt Nam.

- Từ việc xác định toạ độ của văn hoá việt nam về không gian, thời gian và chủ thể của văn hoá việt nam cho đến diễn trình văn hoá Việt Nam. 

- Môn học giới thiệu tập trung về những vấn đề đặc trưng của văn hoá truyền thống, đặc trưng các vùng văn hoá ở Việt Nam.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Đọc sách giáo khoa và các tài liệu khác trước trước khi đến lớp

- Truy cập trang web của khóa học (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) cập nhật thông tin và các tài liệu của khóa học, hỗ trợ trực tuyến từ các giáo viên và các học sinh khác, và để thực hành và đánh giá.

- Tích cực tham gia hoạt động trong lớp 

- Hoàn thành tất cả các bài tập và các nhiệm vụ khác được đưa ra bởi giảng viên. 

- Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay cá nhân trong lớp cho mục đích học tập

- Không nói chuyện riêng, đến lớp muộn, nghe điện thoại, để chuông điện thoại, nhắn tin có thể phá vỡ môi trường học tập của lớp

- Tham dự từ 80% giờ học để để đủ điều kiện tham gia kỳ kiểm tra cuối cùng.

clos.LO Details: Trang bị cho SV cách nhìn nhận có tính hệ thống và tổng hợp để tiếp cận cơ sở lý luận của văn hoá học: khái niệm, chức năng, cấu trúc, ...
Giúp SV biết cách nhìn nhận và đánh giá một hiện tượng văn hoá.
Giúp SV nắm được những nét đặc trưng của nền văn hoá Việt Nam, để từ đó hiểu và nắm bắt được bản sắc của nền văn hoá Việt Nam.

Sau khi hiểu được văn hoá là gì cũng như những đặc trưng, bản sắc của Văn hoá Việt Nam, SV có một cách nhìn nhận vấn đề dưới góc độ văn hoá, sáng tạo nghệ thuật và định hướng phát huy trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hoá.

general_details.StudentTasks:
- Đọc sách giáo khoa và các tài liệu khác trước trước khi đến lớp

- Truy cập trang web của khóa học (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) cập nhật thông tin và các tài liệu của khóa học, hỗ trợ trực tuyến từ các giáo viên và các học sinh khác, và để thực hành và đánh giá.

- Tích cực tham gia hoạt động trong lớp 

- Hoàn thành tất cả các bài tập và các nhiệm vụ khác được đưa ra bởi giảng viên. 

- Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay cá nhân trong lớp cho mục đích học tập

- Không nói chuyện riêng, đến lớp muộn, nghe điện thoại, để chuông điện thoại, nhắn tin có thể phá vỡ môi trường học tập của lớp

- Tham dự từ 80% giờ học để để đủ điều kiện tham gia kỳ kiểm tra cuối cùng.

clos.LO Details: Trang bị cho Sinh Viên cách nhìn nhận có tính hệ thống và tổng hợp để tiếp cận cơ sở lý luận của văn hoá học: khái niệm, chức năng, cấu trúc, …
Giúp Sinh Viên biết cách nhìn nhận và đánh giá một hiện tượng văn hoá.
Giúp Sinh Viên nắm được những nét đặc trưng của nền Văn hoá Việt Nam, để từ đó hiểu và nắm bắt được bản sắc của nền văn hoá Việt Nam.
Sinh Viên có một cách nhìn nhận vấn đề dưới góc độ văn hoá, sáng tạo nghệ thuật và định hướng phát huy trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hoá.

sessions.Student Materials:
"Giảng viên tổ chức cho sinh viên đi thực tế chương 2 tại một trong những bảo tàng sau: 

-Bảo Tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia

-Bảo tàng Lịch sử Việt Nam

-Bảo tàng Đà Nẵng, Bảo tàng Cần Thơ"
sessions.Student's Tasks:
"Sinh viên làm báo cáo thu hoạch ngoại khoá.

Bài tập tự luận: Sinh viên chọn một hiện tượng, một biểu tượng quan sát được trong buổi học ngoại khoá để chỉ ra những đặc trưng của văn hoá Việt Nam.

Yêu cầu: 1. Sinh viên chọn một hiện tượng, 1biểu tượng văn hoá quan sát được trong buổi ngoại khoá.

2. Từ đó phân tích để thấy được những đặc trưng cơ bản của nền văn hoá ở Việt Nam.

Tiêu chí đánh giá: + Chọn hiện tượng, biểu tượng hay: 2/10 + Phân tích tốt và chỉ ra được các đặc trưng: 6/10 + Bố cục bài viết khoa học, rõ ràng, mạch lạc: 2/10 "

general_details.Syllabus Name: Vietnamese Culture _ Cơ sở văn hóa Việt Nam
general_details.Time Allocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_details.Description:
This course is designed to provide students with a understanding of the foundations and the dimensions of Vietnamese culture, origin, characteristic; pay particular attention to the relationship between Vietnamese culture and the present-day life of the Vietnamese people and to the different elements of the culture which are under the social structures, belief systems, literature, arts, customs, etc... Topics mainly include: (1) the foundations of Vietnamese civilization: its geography, language, and history; (2) the core concepts in Vietnamese thoughts and religions: Aninism, Taoism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Catholicism, the new sects religion;...(3) Literature  (4) Society and Life, including education, the role of women, Vietnamese food, festivals and leisure activities ; (5) Arts and Architecture (6) Vietnamese performing arts like Ca trù, Tuồng, Hát Bội...

-Teaching method: Presentation, Discussion, teamwork, critical thinking, field-trip.
general_details.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time.

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose.

- Promptly  access to the FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information.

general_details.Syllabus Name: Đường lối cách mạng của Đảng cộng sản Việt Nam
general_details.Time Allocation:
1 session = 45 minutes

Total Course Time: 36 sessions in the classroom, 14 sessions for students to study by themself   

Interactive Classroom Teaching
general_details.Pre-Requisite: MLN101 và studied HCM201 (attend at least 80% of sessions)
general_details.Description: Nội dung học phần bao gồm những vấn đề cơ bản về lịch sử ĐCS Việt Nam và đường lối cách mạng của ĐCS Việt nam. Nội dung gồm 9 chương: Chương mở đầu (Nhập môn), chương I: Sự ra đời của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam  và Cương lĩnh chính trị đầu tiên của Đảng, chương II: Đường lối đấu tranh giành chính quyền (1930-1945), chương III: Đường lối kháng chiến chống thực dân Pháp và đế quốc Mỹ xâm lược (1945-1975),  chương IV: Đường lối công nghiệp hoá; chương V: Đường lối xây dựng nền kinh tế thị trường định hướng xã hội chủ nghĩa, chương VI: Đường lối xây dựng hệ thống chính trị, chương VII: Đường lối xây dựng văn hoá và giải quyết các vấn đề xã hội; chương VIII: Đường lối đối ngoại.
general_details.StudentTasks: Phải có giáo trình Đường lối cách mạng của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam (Dành cho sinh viên đại học và cao đẳng khối không chuyên Mác- Lênin và tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh của Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo.                                                                                                                                             Thực hiện đầy đủ các yêu cầu của giảng viên khi học trên lớp cũng như các chủ đề sinh viên tự chuẩn bị  trước khi đến lớp.
general_details.Tools: Hội đồng Trung ương chỉ đạo biên soạn Giáo trình quốc gia các bộ môn khoa học Mác-Lênin, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh: Giáo trình Lịch sử Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam.C18

clos.LO Details: Cung cấp cho sinh viên những nội dung cơ bản của đường lối cách mạng của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam, trong đó chủ yếu tập trung vào đường lối của Đảng thời kỳ đổi mới trên một số lĩnh vực cơ bản của đời sống xã hội phục vụ cho cuộc sống và công tác. Xây dựng cho sinh viên niềm tin vào sự lãnh đạo của Đảng, theo mục tiêu, lý tưởng của Đảng.
Giúp sinh viên vận dụng kiến thức chuyên ngành để chủ động, tích cực trong giải quyết những vấn đề kinh tế, chính trị, văn hoá, xã hội theo đường lối, chính sách, pháp luật của Đảng và Nhà nước.
